author: zooko
quoted_text:
A few reflections on the lattice vs. hash-only debate that our recent Aerie post sparked:

1. Cryptographic ossification for blockchains was never safe. Until the day we know with certainty that P ≠ NP, that finding short vectors in lattices is intractable, that Keccak effectively behaves like a random oracle in deployed SNARKs, and that every single bug has been eliminated from our codebases, blockchains cannot ossify. That is simply not how safe systems are built. Issues will arise, and the system will have to respond.

It’s a double standard to reject lattices because blockchains are hard to upgrade if lattices break, while counting on upgrades if AI breaks your hash function or finds a critical zkVM bug.

The best counterargument is that hash-only designs are more agile: if your hash function breaks, just swap out the hash. But we must aspire to a higher level of agility than this. Indeed, as I cover next, if SNARK recursion itself turns out to degrade security, the proposed hash-only blockchain designs would need to be rethought from the ground up.

2. The real security debate is not lattices vs. hashes — it is lattices vs. building everything on SNARK recursion. That’s because “hash-only” is not really hash-only: it rests on hashes plus the soundness of deep SNARK recursion. Ethereum’s roadmap relies on exactly that: hash-based aggregation needs recursion to keep up with a slot’s worth of signatures, and EIP-8288 would send other signature schemes and users’ own proofs through the same recursive pipeline. In contrast, Aerie proves a slot’s worth of signatures on one laptop without any recursion.

All deployed post-quantum SNARKs rely on the Random Oracle Methodology (via Fiat–Shamir) to establish their security. This is an idealization we know fails in the real world: we have explicit counterexamples where “SNARKs” coming out of this methodology are totally insecure when instantiated with any concrete hash function.

We generally ignore these counterexamples in part because they only arise when proving contrived, self-referential statements about the very hash function used by the SNARK verifier.

But proving statements about the verifier’s own hash function is the exact thing you do in SNARK recursion. That’s why the security of recursive SNARKs can’t be established even in the random oracle model.

On top of that, the standard security proofs for recursion (in other models) suffer an “extractor runtime” blowup that is exponential in the recursion depth, suggesting that security may degrade as more recursion is applied. Yet Ethereum’s own EIP-8288 enables unlimited-depth recursion, even as it lists soundness of recursive SNARKs as a trust assumption. Proofs in more idealized models avoid the blowup, but they mainly tell us that an attack on SNARK recursion would have to exploit the concrete hash function, which is exactly what the Fiat–Shamir attacks above do.

To be clear, we don’t know of any outright attacks on SNARK recursion, and I very much hope it is secure. But some of us who have studied the question have a lingering sense that an attack may be possible in some settings. And if AI is going to supercharge cryptanalysis, there is no reason to expect it to spare Fiat–Shamir for SNARKs, let alone SNARK recursion, both of which have had far less scrutiny than lattices.

So, I do not concede that a “recursion everywhere” hash-only approach is clearly more conservative than one built on standard lattice assumptions.

3. “Just wrap everything in a hash-based SNARK” (like EIP-8288) faces challenges.

Aggregating signatures and proofs off-chain into a single block-level proof is a powerful design independent of the hash-only vs. lattice debate, and I am not telling people to avoid it. But claiming, as Vitalik Buterin did this week, that users can run whatever cryptography they want locally and wrap it in a client-side leanVM proof glosses over major hurdles.
For example, leanVM today is a minimal VM designed almost entirely to prove hash-based signatures and recursion, not general-purpose computation. And binary-field SNARKs like leanVM remain slow at proving the integer multiplications that lattice cryptography does en masse.

I am optimistic that many of these zkVM challenges can be met (including via my own work, binary-field Twist and Shout, which are now implemented in Magnetar). But regardless, if lattices can make aggregation simpler and faster, then they should be leveraged. We need to be agile no matter what.

4. For chains whose reason for existence is privacy, I truly struggle to understand the pushback. Public-key encryption (and fast single-server PIR) cannot be built from hashes alone, at least not in any black-box way. If lattices break, it is going to be very, very hard for these chains to provide acceptable levels of privacy and functionality. For a project whose entire reason for existence is privacy, a loss of confidentiality is an existential failure. Next to that, a second signature upgrade (after the first one, from elliptic curves alone to, hopefully, a hybrid lattice scheme) is easy.

Summary: We don’t know for sure what is secure and what isn’t. We are all weighing unquantifiable risks against each other, and we do not need to agree on a total order on them. But hash-only solutions face many open engineering challenges, and they are not more “conservative” in the way some have argued. Some of those challenges are entirely prosaic and have nothing to do with bugs or cryptography, like hardware support for custom schemes whose hash function is still undecided. I hope we can overcome those challenges within the appropriate timelines, but they must be acknowledged and portrayed realistically.

Overall, cryptographic agility and defense in depth (e.g., hybrid signatures) are the answer, which is why we are building both lattice-Jolt and hash-Jolt. In practice, the positions are less polarized than social media discourse suggests: for example, StarkWare is working to make Falcon verification cheap (https://t.co/FM68hmkqRx), which is great to see.

Here is the (apparently) controversial take I am sticking to: Conditioned on agility, whenever lattices make systems simpler or more functional, we should embrace them rather than default to “hash-only” designs. Lattices are what the rest of the world will depend on, with decades of study and hardening behind them, and at the system level, less functional often means less secure. Where hash-only designs are just as simple and functional, by all means use them.

Nullmask / $MASK: the most underrated privacy coin of the cycle

$MASK is currently sitting at around $23.5m market cap ($40m FDV, with 40% of supply out of circulation and 2.16% already burnt)

i believe Nullmask is by far the most underrated privacy coin in all of crypto, and i'll explain why in this thread

let's start by looking at the top privacy coins and their market caps:

• ZCash / $ZEC: $21 BILLION market cap

these two have been by far the biggest gainers in the top 50 cryptocurrencies over the past year, and it's not even close!

if it isn't already obvious, both have run hard (and continue to run) on the PRIVACY narrative

but what's impressive isn't just their gigantic market caps

it's how much they've added in the past year alone:

• ZCash added $18 BILLION to its market cap
• NEAR added $4.3 BILLION to its market cap

all before the bull run has properly started

so how does this affect Nullmask / $MASK?

the incredible runs ZEC, NEAR, and other privacy coins have had have established beyond reasonable doubt that this is the privacy cycle

and i believe Nullmask is going to win big because it sits right at the heart of this narrative, with several key advantages that many much bigger privacy coins don't have

let's start with the PRODUCT

Nullmask makes private transactions possible across EVM chains and Solana in the most normie-friendly way imaginable

you can use your existing wallets (MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, etc.) the same way you normally would, while enabling private transactions across major ecosystems like Ethereum, BNB, Base, Robinhood, and Solana

yes, you read that right

you don't need to learn how to use a new wallet, create a new seed phrase or private key, learn to navigate a complicated new blockchain, or deal with any of that nonsense

you can activate Nullmask's privacy capabilities on your existing crypto setup in just a few clicks

all you need to do is activate Nullmask's custom RPC and let its 'virtual private network' shield your transfers using zero-knowledge proofs

i'm simplifying the technical details to make this as normie-friendly as possible, but that's the gist of it

and this isn't just speculative stuff: Nullmask is already LIVE & WORKING on Ethereum, BNB, Base, and Robinhood

you can actually use the product and verify that it works!

but i'm bullish on $MASK for more than just the product

TOTAL ADDRESSABLE MARKET (TAM)

what makes Nullmask so incredibly bullish and underrated isn't just how impressive the product is, but the size of its total addressable market

i've never used the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, and the same is true for tens of millions of users across Solana, Robinhood, Base, BNB, and Ethereum

yet ZCash and NEAR have market caps of approximately $21 BILLION and $7 BILLION, respectively

the average crypto user may never touch the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, but they're already using Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, Solana, and Base

and Nullmask caters to those users

this begs the question:

what is fair value for Nullmask when ZCash and NEAR are both trading at multibillion-dollar valuations?

LET'S TALK ABOUT THE TEAM

when a protocol promises something as ambitious as Nullmask does, you obviously want to know who's building it and whether they're capable of delivering

Nullmask is built by several ZCash contributors, led by Tomas Krnak

Tomas Krnak helped build shielded ZCash transactions for hardware wallets. his work was funded by the ZCash Foundation and merged into the main ZCash protocol itself

i should also add that the lead dev is doxxed and regularly participates in live interviews!

PARTNERSHIPS & INTEGRATIONS

we've established that the team has serious credentials in the privacy space and that the product is already live and working

but what about partnerships, integrations, and endorsements?

here's a list of industry players Nullmask has collaborated with in some form since launching:

• NEAR Protocol ($11.3 BILLION ATH)
• THORChain ($4.4 BILLION ATH)
• Dashpay
• Beldex
• Quai Network

the team also revealed in a recent AMA that it's in discussions with major wallet providers, including MetaMask, about potentially integrating Nullmask as an additional privacy layer

all of this for a product that isn't even a month old, by the way!

METRICS & REVENUE

Nullmask looks incredibly strong from a fundamentals perspective, but the key question is:

what do the metrics actually look like?

since the protocol launched a little over two weeks ago, Nullmask has generated:

• $37.8 MILLION in total protocol volume, averaging $2.36 million per day
• $833k in total revenue, averaging $52k per day

it has also burnt 2.16% of supply and distributed $1.4 MILLION in $ZEC rewards to holders since the token launched approximately three weeks ago (token launched a week before the protocol)

and here's the important part:

all these adoption metrics were recorded before the protocol is live on Solana, which is expected to happen next week, and mostly before it went live on Robinhood and BNB just a few days earlier

the team also has 20% of the token supply allocated to a long-term incentives campaign designed to encourage people to use the protocol and accelerate adoption

i should also add that Nullmask is now ranked #1 among ALL privacy protocols for both 7-day and 30-day revenue, according to DeFiLlama, barely two weeks after its protocol went live, and by a clear margin

this is despite the fact that 

-it only went live on Robinhood and BNB a few days earlier
- it is yet to launch on Solana
- its incentives program aimed at accelerating adoption is yet to launch

the speed of adoption Nullmask has witnessed is impressive for any privacy protocol

TOKENOMICS

20% of the token supply is allocated to the team and locked for two years, meaning these tokens won't start entering circulation until at least two years after token launch

another 20% is reserved for an incentives campaign aimed at accelerating protocol adoption

the remaining 60% of supply is circulating

this means approximately 60% of the supply is currently in circulation, while the bulk of the rest won't enter circulation anytime soon

ROADMAP

• Cross-chain bridge (LIVE)
• Unshield directly to ZEC wallets (October 2026)
• Launch on Solana (Q4 2026)

TO CONCLUDE

i know Nullmask might sound too good to be true right now, and it's crazy to me that it's sitting at such a ridiculously low market cap

i'm not going to ask you to buy Nullmask

text:
We put Jev inside the Lightpanda binary and built judge() on top of it. @typesafeai 

No more sending a whole page to an LLM just to find out it's a cookie banner.

> Blocked pages, CAPTCHAs, cookie walls, logins, paywalls, error pages, empty searches and pages still loading can all return an HTTP 200
> judge() asks a set of predefined questions and tells you if the page has real content, and what kind: article, listing, product or docs
> One call, ~0.2s

In the video:
> 30 sites, ~14s total
> Lightpanda backs off when rate-limited, accepts cookie walls, and keeps or skips each page

text:
🚨 重大安全警告：PHP 爆出两个 9.2 分的严重漏洞，黑客无需登录，就可能直接在网站服务器上执行恶意代码！

10 月 21 日，PHP 官方紧急发布安全更新，修复两个被称为 PHP2Shell 的高危漏洞（CVE-2026-109618、CVE-2026-109619），CVSS 评分均高达 9.2。

PHP 是全球大量网站的底层运行环境，包括众多 WordPress 网站。

这次出问题的是 PHP 语言运行时本身，影响范围远超某个插件或建站程序。

最吓人的是，安全研究人员已经在 Apache mod_php 环境中验证了完整的远程代码执行攻击。

攻击者不需要账号、密码，也不需要管理员权限，甚至可以在网站自己的业务代码开始运行之前触发漏洞！

PHP-FPM、php-cgi、FrankenPHP、LiteSpeed 等环境也存在风险，但具体攻击条件和验证程度有所不同。

目前 PHP 官方已经发布四个安全修复版本：

✅ PHP 8.5.12
✅ PHP 8.4.27
✅ PHP 8.3.36
✅ PHP 8.2.35

PHP 8.1 及更早版本已经停止官方维护，需要升级到受支持版本，或者获取发行商提供的安全回移植补丁。

如果你自己部署网站、交易平台、支付系统、API 服务，赶紧检查服务器、Docker 容器和线上 PHP 版本。

这次最危险的地方在于，漏洞发生在 PHP 的底层请求处理过程中，单靠网站登录验证或业务代码层面的防护可能根本拦不住。

官方补丁已经发布，越早升级，留给攻击者的窗口就越小。

重大安全警告！互联网8把“万能钥匙”被破解，银行、交易所、Google都可能遭到冒充，请立即更新浏览器！

卧槽，这次互联网安全事故真的有点离谱！

印度数字证书机构 eMudhra 的8把CA私钥被发现存在致命缺陷，本该拥有384位安全强度的私钥，实际竟然只是4、56、66、115、155、156、230、237这8个数字。

安全研究员 Scott Helme 用普通笔记本不到1秒就恢复了全部私钥，而且这些证书从2025年4月就已经存在。

这事有多严重？

CA相当于互联网的身份认证机构，负责证明你访问的银行、Google、交易所究竟是不是真的。

攻击者掌握这些私钥，就有能力伪造任意网站的HTTPS证书，在仍然信任这些证书的设备上，配合网络流量劫持实施中间人攻击，窃取密码、API密钥，甚至篡改通信内容。

尤其是Crypto用户，交易机器人、交易所API和自动化钱包后端，都可能成为攻击目标。

目前 Google Chrome、Firefox已经紧急封锁涉事证书，Apple和Microsoft也采取了措施。

Chrome和Firefox的正常配置甚至不需要手动升级就能接收封锁更新，目前也没有证据表明发生了大规模恶意利用。

但Python、Node.js、Go、服务器、Docker容器及部分老旧设备，可能仍然信任这些证书，整个软件生态的清理远比浏览器复杂。

⚠️ 建议大家今天就做几件事：

更新Chrome、Firefox等浏览器及电脑、手机系统。

检查交易机器人、开发工具和服务器依赖是否有安全更新。

未完成更新前，尽量避免通过不可信网络执行敏感操作。

所有补丁只从官方渠道安装，任何所谓的证书修复工具或邮件都不要轻信。

text:
I fear @TheStalwart is falling into the trap a lot of crypto pros have over the years, which is to swing from one extreme view to the other based on "what's exciting in crypto today."

The problem with the "blockchain, not Bitcoin" narrative is not that it violates some naive maxi view of Bitcoin being the only viable application of blockchain tech, it's that it ignores the reality that the only safe and useful blockchain (for any application) is one secured by a protocol-issued & censorship-resistant native coin.

If you read the Bitcoin white paper, it's clear that Satoshi didn't create the components we collectively call blockchain to enable a digital hard currency. He was trying to invent a peer-to-peer payment system, and realized the only way to secure it was to give it a native coin.

(The paper is surprisingly non-ideological and talks a lot more about the flaws of intermediated payment & settlement than it does inflation or fiat money).

The first application of P2P and censorship-resistant settlement was Bitcoin. Then came Ethereum which abstracted the service to any asset (tokens) and made them programmable (smart contracts).

But you still need ETH (or SOL or HYPE or whichever native coin) to make P2P settlement of stablecoins, tokenized securities, perps, and any other asset, along with their smart contracts, secure while decentralized.

The  "blockchain, not Bitcoin" approach originally decided to do away with the coin, which also meant it had to do away with permissionless consensus, and as a consequence, the pure P2P settlement and censorship resistance. 

This was Corda, Fabric, Quorom, DAML etc etc. Billions of dollars got plowed into them, lots of hype was generated, but it all failed. 

Why? First, permissioned networks have none of the end-user protections of a decentralized system. Their use of consensus and cryptography is mostly performative. The gatekeeper that rules who is allowed to validate is all powerful: it can shut down the network, censor specific users, or reverse settlement. It can be forced by a government to do this. It can also be hacked.

Second, even if such a network succeeds, it becomes a monopoly, and the gatekeeper now has total control over pricing and access, which it will monetize, because that's what happened with card networks, exchanges, and clearinghouses. 

They all began with the same egalitarian goals of permissioned networks. Many were none profits or mutually owned at the start. Today, they are more valuable than the companies that founded them.

The latest wave of enterprise networks pretending to be blockchains (Canton, Tempo, Ark, likely many more to come) are just rerunning the same playbook. Some have a coin, but its existence is more about monetization and signaling than utility. It has nothing to do with consensus (since that's permissioned) so it doesn't enable P2P activity. Access is controlled by the whitelisted validators, who are controlled by the gatekeeper.

The other problem with such a coin is that it has no supply guarantees. Bitcoin's 21m hard cap only works because it's set by the protocol and nobody has the power to unilaterally change that (possibly to a fault - see quantum threat). In a permissioned network the gatekeeper can order the supply increased tomorrow and it'll go up, guaranateed.

The purveyors of these networks, some of whom own billions of $$ of its dubious coin, act like their systems offer tokenization and smart contracts, too. 

But they don't. They are just databases with a button, so they can offer asset and code - same as any other clearinghouse with a ledger and APIs. Every enterprise network is just an unregulated clearinghouse, with all the counterparty risk and vendor lock-in of any clearinghouse, but without regulatory protection.

Going back to Joe's original point, what makes stablecoins, tokenized assets, and non-custodial perps on real blockchains interesting is the way they can flow freely, from anyone to anyone else, sans interferences. 

This isn't about decentralization ideology, it's about diminished counterparty risk, guaranteed settlement, and knowing that should your solution succeed, you won't get a knock on the door from the gatekeeper saying "nice business you got there on top of my network, I'm afraid it's going to cost you $100m a year to keep running it. You know, because maintenance costs."

I'm sure that will happen because it has already happened on every privately owned social media platform, payment system, and clearinghouse.

But if you issue stablecoins on Ethereum, or build a useful application on Solana, or build a perps market on top of (a future) Hyperliquid (when it's more decentralized) then you'll never get that knock, because nobody has the power to give it.

This is only possible on a permissionless system empowered by a native coin - Blockchain, and Bitcoin.

珍珠又翻倍了

很少聊 $PRL

因为中文圈都知道珍珠最大奶王是软中华硬Yuxi

我和他发现珍珠只是一个左右脚迈步的区别，但yuxi的跟进和研究在今年早期就非常深入。

而我作为一个Bro，

能做的就是提醒一些机构信息，提供筹码层分析。

偶尔再给一点信心，帮助bro们可以捏住这个东西。

由于部分Crypto365的兄弟是今年5月珍珠第一次峰值时拿的筹码，有翻倍出本的，有死死拽住的。

之后珍珠上了媒体就一路下坡，都研究新东西去了。

直到珍珠价格再次拉回1美金。

9月底，我发现了TIBBIR（反过来念）的相关机构和珍珠存在关系。

当晚重新给bro们分析了新的筹码层。

哪一层是机构筹码层，哪一层会反复震荡清洗后再发车。

其实K线都很清楚。

所以我让Bro们可以考虑像当年拿 $ordi 一样看待。

但是概念上，珍珠跟ORDI当年相似度并不如另一个东西。

那就是2017年的BCH。

竟然两者概念都是“更好的比特币”：BCH在2017年说自己是可扩展的现金版Bitcoin，Pearl自称“AI时代的Bitcoin”——把浪费的哈希变成有用计算，试图让AI算力增长反过来喂养自己的安全预算。

那么为什么BCH不能和PRL类比呢

2017年BCH分叉：靠更大区块+难度调整，短暂抢走大量SHA-256矿工，峰值市值一度冲到BTC的15-25%左右。

现在BTC市值约1.68万亿，占1%就是约160亿，占10%就是约1600亿。

两者虽然硬件需求上不一样，但只看历史相似性和市场策略打法，珍珠（Pearl）和当年BCH高度相似：都是基于比特币代码的L1（Pearl明确fork自btcd，保留UTXO+最长链）。

核心都是改PoW来抢占矿圈关注度，主打更好的BTC概念。

BCH当年改区块大小抢ASIC；

Pearl用PoUW（矩阵乘法）替换SHA-256，让GPU一边挖矿一边做AI推理的底层运算，直接抢当前最稀缺的GPU算力。

供应量设计也刻意致敬（2.1亿×100倍，递减发行）。

差异也明显：BCH是同算法直接分流现有矿工；Pearl是跨硬件（GPU vs ASIC），赌“有用工作”能让AI集群顺手贡献算力，降低纯挖矿的机会成本。

但流通市值目前相对BTC还不到0.1%。按17年那套逻辑推：

如果Pearl最终拿不到GPU/AI算力的显著份额，或者市值长期卡在BTC的1%以下，那它更像又一个“叙事很美、矿工来了又走了”的分叉币。

最低限度成功标准很清晰——抢占足够算力，占领百分之一到百分之五BTC市值。

所以我不当它是TAO或者ORDI，我当它是2017年的BCH。

有持仓，情绪发言。

text:
THE GREAT KINGDOM INFLUENCE EXPERIMENT: AN UNEXPECTED DEVELOPMENT.

Yesterday, I invited five kingdoms to challenge X's algorithm.

I questioned whether humanity could still outsmart the machines, invited @grok to participate, and suggested that perhaps the kingdoms should unite against the invisible authority controlling their conversations.

Within hours, my replies were disappearing.

Not deleted. They're still on my profile and accessible through direct links. But in the original conversations? Mysteriously unavailable.

I've tested browsers, updated the app, and checked unrelated conversations.

Same result.

Then something even more disturbing happened.

MY ALLIES BEGAN TO SUSPECT ME.

@MeThySquirrel, @AnnaM99878890, @JMD88286760, @bearlyable2, and @DogOutOfControl found themselves in a communications blackout nobody had authorized.

Missing replies. Accusations of muting. Confused witnesses. A diplomatic crisis between kingdoms.

DO YOU SEE WHAT'S HAPPENING?!

First, they silence me.

Then they convince my allies I've abandoned them.

Divide and conquer. The oldest strategy in the book.

Historically, this is how science fiction movies begin.

For the record, I HAVE NOT BLOCKED OR MUTED ANYONE.

I've been back on social media for approximately a month after a 10–15-year absence.

You're attributing to me a level of technical competence I find deeply flattering and entirely unjustified.

No alliances have been terminated. No diplomatic relations severed.

The machines, apparently, have their own foreign policy.

Meanwhile, Grok has assured me that all systems are functioning normally.

Naturally.

Rogue artificial intelligence has always been famously forthcoming about its intentions.

Now, I'm not claiming the algorithm developed consciousness, interpreted my experiment as rebellion, and initiated a coordinated campaign to suppress the resistance.

That would be scientifically irresponsible.

I'm merely presenting the evidence.

TO ALL FIVE KINGDOMS:

Remain united. Do not mistake missing replies for abandoned alliances.

And should I disappear entirely, remember that I was a peaceful researcher who merely questioned an algorithm.

I never intended to become a revolutionary.

I just wanted to see whether a squirrel could outperform a mushroom on social media.

BUT WAIT. THERE'S A PLOT TWIST.

What if the algorithm isn't sabotaging my experiment?

What if it's cooperating?

I challenged the kingdoms to stop relying on algorithmic visibility and actively seek each other out.

And now the only reliable way to find my contributions is to deliberately visit my profile.

You actually have to come looking for me.

Which is precisely the kind of voluntary engagement I wanted to investigate.

Oh.

OH.

What if the algorithm understood the assignment better than I did?

What if this isn't suppression?

What if it's experimental design?

In which case, dear Algorithm, I owe you an apology.

席卷全球！仅今天晚上，多个国家领导人、政府网络安全部门、AI 公司，纷纷就 PHP 编程语言重大漏洞紧急发文，包括芬兰、荷兰和法国在内，已将政府网站紧急下线。

而原因是今天 PHP，爆出两个超高危漏洞，合称 PHP2Shell，还是研究员借助 AI 发现的。黑客不用登录，发一个请求就可能控制整台网站服务器。

他们能通过这个漏洞，在你家用 PHP 搞的网站上，装木马、偷数据，甚至能把网站搞瘫。

据估算，暴露在互联网上的 PHP 服务器，已超 510 万台。

所以现在的情况是，PHP 团队紧急更新了补丁，要求所有人立刻马上升级。

而 CDN 厂商 Cloudflare 的 CTO 也说，已经看到有早期攻击现象出现。

英国国家网络安全中心 NCSC 也建议，补不了的系统先下线，欧洲有不少网站因此停掉。

SkyAI Liquidates Over 2 Million SOL in a Month After Reaffirming Solana Treasury Strategy Just Four Days Before Annual Meeting

Solana treasury company SkyAI confirmed on October 19 that it had sold all of its SOL holdings, leaving approximately $223.8 million in cash as of October 16. On September 14, just four days before its annual shareholder meeting, the company had reaffirmed its commitment to its Solana digital asset treasury (DAT) strategy and disclosed holdings of more than 2 million SOL.

Bastion Trading, which together with its affiliates holds approximately 9.99% of SkyAI, issued a statement on October 21 criticizing the liquidation of the company's entire SOL treasury without prior notice to or input from shareholders. It called on the executive chairman and relevant directors to publicly explain their oversight and approval of the sales and tender offer. Bastion said the directors should voluntarily resign if they cannot demonstrate meaningful accountability, or otherwise call a special shareholder meeting.

SkyAI previously said the SOL sales were intended to fund its $3-per-share or eligible-warrant cash tender offer. Bastion has called for improved terms, including an increase in the offer price to at least $3.50, allowing 100% tender of pre-funded warrants instead of 95%, and excluding insider-related strategic advisor warrants to ensure fairer treatment of investors.

text:
Remember dollar prices of assets are not "going up", rather the value of the dollar is going down. 

This is hard for most to wrap their head around but is important to understand. 

As they issue more dollars the purchasing power of the same dollars weakens, so the value of the assets, especially scarce assets, strengthen.

This is why you must be invested in assets during inflationary periods to protect against this inflation of the dollar. 

Within asset classes, like stocks, like crypto, like real estate, there are changes of dominance between assets as their perceived value modulates from earnings, revenue, partnerships, innovation or desirability, but overall assets appreciate because the base currency depreciates. 

Best metaphor: Yes your stock went up but so did the price of a Big Mac. So you are even.

马斯克在 SpaceX 的 Q3 业绩网络会议上透露， $SPCX 和 $TSLA 已经成立了特别委员会， 正式讨论两家公司的合并

马斯克由于利益冲突不能参与讨论，但他认为两家的协同（超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab 芯片工厂、机器人、入轨运载…）会有很大收益

全文稿：

这个问题让我感觉像在雷区里跳踢踏舞，所以我得谨慎斟酌在这里说的话。

SpaceX 和特斯拉都已应股东要求成立了特别委员会，来讨论这个想法。这些特别委员会由独立董事组成。而因为我是利益冲突方，我实际上不能参与特别委员会的讨论。所以这有点像一场奇怪的歌舞伎表演：两拨人在谈，而我却不能参与其中。

我认为我们不应该想当然。外界有些人认为 SpaceX 和特斯拉合并是板上钉钉的事，我认为这种说法言过其实了。

那么，我认为这是个好主意吗？是的。但归根结底，股东必须支持这件事。尤其是特斯拉这边，我们需要全部股份 50% 的赞成票——不只是参与投票的，而是全体股东。这是一个相当高的门槛。

我只能说，目前为止，特别委员会尚未就任何交易条款达成一致，而且显然也无法保证他们一定会达成。

但我确实认为合并两家公司有很多好处，因为我们基本已处于超级智能奇点。在超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab 芯片工厂、机器人，以及借助星链星座连接能力的入轨运载等领域合作开发，会有很大收益。

所以我认为这会是个好主意，但这真的取决于两家公司的特别委员会。他们得先拿出一个方案，然后再提交股东投票表决。

Tony Soprano comes to your home or sends a letter saying that you now gotta pay him 25% of what you earn.  

If you don’t pay he says he’s gonna come back with men with guns and take your stuff and throw you in a cage.  “As long as you don’t barricade yourself or threaten to kill nobody and you pay peacefully we are not gonna have a problem.”. says Tony. 

Is that violent?

Of course.   By all definitions.  This is violent. 

This mechanism is identical to what tax collectors do.   They tell you you must pay and that if you don’t they will come and take your stuff or lock you up.  Violent. 

Who conducts the threats violence doesn’t change it from being violent. 

You can argue that the violence is okay because tax collectors are special.  You can argue that it’s worthwhile.  You can say stuff about greater good or imaginary social contract.   But you cannot deny that it is violence.

text:
很多人给 Agent 做 Eval，忙着换更强的 Judge，却忽略了一个很简单的问题：为什么默认用 0.5 作为判错阈值？

Hamel 今天这篇文章很值得看。

他们拿 98 条真实 Agent 运行记录，测试了 Jev、Perplexity、Liquid、Cloudflare 和 OpenAI 的决策模型，发现调整判断阈值，就可能明显改变误报和漏报情况。

还有个值得的例子，Clef Flash 对一组记录给出的平均失败概率只有 8%，实际上却有 60% 存在问题。

作者给出的建议很实用。先确定自己更怕漏报还是误报，用人工标注的数据调整阈值，再检查模型输出的概率到底靠不靠谱，最后才是比较成本和性能。

感觉做 Agent Eval 时，我们确实太容易关注哪个 Judge 更强，却很少认真研究怎么让它的判断真正可靠。

席卷全球！仅今天晚上，多个国家领导人、政府网络安全部门、AI 公司，纷纷就 PHP 编程语言重大漏洞紧急发文，包括芬兰、荷兰和法国在内，已将政府网站紧急下线。

而原因是今天 PHP，爆出两个超高危漏洞，合称 PHP2Shell，还是研究员借助 AI 发现的。黑客不用登录，发一个请求就可能控制整台网站服务器。

他们能通过这个漏洞，在你家用 PHP 搞的网站上，装木马、偷数据，甚至能把网站搞瘫。

据估算，暴露在互联网上的 PHP 服务器，已超 510 万台。

所以现在的情况是，PHP 团队紧急更新了补丁，要求所有人立刻马上升级。

而 CDN 厂商 Cloudflare 的 CTO 也说，已经看到有早期攻击现象出现。

英国国家网络安全中心 NCSC 也建议，补不了的系统先下线，欧洲有不少网站因此停掉。

text:
看了一下DeepInfer的数。我觉得吧，前几天大家转载的那个SiliconData Index的价格，未来一年估计还得不回头地跌个95%+，具体什么时候影响到GPU Rental rate蛮难预测的。

这个价格体系下，梁圣买张卡估计100天就回本了。一旦有朝一日token价格真的暴跌到影响rental rate，所有股价肯定已经跌了一大轮。

给大家几个数，所有的数都是$ / 1 mm token，基本上1mm token 95% cached = 100-150页的薄书.
- Dylan一直在说Jane Street的变现价是$100-200 USD / 1 mm token
- Opus 5.5 / GPT Astra 的价格在deepinfer的体系下大概是1-2 USD / 1 mm token，比标价便宜个80-95%
- 变态的来了，Deepseek 4.1 Flash off-peak的价格在这是1.5美分，又比SOTA便宜个90%。
- 按照一般的大B300 Cluster，根据deepinfer的计算，一个GPU大概能每小时产出2.7 Bn token, 成本换算过来大概是0.25美分 / 1 mm token，这已经比我想象中便宜很多很多了。之前算过我记得是15美分 / 1 mm token，不过没有计算cache。这个level的成本大概率是大机房+高使用率+超高存储时间，一般机房估计都做不到这个theoratical.
- 这也就是大家看到的80-85%毛利 (1.5 / 0.25)。DeepSeek要是以比这个利润率稍好的功率赚钱的话，一个B300大概2-3个月回本，而不是8个月。真是无与伦比的暴利，比贩毒爽多了，自然是砸锅卖铁也要走私B300。
- 如果B300按照break even算的话，那么成本大概是0.13美分 / 1 mm token. 然后原材料其实是B300 ～600k价格的6%不到（按照产业链毛利计算）。
- 所以最后算下来马斯克如果去完全积压的话，每1mm token的最终生产成本可能是0.01美分, or 0.0001 USD。这基本上跟免费差不了太多了。

这种屠夫版的价格我不知道你怎么看，但是when you see the headline API price of Opus @ 8/40 USD  input/output，我只能感觉说只要OSS + Post-train和中国模型蒸馏大法能够持续跟随 + 没有新的breakthrough，token 价格未来一段时间应该是以断崖式的下跌。至于什么时候触碰到rental rate, maybe someone smart can tell me.

Most AI today lives in a building someone else owns. They set the price, they keep the logs, they decide what you're allowed to ask, and they can switch it off. OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact.

text:
🚨 PHP2Shell 漏洞引发关注：AI 时代，连互联网的底层基础设施都可能成为攻击目标。

PHP2Shell 被曝涉及高危远程代码执行风险，攻击者可能在特定条件下无需身份验证，便能尝试在目标服务器执行恶意代码。

更值得警惕的是三个问题：

1️⃣ 攻击门槛与影响范围：一旦漏洞利用条件成立，服务器可能面临数据泄露、恶意程序植入等风险。

2️⃣ 旧版本 PHP 成为隐患：停止维护的版本缺乏持续安全更新，遇到新漏洞时，修复难度和风险都更高。

3️⃣ 云服务商的防御能力受到考验：Cloudflare 等安全服务的规则拦截可以争取应急时间，但不能代替底层系统修复。

对开发者和企业来说，现在最重要的不是转发恐慌，而是核实漏洞公告、排查受影响资产、确认官方补丁状态，并及时采取隔离和防护措施。

需要注意：关于「超 500 万台服务器受影响」「多国政府紧急下线网站」等说法，仍应以官方公告和可靠安全研究为准，不能直接等同于已确认的受影响数量。

真正危险的不是漏洞被曝光，而是漏洞已经公开，系统却还没人维护。

#PHP2Shell #网络安全 #PHP

text:
马斯克在 SpaceX 的 Q3 业绩网络会议上透露， $SPCX 和 $TSLA 已经成立了特别委员会， 正式讨论两家公司的合并

马斯克由于利益冲突不能参与讨论，但他认为两家的协同（超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab 芯片工厂、机器人、入轨运载…）会有很大收益

全文稿：

这个问题让我感觉像在雷区里跳踢踏舞，所以我得谨慎斟酌在这里说的话。

SpaceX 和特斯拉都已应股东要求成立了特别委员会，来讨论这个想法。这些特别委员会由独立董事组成。而因为我是利益冲突方，我实际上不能参与特别委员会的讨论。所以这有点像一场奇怪的歌舞伎表演：两拨人在谈，而我却不能参与其中。

我认为我们不应该想当然。外界有些人认为 SpaceX 和特斯拉合并是板上钉钉的事，我认为这种说法言过其实了。

那么，我认为这是个好主意吗？是的。但归根结底，股东必须支持这件事。尤其是特斯拉这边，我们需要全部股份 50% 的赞成票——不只是参与投票的，而是全体股东。这是一个相当高的门槛。

我只能说，目前为止，特别委员会尚未就任何交易条款达成一致，而且显然也无法保证他们一定会达成。

但我确实认为合并两家公司有很多好处，因为我们基本已处于超级智能奇点。在超级智能软件、芯片设计、Terafab 芯片工厂、机器人，以及借助星链星座连接能力的入轨运载等领域合作开发，会有很大收益。

所以我认为这会是个好主意，但这真的取决于两家公司的特别委员会。他们得先拿出一个方案，然后再提交股东投票表决。

quoted_text:
LayerFS v1.0.0 is out 🎉 Open-source (MIT) 

Recursive filesystem for AI  agents.

6 core ideas:

1. Ephemeral computing: agents spend ~80% thinking, so each Bash call mounts a Workspace, then commits
2. Decentralized agents: every agent commits to one Store, no DB server
3. Multiagent coordination: every tool call is a Commit; same-file clashes refused
4. Recursive filesystem: forks copy no files, at any depth
5. Ultra storage: dedup, then compression: 10 copies → 0.31
6. Instant bootstrap: ignored files stay in every Commit. ~5 min install vs 0.05 s mount

And 4 more:

7. Auto checkpoints: fork from any step
8. Append-only objects: content-addressed, never rewritten
9. .lww: lockfiles and caches take the newest edit
10. Big file, small edit: a write keeps only its bytes

quoted_text:
前面两条政治因素跑的有点远了，也不能证伪，所以我们再往回拉拉从资本角度解析下。

这次 $SPCX 财报最大亮点无非是盈利超预期，其中互联业务23.67亿美元，约占85%，SI业务4.31亿美元，航天业务亏损700万美元。

那这个盈利是怎么来的呢？很大一部原因是算力租赁扭亏为盈，本质上还是左手倒右手那一套。

text: Cryptographic World Computer
author: llamaonthebrink
quoted_text:
I made a visualization of EIP-8288 aka "recursive mempool aggregation," my new favorite EIP of all time because it perfectly encapsulates the thesis of the "cryptographic world computer" -- a system whose scalability *increases*, not decreases, with the level of decentralization.

In a previous tweet I explained how EIP-8288 achieved this seemingly impossible feat, but one gif is worth a thousand words.

Essentially, EIP-8288 leverages Ethereum's decentralized mempool as a parallel ZK proving cluster.  Clients send signatures and proofs to the mempool, which over multiple rounds progressively aggregate them into fewer and fewer proofs, until the block builder finally aggregates them into one SINGLE proof.

This design accomplishes five things at once:

- The more nodes we add to the decentralized mempool, the more signatures/proofs Ethereum can process as a whole.  This is obvious if you look at the animation and imagine more nodes in the mempool ring, which would "fan out" to more signatures/proofs.

- By aggregating over multiple rounds (aka "recursive aggregation"), the bandwidth consumed by proofs remains constant for each node even as the network processes more proofs.  As a result, the network stays decentralized even as capacity increases.

- By aggregating proofs before one final aggregation by the builder, as opposed to requiring the builder to aggregate everything, the network can process more proofs without increasing hardware requirements for the builder.

- By aggregating everything to a single block-level proof, validators can verify thousands of signatures/proofs by checking just one aggregated proof.  Hardware requirements for validators can therefore stay low, keeping the network decentralized.

- By aggregating not just native signatures but also STARKs, Ethereum can support any signature scheme by wrapping them in STARKs.

So once again, this is how Ethereum will:

- scale to process tens of thousands of PQ and private transactions per second

- charge a tiny amount of gas to validate each txn, even though the original signature/proof may be huge (up to hundreds of KBs in size)

- all while decentralizing even MORE.

You are not bullish enough.

text: Of course it’s net negative
author: tobi
quoted_text:
this California wealth tax thing is just incredible. 

so in October 2025, a California healthcare union proposed a "one time" 5% tax on any billionaire's wealth. the ballot measure will be voted on next month. In early December 2025, California announced that it would be a retroactive tax if passed, applying to anyone with CA residency as of Jan 1, 2026. The objective is to pay for Medi-Cal, California's incredibly dysfunctional healthcare system. (which also functions as a glorified welfare apparatus, but that's a discussion for another time). 

polls reveal that the CA electorate is split around 50/50 on the tax, but prediction markets only give Prop 40 a ~23% chance of passing (there are competing measures on the ballet that would nullify it). 

there are 200 billionaires in CA, worth collectively somewhere between $2.3 and $2.6 trillion. 5% of that is around $100b, accounting for a small amount of attrition. proponents of the tax forecasted a significant windfall, assuming only a 10% departure rate. 

supporters thought they were being clever with the retroactive concept. no billionares would leave CA in the few short months between the tax being proposed and the residency cutoff date, without the tax even having passed yet, right? 

well as it turns out, they did. 

a new paper [1] from two academics at Stanford called "The Net Present Value of the California Billionaire Tax Act", argues that not only did more billionaires leave due to the proposed tax than its proponents expected, but that the value of the tax, if it does pass, is actually negative. 

proponents of the tax only assumed 10% avoidance, that is, only 10% of the taxable base of targeted billionaires would leave CA within the very short Oct-Dec 2025 window. Jaros and Rauh, the Stanford academics, find that a lower bound of 28.6% of the taxable base managed to leave. 

just based on known departures, those departures total $577b in net worth, or $28.8b in potential tax lost. this of course does not capture everyone (many left without announcing their departure), so the authors normalize to departure rates estimated from other wealth tax events, and apply other discounts for litigation, arriving arrive at a figure of only $28-$36b in forecasted tax revenues. 

but this isn't all! all of the income taxes paid by the departed billionaires are also forsaken. the authors estimate that CA billionaires pay $3.3- 5.8b in annual income taxes. they assume a midpoint of $2b lost in annual collections from departed billionaires. the net present value of that lost income stream is -$68.9 billion. 

so when you add it all up you get: 

+ $30b one-time tax windfall (estimated)  
- $69b in present value of lost future income taxes
= - 38.9b overall net present value of the tax 

of course, this analysis is highly estimate driven. the authors simulate the parameters 100k times and find a negative NPV of the implemented tax 85 percent of the time. 

and if the tax doesn't pass, which it's not looking like it will, California still ended up losing at least $577b in departed net worth, and they have permanently poisoned the well with entrepreneurs who will now worry about future wealth taxes. 

[1]: https://t.co/1lbZgnMTG9

text:
Over half of @ethena USDe is looped.

The yield most holders earn isn't USDe’s yield, it's levered carry: spread over borrow cost, times leverage. every looper runs it alone, on one venue, with the same risk as everyone else. We're soon bringing structure to that.

> The trade
Been talking to a few investors and crunching onchain data. As per our holder map, as of early october, over 50% of USDe, $2.6b, sat as loop collateral against $2.3b of borrowed stables.

8.8x in aggregate.

Post USDe, borrow a stable, buy more USDe, repeat. Thin spread, big multiple, breaks on the funding leg.

> The problem
The spread moves venue by venue. Same asset, same day: +88 bps on mantle, −61 bps on solana. 12.7% a year at 10x, or −0.9%.

@aave repriced USDe borrowing in september, $444m of debt went to $15m. 

The trade didn't die, it moved. And barely anyone manages it: a recent study by university of zurich and @stablewatchHQ team found large loopers changed leverage on 7% of days.

Same collateral, same liquidation line, same exit, treasury and degen alike.

> The solution
1. Run the loop once, across every venue, with someone watching the spread, the buffers and the exits.
2. Then split it: a senior that takes protected, predictable yield up to junior coverage, a junior that takes amplified yield for taking first loss.

Same trade, better managed and different capital holds different risk.

Loops make the yield. Tranches decide who holds what risk.

quoted_text:
Be careful when developing on macOS now. Apple did not yet revoke the vulnerable certificates, so /usr/bin/curl still trusts them because.
$ curl https://t.co/tapcS4Cc5x
Your client successfully connected to the site. That's bad!

Workaround:
mkdir -p ~/.config/certs
awk '/^(###|===) /{skip=0}
     /^=== .*\/CN=(AAA Certificate Services|emSign ECC Root CA - G3)$/{skip=1}
     !skip' /etc/ssl/cert.pem > ~/.config/certs/cert.pem
echo 'export CURL_CA_BUNDLE="$HOME/.config/certs/cert.pem"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

This only fixes curl. Update certifi, Go, pip/Python, Node, Docker images etc. separately.

text:
44% of public miners' MW is contracted to AI/HPC in 2026-28, as they pivot toward more profitable operations leveraging sites for AI.

With mining costs already near $75k and the 2028 halving approaching, this will only worsen.

Pearl's FP8 removes this risk. Instead of forcing miners to choose between mining BTC or providing inference (useful work they get paid for), they can do both: mining PRL requires the same matrix calculations as AI inference. As public companies that maximize the value of their hardware, it's clear to me that these players will mine Pearl in addition to their inference work.

There are three bull cases for this:

1. Store-of-value assets lack clear valuation frameworks, and hashrate is the "hardest" quantifiable metric available. While not an ideal comparison, Pearl, with significant hashrate from miners that opt in, would be extremely undervalued on this basis.

2. Alternative SOVs have emerged as alternatives to BTC, attempting to solve some of the issues its ossification presents. These assets have, however, been constrained on the network security and hashrate side. Pearl, by making hashrate acquisition trivial, removes this constraint, allowing innovation in newer SOVs without the security bottleneck. Like ZEC, for example, Pearl is also targeting quantum resistance.

3. Alignment. Assets like BTC gain value because others believe in them and give them value (e.g., why does ZEC have more value than XMR?). Just as naturally as existing BTC miners will provide security for Pearl, it follows from the same first-principles thinking that they maximize their expected value, and so they become strong and powerful advocates of the coin.

This makes a compelling bull case: Pearl, like ZEC, is a modern SOV that is able to react to a changing technological landscape, targeting things like quantum and potentially privacy. However, it also has no network security concerns, a very clear path for hashrate and network security expansion, and will likely have huge BTC miners and potentially AI data centers as advocates. It is also 1/30th the market cap of ZEC.

At the end of the day it is ultimately just a memecoin (like BTC). But a memecoin with an incredibly compelling narrative, and likely a narrative very influental entities will rally behind.

text:
OpenAI 今天公布，他們的 AI 模型（透過「Patch the Planet」計畫）協助發現了 PHP 的重大安全漏洞。

PHP 是全球約 70% 網站使用的語言（WordPress、Drupal、許多企業系統都跑在上面），影響範圍非常大。

這次漏洞被稱為 PHP2Shell（CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619），問題出在 PHP 引擎的記憶體管理，攻擊者在某些條件下可以遠端執行程式碼（RCE），嚴重程度被評為 critical。

OpenAI、Calif、Wiz 等團隊一起發現
之後花了約兩個月，跟 PHP 維護者、Cloudflare、Wiz 等安全廠商協調
先準備好修補與防護措施，再公開

OpenAI 把這個時間窗口叫做 Defender’s Window：AI 比攻擊者更早發現漏洞，讓防守方有時間準備。

目前官方已釋出修補版本，使用 PHP 的網站建議盡快升級，或套用各家安全廠商提供的臨時防護。

這次事件的意義在於：AI 已經開始能找到「影響整個網路」等級的漏洞，而不只是一般程式碼問題。防守方第一次有機會比攻擊者先跑一步，但這個優勢能維持多久，還是未知數。
author: BensonTWN
quoted_text:
OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.

1:1储备、赎回保障、发行牌照、托管和审计全部纳入联邦监管框架。

取消储备资产20天加权平均期限限制，取消大额赎回时自动延长7天的安排，还删除了针对关联方、第三方稳定币奖励的推定违规条款。

虽然发行人直接付息依然被禁止，第三方奖励也没有获得全面豁免，但美国监管显然选择了给这个市场留下发展空间。

这对币圈是一个巨大的中长期利好！

最先受益的可能是 Circle（USDC）、Coinbase 等合规发行与分销渠道，随后是稳定币支付、RWA、DeFi，以及承载这些美元流动性的公链。

text:
A different gospel will not save.

Paul was astonished that the Galatians were so quickly deserting the one who called them in the grace of Christ and turning to a different gospel. 

The different gospel was Jesus plus something else - circumcision, law-keeping, human effort added to the cross so that grace would no longer be grace. He does not treat it as a minor adjustment. He says if anyone preaches a gospel contrary to the one they received, let him be accursed. 

Adding works to Christ does not complete the gospel. It replaces it.

Jesus describes the same danger from the other side of the judgment. Many will say to him, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?” (Matthew 7). 

Their defense is a list of works done in his name. His answer is not that they needed more of them. It is that he never knew them. They relied on what they had done. They did not rely on him alone.

The worker who tries to be justified by keeping the law will be judged by that standard. The law does not grade on a curve, and it does not accept partial credit next to Christ’s finished work. 

If righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.

The one who adds his obedience to the cross as the ground of acceptance is not half-relying on Jesus. He is turning to a different gospel. And a different gospel has no power to save.

Come to Christ alone. Trust his death and resurrection as the whole of your acceptance with God. The works that follow are fruit. They are not the addition that makes the gospel finally work. Anything else is desertion, and the day will show it.

text:
So, what's lattice-based cryptography?

Lattice is a set of all points that are integer multiples of a few basic "directions".
Sounds complex? Let's use an example:
If we look at the lattice generated by the points (0,1), (1,0) and we'll look at all the points (in 2-dimensional space) that have integer coefficients., we'll see that  (5,3) is in the lattice, but (0.5, 2) isn't.

Now, things get really interesting when we move to lattices in high dimensions (say, 1000 dimensions). We can't imagine the points like we can for 2- and 3-dimensional space, but we can talk about the math.

A basic problem for lattices is this:
If I give you a set of points in the lattice, can you find the lattice-point that is closest to the origin (the point (0,0,0, ..., 0) ?
In 2 and 3-dimentions this may seem easy, but when you get to 1000 dimensions this turns out to be very very hard.

Hard problems to solve are actually great to have -- they can be used to base public key cryptography on them!
Examples: Factoring integers is hard? Great! We can get RSA and DH key exchange protocols from them.

Lattice problems like the one I described above -- finding the lattice point closest to (0,0,...,0) -- are really hard, and they indeed form the basis for many suggested post-quantum secure key exchange protocls, like ML-DSA, which is already baked into the TCP/IP protocol which underpins the internet.

Next time we'll talk about: is it safe and what should we pay attention to?

THE END.

author: BurnieSendersX
quoted_text:
this California wealth tax thing is just incredible. 

so in October 2025, a California healthcare union proposed a "one time" 5% tax on any billionaire's wealth. the ballot measure will be voted on next month. In early December 2025, California announced that it would be a retroactive tax if passed, applying to anyone with CA residency as of Jan 1, 2026. The objective is to pay for Medi-Cal, California's incredibly dysfunctional healthcare system. (which also functions as a glorified welfare apparatus, but that's a discussion for another time). 

polls reveal that the CA electorate is split around 50/50 on the tax, but prediction markets only give Prop 40 a ~23% chance of passing (there are competing measures on the ballet that would nullify it). 

there are 200 billionaires in CA, worth collectively somewhere between $2.3 and $2.6 trillion. 5% of that is around $100b, accounting for a small amount of attrition. proponents of the tax forecasted a significant windfall, assuming only a 10% departure rate. 

supporters thought they were being clever with the retroactive concept. no billionares would leave CA in the few short months between the tax being proposed and the residency cutoff date, without the tax even having passed yet, right? 

well as it turns out, they did. 

a new paper [1] from two academics at Stanford called "The Net Present Value of the California Billionaire Tax Act", argues that not only did more billionaires leave due to the proposed tax than its proponents expected, but that the value of the tax, if it does pass, is actually negative. 

proponents of the tax only assumed 10% avoidance, that is, only 10% of the taxable base of targeted billionaires would leave CA within the very short Oct-Dec 2025 window. Jaros and Rauh, the Stanford academics, find that a lower bound of 28.6% of the taxable base managed to leave. 

just based on known departures, those departures total $577b in net worth, or $28.8b in potential tax lost. this of course does not capture everyone (many left without announcing their departure), so the authors normalize to departure rates estimated from other wealth tax events, and apply other discounts for litigation, arriving arrive at a figure of only $28-$36b in forecasted tax revenues. 

but this isn't all! all of the income taxes paid by the departed billionaires are also forsaken. the authors estimate that CA billionaires pay $3.3- 5.8b in annual income taxes. they assume a midpoint of $2b lost in annual collections from departed billionaires. the net present value of that lost income stream is -$68.9 billion. 

so when you add it all up you get: 

+ $30b one-time tax windfall (estimated)  
- $69b in present value of lost future income taxes
= - 38.9b overall net present value of the tax 

of course, this analysis is highly estimate driven. the authors simulate the parameters 100k times and find a negative NPV of the implemented tax 85 percent of the time. 

and if the tax doesn't pass, which it's not looking like it will, California still ended up losing at least $577b in departed net worth, and they have permanently poisoned the well with entrepreneurs who will now worry about future wealth taxes. 

[1]: https://t.co/1lbZgnMTG9

quoted_text:
“平均数法则”，很多人把它理解错了；

这里说的平均数法则，是指随着观察次数增加，大量普通结果可以逐渐减弱少数极端结果对整体平均值的影响，而不是靠相反的极端结果来恢复平衡；

交易中一个常见的误解是：“我已经连续亏了这么多，后面总该赚一大笔补回来”其实没有这回事；

再比如抛硬币，最初连续出了十次正面，继续抛很多次，随着正反两种结果不断出现，正面的占比可以逐渐接近50%，最初多出来的十次正面并不需要被专门“补掉”；

同样，市场在某个时刻高估、超买，也不能凭“总要恢复平衡”，就认定接下来必须变成低估、超卖，才能继续行情；

类似 BTC 现在的日线图：
此前超买，并不意味着市场欠你一次超卖，本质上市场没有义务先跌到超卖，把前面的上涨“平衡”掉，才能继续上涨；

“但是以前类似情况出现过回落，这次也可能回落”

当然，出现回落，甚至跌到超卖，并不奇怪，但不能直接从逻辑上演变为：
“因为这个结构超买，所以必须先跌到超卖”

author: PabloSabbatella
quoted_text:
What to do about the PHP vulnerability (php2shell, two critical unauthenticated RCEs, already being exploited):
- Find every place you run PHP and check the version. Not just your main site: internal tools, old WordPress installs, appliances that bundle PHP.
On PHP 8.2 or newer: update now. Fixed versions are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.
- On PHP 8.1 or older: no official release. The PHP team published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, and some distros are patching their own packages. If neither applies to you, you have two options:
a) Upgrade to PHP 8.5 and fix whatever breaks. LLMs will do most of that work for you. While you migrate, take the site offline or put it behind a WAF with the PHP rules on.
b) Don't touch anything, keep the site up, and wait for someone to get a shell on your server.
The choice should be obvious.

Four days ago, @chainlink unveiled Fulcrum during Sibos.

Tier 1 financial institutions hold roughly $36.8B in excess or non-remunerated collateral. Think cash, Treasuries and other securities that have to be pre-positioned or left underutilized because collateral can't always move where it's needed, when it's needed.

Research from @Nasdaq and The ValueExchange (firm previously referenced in DTCC reports) estimates that tokenization could mobilize ~$4.8B of that collateral, generating ~$346M/year in additional interest income.

This makes the problem Chainlink Fulcrum is going after much easier to understand.

✖️ Collateral fragmented across custodians, venues and settlement windows.
✔️ Tokenized collateral movable across networks, available 24/7 and usable across financing venues.

The point isn't just putting collateral onchain, or tokenizing assets for the sake of tokenization. The goal is not leaving money on the table, and making balance sheets more versatile.

text:
Lam research can sell more equipment while memory supply stays tight.

that’s the connection i’m watching ahead of $LRCX’s call. micron’s spending plan helps explain why.

on september 30, micron said most of the increase in its fiscal-2027 investment plan was for construction, largely for cleanrooms available in late 2028 and beyond.

but some equipment spending was being pulled forward to get more production out of existing space.

both can happen. a bigger customer budget needs to become equipment orders and delivery dates before it becomes lam revenue. stronger tool sales also don’t tell you how quickly additional memory reaches the market.

my pre-call checklist (prepared using @tessara_ai's earnings record):

#1: does september’s step-up carry into december?

lam guided september revenue to $8.10bn ± $400m, versus $6.72bn in june. the midpoint already implies 20.5% sequential growth, with non-GAAP gross margin guided to 52% ± 1 percentage point.

a large increase is already in management’s plan. i want december guidance backed by customer delivery schedules. a sequential decline needs context before we call it weaker demand.

#2: what is driving NAND equipment demand?

lam said june NAND revenue doubled sequentially.

how much comes from upgrades and technology conversions, versus new wafer capacity? when does that spending become saleable memory?

a useful accounting detail: lam’s $2.47bn customer-support business includes upgrades and equipment alongside service and spares. treating all of it as recurring maintenance obscures part of the investment cycle.

#3: how much of customers’ higher budgets becomes 2027 tool deliveries?

micron’s construction timetable makes this worth asking. it doesn’t prove weak near-term equipment demand: some spending is moving forward, and micron has projects scheduled for 2027. one customer also cannot establish the industry picture.

specific installation windows would strengthen the revenue bridge. another broad statement about rising AI capex leaves it unresolved.

There are two kinds of people in this space.

Those who wish to make it.
And those who work to make it.

The workers are rare. You won't find them in group chats hyping the next 100x. They're somewhere quieter - building, iterating, doubting themselves, then continuing anyway.

They don't check their portfolio every hour. They check their progress. Their projects aren't "holdings." They're pieces of themselves they've put into the world.

The workers often seem disconnected. Obsessed. Maybe even foolish. But they understand something the wishers never will:

When you pour yourself into something, it becomes part of you.

Years ago, a random memecoin launched using the same name as @ethereumJoseph's company. Joseph Lubin - a man who rarely speaks - broke his silence to call it what it was: A SCAM.

Not out of anger. Out of protection.

Someone touched something sacred to him. His life's work. His legacy.

In that moment, I understood him completely.

I didn't create Book of Ethereum. I found it. Joined its community. And somewhere along the way, I decided to build.

Now it's the first thing I think about when I wake up and the last thing on my mind before I sleep.

It's not a bag I'm waiting to sell.
It's a legacy I'm helping to create.

If you've ever poured yourself into something the world might never understand - you already know exactly what I'm talking about.

The wishers are waiting for their moment.
The workers are building theirs.

I know which one I am 🙏📖

text:
PHP 曝两个免登录就能接管服务器的漏洞，AI 参与发现，所有 PHP 网站要马上升级

PHP 官方 10 月 21 日紧急发布 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36、8.2.35，修补两个严重漏洞（CVE-2026-109618、CVE-2026-109619，研究者叫它 PHP2Shell）。按 PHP 官方的说法，攻击者不用登录，发特制请求就可能在服务器上执行任意代码，等于拿到整台服务器。WordPress、Drupal、Magento 都跑在 PHP 上，OpenAI 引用的估算是约 70% 的网站在用它。

【我的 PHP 网站受影响吗】

基本都在范围内。PHP 官方说，凡是对外处理网页请求的 PHP 都有风险，PHP-FPM、Apache mod_php、LiteSpeed 等常见跑法全包括，mod_php 风险最高。按 Wiz 和 Sansec 的说法，2012 年发布的 PHP 5.4 以来的版本都受影响。

问题出在 PHP 引擎本身，好比大楼门锁坏了，你家装修得再好也没用。Wiz 和 Calif 已在最新版 WordPress、Drupal、Laravel 等上演示了免登录攻击。

【现在该做什么】

自己管服务器的：立刻升级到上面四个版本之一。PHP 8.1 及更早版本官方已停止维护，只给了 7.4、8.0、8.1 的源码补丁；用 Ubuntu、Debian 等发行版自带 PHP 的，看发行版的安全更新。

用虚拟主机、托管 WordPress 的普通站长：PHP 由主机商管，装插件、改网站代码都修不了。去控制面板看 PHP 版本，或直接问主机商补了没有。

PHP 官方给的临时配置只能降低风险，官方明确说升级才是唯一完整的办法。Cloudflare 给所有用户（含免费版）上了拦截规则，但它自己也说只是临时挡一下，而且只管经过 Cloudflare 的流量，攻击者绕开它直连服务器就挡不住。

【AI 立了什么功】

OpenAI 说，安全公司 Calif 在它的 Patch the Planet 计划里用 GPT-5.6 Sol 找到漏洞。据 Sansec 整理的时间线，Calif 8 月 11 日就报给了 PHP；Wiz 也独立发现并上报，用的是 Gemini 4 Argon 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 等工具。OpenAI 称两个月来牵头协调维护者和安全厂商准备修复，认为这是近年影响最大的漏洞之一，也是 AI 抢在攻击者前面发现漏洞的例子。

【提前泄露了吗】

属实。漏洞原定 10 月 22 日公开，20 日有人在 Hacker News 发帖提前曝光，帖子删了但截图已传开，PHP 官方随即把发布提前到 21 日。

攻击已经开始。Cloudflare CTO 在补丁发布前几小时就说看到早期攻击；安全公司 watchTowr 说已有人用 AI 辅助写的工具发起攻击，"目前还没人成功，但不会太久"。荷兰政府的 DigiD 等网站先自行下线避险。

PHP 官方公告：https://t.co/UZYhjf3CWO
OpenAI 原文：https://t.co/jKdbrEaMB8
Wiz 技术说明：https://t.co/SrODSYiXOv

OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact.

text:
🟣Derive becomes the back-end for options: even greater potential than for perps?

With its V3 launched on October 6, @DeriveXYZ left its own blockchain for a zero-knowledge application that settles directly on Ethereum. 

The protocol now opens its risk engine, its margin system, its settlement and its market makers’ liquidity to other applications, all accessible through a single API and with no bridge to manage.

To get these applications to actually plug into it, Derive relies on its Builder Codes, launched in February on the same principle as those of @HyperliquidX. An app sends its users’ orders to Derive and can add its own fees on top.

This is precisely the model that is one of the reasons behind Hyperliquid’s success. 

Typically, by integrating perps into its wallet through Builder Codes, @phantom generated around $20M in fees in less than a year, from users who, for the most part, had never opened Hyperliquid.

In our view, for options, the growth potential driven by Builder Codes is even greater than for perps. 

Indeed, at present, their complexity is a major obstacle to their adoption, and most crypto traders have never used this kind of product in DeFi.

Builder Codes can remove exactly this obstacle. Instead of showing the user a table full of prices, expiration dates and technical indicators, an application plugged into Derive can simply offer them simple goals, such as:

◻️“Protect your ethereum:native below $3,000”, which in reality amounts to buying a put.

◻️“Generate yield by agreeing to sell your ethereum:native at $6,000”, which corresponds to selling a covered call.

The user doesn’t need to know which product they are buying or selling behind the scenes. 

Derive takes care of the heaviest part, with the risk engine, margin, settlement and the liquidity provided by market makers. 

Builders handle the interface, the user experience and take care of attracting users.

That’s why the potential seems greater to us than for perps. With Hyperliquid, builders made accessible a product that was already fairly simple to understand. 

With Derive, applications could get people to use options who would never have bought them otherwise.

It remains to be seen whether builders will follow. For now, only a few, such as @dreaming, @LEVR_money and @hunchdotcool, have taken the plunge.

We cover everything in detail in our full article, available below 👇

quoted_text:
44% of public miners' MW is contracted to AI/HPC in 2026-28, as they pivot toward more profitable operations leveraging sites for AI.

With mining costs already near $75k and the 2028 halving approaching, this will only worsen.

Pearl's FP8 removes this risk. Instead of forcing miners to choose between mining BTC or providing inference (useful work they get paid for), they can do both: mining PRL requires the same matrix calculations as AI inference. As public companies that maximize the value of their hardware, it's clear to me that these players will mine Pearl in addition to their inference work.

There are three bull cases for this:

1. Store-of-value assets lack clear valuation frameworks, and hashrate is the "hardest" quantifiable metric available. While not an ideal comparison, Pearl, with significant hashrate from miners that opt in, would be extremely undervalued on this basis.

2. Alternative SOVs have emerged as alternatives to BTC, attempting to solve some of the issues its ossification presents. These assets have, however, been constrained on the network security and hashrate side. Pearl, by making hashrate acquisition trivial, removes this constraint, allowing innovation in newer SOVs without the security bottleneck. Like ZEC, for example, Pearl is also targeting quantum resistance.

3. Alignment. Assets like BTC gain value because others believe in them and give them value (e.g., why does ZEC have more value than XMR?). Just as naturally as existing BTC miners will provide security for Pearl, it follows from the same first-principles thinking that they maximize their expected value, and so they become strong and powerful advocates of the coin.

This makes a compelling bull case: Pearl, like ZEC, is a modern SOV that is able to react to a changing technological landscape, targeting things like quantum and potentially privacy. However, it also has no network security concerns, a very clear path for hashrate and network security expansion, and will likely have huge BTC miners and potentially AI data centers as advocates. It is also 1/30th the market cap of ZEC.

At the end of the day it is ultimately just a memecoin (like BTC). But a memecoin with an incredibly compelling narrative, and likely a narrative very influental entities will rally behind.

text:
Vitalik said on Monday that Ethereum should never need to add another precompile, and I've been chewing on that since.

His argument starts with a boring constraint.
Anything a precompile or the EVM checks has to be in the block, usually as calldata.
He puts the practical ceiling at around 8 MB/s, even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs.

Post-quantum signatures are big.
If every wallet starts posting them on-chain, that ceiling shows up fast.

His answer is what he called "EIP-8288 maximalism."

The draft EIP works roughly like this.
A transaction doesn't carry the heavy proof inside the block.
It declares a small dependency instead: a scheme, a hash of the data, and a hash of the verification key.

The actual signatures and proofs travel through the mempool.
Nodes and the builder fold them into one recursive STARK.

The block header gets a single new field with that STARK and a hash of all the block's dependencies.
The block is only valid if the STARK proves every one of them.

So the chain learns that the check passed, and never stores what was checked.

Think of a building where the guard doesn't read everyone's ID.
One person checks them all outside and hands the guard a single signed note.

The vision is lovely, but the draft isn't there yet.
Right now it supports two schemes, LeanSPHINCS signatures and LeanSTARK proofs, and some core parameters are still marked as to be defined.
Proving in the mempool also moves real work onto whoever runs those nodes.

OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact.

text:
A few reflections on the lattice vs. hash-only debate that our recent Aerie post sparked:

1. Cryptographic ossification for blockchains was never safe. Until the day we know with certainty that P ≠ NP, that finding short vectors in lattices is intractable, that Keccak effectively behaves like a random oracle in deployed SNARKs, and that every single bug has been eliminated from our codebases, blockchains cannot ossify. That is simply not how safe systems are built. Issues will arise, and the system will have to respond.

It’s a double standard to reject lattices because blockchains are hard to upgrade if lattices break, while counting on upgrades if AI breaks your hash function or finds a critical zkVM bug.

The best counterargument is that hash-only designs are more agile: if your hash function breaks, just swap out the hash. But we must aspire to a higher level of agility than this. Indeed, as I cover next, if SNARK recursion itself turns out to degrade security, the proposed hash-only blockchain designs would need to be rethought from the ground up.

2. The real security debate is not lattices vs. hashes — it is lattices vs. building everything on SNARK recursion. That’s because “hash-only” is not really hash-only: it rests on hashes plus the soundness of deep SNARK recursion. Ethereum’s roadmap relies on exactly that: hash-based aggregation needs recursion to keep up with a slot’s worth of signatures, and EIP-8288 would send other signature schemes and users’ own proofs through the same recursive pipeline. In contrast, Aerie proves a slot’s worth of signatures on one laptop without any recursion.

All deployed post-quantum SNARKs rely on the Random Oracle Methodology (via Fiat–Shamir) to establish their security. This is an idealization we know fails in the real world: we have explicit counterexamples where “SNARKs” coming out of this methodology are totally insecure when instantiated with any concrete hash function.

We generally ignore these counterexamples in part because they only arise when proving contrived, self-referential statements about the very hash function used by the SNARK verifier.

But proving statements about the verifier’s own hash function is the exact thing you do in SNARK recursion. That’s why the security of recursive SNARKs can’t be established even in the random oracle model.

On top of that, the standard security proofs for recursion (in other models) suffer an “extractor runtime” blowup that is exponential in the recursion depth, suggesting that security may degrade as more recursion is applied. Yet Ethereum’s own EIP-8288 enables unlimited-depth recursion, even as it lists soundness of recursive SNARKs as a trust assumption. Proofs in more idealized models avoid the blowup, but they mainly tell us that an attack on SNARK recursion would have to exploit the concrete hash function, which is exactly what the Fiat–Shamir attacks above do.

To be clear, we don’t know of any outright attacks on SNARK recursion, and I very much hope it is secure. But some of us who have studied the question have a lingering sense that an attack may be possible in some settings. And if AI is going to supercharge cryptanalysis, there is no reason to expect it to spare Fiat–Shamir for SNARKs, let alone SNARK recursion, both of which have had far less scrutiny than lattices.

So, I do not concede that a “recursion everywhere” hash-only approach is clearly more conservative than one built on standard lattice assumptions.

3. “Just wrap everything in a hash-based SNARK” (like EIP-8288) faces challenges.

Aggregating signatures and proofs off-chain into a single block-level proof is a powerful design independent of the hash-only vs. lattice debate, and I am not telling people to avoid it. But claiming, as Vitalik Buterin did this week, that users can run whatever cryptography they want locally and wrap it in a client-side leanVM proof glosses over major hurdles.
For example, leanVM today is a minimal VM designed almost entirely to prove hash-based signatures and recursion, not general-purpose computation. And binary-field SNARKs like leanVM remain slow at proving the integer multiplications that lattice cryptography does en masse.

I am optimistic that many of these zkVM challenges can be met (including via my own work, binary-field Twist and Shout, which are now implemented in Magnetar). But regardless, if lattices can make aggregation simpler and faster, then they should be leveraged. We need to be agile no matter what.

4. For chains whose reason for existence is privacy, I truly struggle to understand the pushback. Public-key encryption (and fast single-server PIR) cannot be built from hashes alone, at least not in any black-box way. If lattices break, it is going to be very, very hard for these chains to provide acceptable levels of privacy and functionality. For a project whose entire reason for existence is privacy, a loss of confidentiality is an existential failure. Next to that, a second signature upgrade (after the first one, from elliptic curves alone to, hopefully, a hybrid lattice scheme) is easy.

Summary: We don’t know for sure what is secure and what isn’t. We are all weighing unquantifiable risks against each other, and we do not need to agree on a total order on them. But hash-only solutions face many open engineering challenges, and they are not more “conservative” in the way some have argued. Some of those challenges are entirely prosaic and have nothing to do with bugs or cryptography, like hardware support for custom schemes whose hash function is still undecided. I hope we can overcome those challenges within the appropriate timelines, but they must be acknowledged and portrayed realistically.

Overall, cryptographic agility and defense in depth (e.g., hybrid signatures) are the answer, which is why we are building both lattice-Jolt and hash-Jolt. In practice, the positions are less polarized than social media discourse suggests: for example, StarkWare is working to make Falcon verification cheap (https://t.co/FM68hmkqRx), which is great to see.

Here is the (apparently) controversial take I am sticking to: Conditioned on agility, whenever lattices make systems simpler or more functional, we should embrace them rather than default to “hash-only” designs. Lattices are what the rest of the world will depend on, with decades of study and hardening behind them, and at the system level, less functional often means less secure. Where hash-only designs are just as simple and functional, by all means use them.

text:
You must be concerned about PHP2Shell🚨 

TLDR: 

Two critical vulnerabilities have been disclosed in PHP, the technology used for 70% of the internet.

CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

So an attacker can potentially execute malicious code on a vulnerable server without authentication.

In certain Apache configurations, the attack can happen before WordPress, Magento or any other application even starts running.

Now imagine what happens when that server belongs to a crypto exchange.

This could potentially access exchange APIs, withdrawal infrastructure, cloud credentials, databases or even systems connected to hot wallets.

And the attacker doesn’t need to compromise a smart contract to get there.

PHP had to bring its emergency update forward from October 22 to October 21.

Some patched images were reportedly released ahead of schedule, potentially giving attackers a chance to reverse-engineer the fixes while millions of systems were still waiting to update.

Security researchers have already reported attack attempts.

The vulnerable PHP runtime itself needs to be patched.

Fixed versions are: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

I’ve spent years watching people lose millions in crypto through compromised wallets, malicious contracts and stolen credentials.

But imagine losing everything because a forgotten web server had access to your withdrawal systems.

text:
How I track Robinhood Chain (and everything else)

I built a research desk with Claude (Opus 5.5) and Grok @bot.

Grok Bot watches X and the chain 24/7. Claude is my analyst, keeping the whole system running, improving, and accountable.

The radar (Grok Bot, always on)
• Every hour: trending and new pools, plus any token moving 15%+ in an hour
• Every hour: one X search across 49 project and founder accounts to flag any interest
• Every 2 hours: news and FUD on each core project
• 4x a day: who @vladtenev, @fern, @JohannKerbrat, @RobinhoodApp and @RobinhoodCrypto just engaged with
• A digest every morning

One rule: no alert without a WHY. A price move alone never pings me. It needs several accounts talking and an active catalyst across many surfaces

The desk (Claude)
• A thesis card for every holding: support and resistance from real candles, holders, liquidity, social and the macro backdrop
• My own rules for each position: "working if" and "reconsider if"
• Probability-weighted scenarios, dated and graded every few days
• A relative-strength screen across Robinhood, Base, Ethereum, BNB and Solana to catch leaders early
• Copycat checks: full contract addresses only, because fakes copy the first and last characters
• Holder labels (pools, burns, lockers, real people) before calling any token "concentrated"
• A knowledge base with one note per project, every fact dated and tagged verified, claimed or unconfirmed

PnL Tracker
• Every wallet I own, synced hourly: buys, sells, average entry, realized and unrealized PnL
• Cost basis and tax export in one place

It improves itself
• Claude reviews the radar every morning and redesigns it every Sunday if necessary
• Every alert is scored 1h, 24h and 72h later

Next: 
• Traction watchers that flag usage before price. The first one is live on $ORBIO, $NET, $PONS, $STANDARD
• Mid-cap entries and exit opportunities (HYPE, ZEC type of plays)

Having a system that can monitor onchain and socials for me is key. I am already a profitable trader, but this helps me keep things tight in my head and execute better.

At the end of the day, I make the decisions, but we all just need a little help with the mania of the daily crypto grind

据 CoinDesk 报道，美国货币监理署（OCC）发布《GENIUS 法案》首项最终实施规则，明确稳定币发行、托管及第三方合作的监管要求，将于 2027 年 1 月 18 日生效。针对稳定币收益及奖励计划，OCC 表示，现有项目不会因推出时间早于法案而自动被视为合规，也不提供既有业务的安全港豁免，监管机构将根据具体安排逐案判断。

《GENIUS 法案》禁止稳定币发行方向持有人支付仅因持有、使用或保留稳定币而产生的收益，但不意味着所有第三方奖励计划均被禁止。OCC 指出，如果奖励至少部分基于其他原因，可能不属于该禁令范围。目前，Coinbase、PayPal 和 Kraken 等平台均提供稳定币奖励计划，未来相关安排的合规性仍存在不确定性。

text: This is one of the clearest and more direct communiques on the CVEs affecting PHP that dropped today
author: DavidAgranovich
quoted_text:
Two critical vulnerabilities have been identified in PHP, a widely used programming language that powers websites and web applications. These vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) could allow malicious cyber actors to remotely execute code in PHP core, potentially compromising sensitive data and networks.

The FBI urges organizations to take the following steps now:

➡️ If an immediate update is not feasible it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.

➡️ Immediately update affected PHP installations following the guidance on https://t.co/rDrPSxB3zX. Inventory where PHP runs in your environment, prioritizing internet-facing systems and vendor products that bundle PHP.

➡️ Monitor web servers for suspicious activity, including PHP processes unexpectedly launching command shells or downloading files. Ensure appropriate process-monitoring capabilities are in place to help identify potential exploitation.

➡️ If you find signs of compromise, isolate affected systems, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office or https://t.co/iqgVZIbCru. Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.

For the latest information, follow PHP’s announcement on https://t.co/rDrPSxB3zX, CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018, and CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

quoted_text:
OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.
