text:
NVIDIA just open-sourced a blueprint for running AI agents safely, and it reads like a syllabus for anyone who wants to build agent infrastructure.

It's called the OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced at GTC Berlin on Wednesday.

One line in NVIDIA's technical blog stuck with me.
"An agent cannot govern itself."

The design follows from that.
OpenShell treats every agent workload as untrusted, and splits control into four parts.
A Gateway manages sandbox lifecycles and policies.
A Sandbox isolates the agent and restricts what files and processes it can touch.
A Supervisor checks every outbound request against policy and mediates access to credentials.
A Policy Prover formally checks that a policy's permissions stay under a ceiling the organisation sets.

So the agent never holds the keys.
It asks, and something it can't edit decides.
If I were a developer trying to get good at agent infrastructure, this is the order I'd go in.

- Stage one is isolation.
Learn containers, filesystem permissions and syscall filtering well enough to explain why an agent can't read your SSH keys.

- Stage two is egress.
Put a proxy between an agent and the internet, and write allow rules by domain and method.

- Stage three is credentials.
Stop putting API keys in the agent's environment, and have a broker inject scoped, short-lived tokens per request.

- Stage four is policy as code.
Write permissions as files you can diff, review and test, and then look at how the Policy Prover checks them against a ceiling.

- Stage five is observability.
Log every tool call and request so you can replay what the agent did and why.

None of this needs NVIDIA hardware to learn.
The repo is on GitHub, and the RFCs explain each piece.

See links below.

quoted_text:
owning paper is owning a share in the house

this is only valuable insofar as the house is valuable. owning a lot of a dead house is worthless, and any design that would let the house stay at zero is a failed design.

when we went out, there were certain known problems with known timelines (builder codes) and some unsolved problems with unknown timelines. the perp attack described in the main was an unsolved problem, but we hoped to solve it as we made progress elsewhere. we knew it was impossible to set all the parameters and variables perfectly prelaunch - we are the first through the wall in a very adversarial environment - and i thought we would have more time to find solutions. unfortunately, the way things are advancing, we dont have six months until a large perp listing, its coming already. these were labelled as unsolved  “good problems” and here we are. the market forced our hand into making the decision before we found a solution to the problem, and so for the health of the protocol the token is now non-transferrable. i want to thank all of the pre-market perp dexes, especially the hyperliquid ecosystem ones, who were in contact through this process. i am sorry I was not able to find a design for transferability that worked, i tried very hard.

ultimately, the success of papertrade relies on what it always has - whether the end product has user PMF. i have extreme confidence in the product we've built and continue to add to. i have had to personally self-exclude myself from similar products before because i used them too much. the token being transferable or not does not change whether a degen will longterm choose to trade on papertrade or not. the execution, site quality, mechanism, and economics of the trade will. papertrade is the fastest way to go from usdc in your wallet on any chain to a leveraged speculation exposure. providing clean, working, composability derivative liquidity in a permissionless environment is the vision. 

thank you for your all your support since launch, and good luck to us

author: eliebakouch
quoted_text:
verifying the science of LLM training is just a function of compute, and as compute scales you can almost infinitely parallelize and compress time

math was even easier, tons of existing data, you only need inference tokens, it's extremely parallelizable and proofs almost never have negative second order interactions with each other

even if model training is less of a perfect testbed than math, there is no doubt this will happen too. the big difference is that it needs 2*compute (inference and A LOT of training compute) so much less accessible, but the dynamics are the same

labs have spent enormous effort figuring out the right metrics for training. for pre-training it's relatively straightforward - which is also good news for tracking RSI - you establish a scaling ladder and measure the "efficiency gain": for a given budget, how much does a new proposal save compared to baseline to reach the same metric?

the question is how you define this "efficiency gain", which efficiency (flops? time? KV cache? data efficiency?..) and which gain (val loss? knowledge? reasoning?..)

i think it's quite similar for post training (modulo reward hacking), i would hope it's similar for alignment as well but after listening to @dwarkesh_sp <> @polynoamial itw i'm not sure as the "gain" here would assume that we have a correct way to measure behavior without eval awareness, probably other stuff i'm not thinking of here

anyway, when you put all of this together, hard to not believe in RSI

text:
第一章：重生
2019年1月1日，凌晨三点。
我猛地从床上坐起来。
眼前不是熟悉的2026年，而是一间破旧的出租屋。
桌上摆着一台ThinkPad，屏幕右下角显示：
`2019/01/01 03:17`
我愣了足足十秒。
随后，狂喜。
我重生了。
上一世，我是国内顶尖的安全研究员，连续七十二小时处理零日漏洞，最终猝死在工位上。
这一世，我回到了七年前。
但更恐怖的是——
我的脑海里，竟然保留着截至2026年的全部CVE漏洞信息。
不只是编号。
还包括漏洞成因、受影响版本、利用原理，以及那些曾经震惊世界的安全事件。
我颤抖着打开记事本。
输入：
`CVE-2021-44228`
Log4Shell。
2021年才会震惊全球的Java日志组件漏洞。
现在，距离它公开还有将近三年。
我又输入：
`CVE-2024-3094`
XZ Utils供应链后门事件。
距离它被发现，还有五年。
最后，我输入了两个编号。
`CVE-2026-109618`
`CVE-2026-109619`
PHP2Shell。
两个直到2026年10月才会震惊全球的PHP核心漏洞。
CVSS评分高达9.2。
在特定条件下，甚至可以实现未经身份验证的远程代码执行。
而现在，是2019年。
距离它们公开，还有整整七年。
我盯着屏幕，缓缓笑了。
别人重生，靠炒股、买比特币、囤房子。
而我……
掌握着未来七年互联网的所有致命弱点。
上一世，我为了修复漏洞，死在了工位上。
这一世，我突然想明白了一件事。
为什么一定要修复漏洞？
如果全世界都不知道自己的系统存在什么问题。
而只有我知道。
那么……
我为什么不让全世界为这些秘密付费？
我关掉记事本，打开终端。
创建了一个加密目录。
`/home/hek/0day/`
随后，我在里面新建了一个文件。
`2026_PHP2SHELL.txt`
文件的最后，我写下一句话。
“这一世，我不当救世主。”
“我要当那个决定谁能得救的人。”
第二章：第一个一百万
2019年1月3日。
我注册了一个匿名账号。
ID：`hek`
随后开始联系各大厂商的安全响应中心。
我的计划非常简单。
提前寻找、验证并报告一部分漏洞。
领取漏洞赏金。
积累名声。
然后成立自己的安全公司。
至于那些真正致命的漏洞……
我选择暂时保留。
第一个月，我拿到了人生中第一笔六位数奖金。
第三个月，我的账户余额突破一百万。
半年后，一家国际安全公司找到了我。
对方的首席研究员在视频会议里问：
“你到底是谁？”
我靠在椅子上，喝了一口可乐。
“一个普通的安全研究员。”
“普通？”
对方沉默了很久。
“你过去六个月提交的漏洞报告，比我们整个团队过去三年的成果还多。”
我笑了。
因为他不知道。
我提交出去的漏洞，甚至不到我掌握总量的百分之一。
“hek先生，我们愿意聘请您担任首席安全研究员，年薪两百万美元。”
我摇了摇头。
“我对打工没兴趣。”
“那您想要什么？”
我看着屏幕，缓缓说道：
“我要成立一家安全公司。”
“然后呢？”
“让全世界最大的互联网企业，都成为我的客户。”
对方笑了。
“您知道这有多难吗？”
我没有回答。
只是打开了一份文档。
里面列着未来五年，数十个尚未公开的高危漏洞编号。
我随手挑出其中一个，将不涉及利用细节的风险报告发了过去。
十分钟后。
对方的笑容消失了。
“这……这不可能。”
“我们的内部团队根本没有发现这个问题。”
我靠在椅子上。
“所以，现在你明白了吗？”
“明白什么？”
我笑了。
“不是我需要你们。”
“是你们需要我。”
那天晚上，我注册了一家公司。
名字很简单。
`HEK Security`
我将未来七年的CVE信息分成了三个等级。
普通漏洞，用来换取赏金。
严重漏洞，用来换取商业合同。
至于那些足以改变整个互联网安全格局的漏洞……
全部锁进了最高权限的数据库。
其中，有一个单独的目录。
`PHP2SHELL`
我给它设置了一个特殊标签。
`DO_NOT_DISCLOSE`
因为我知道。
真正的大戏，还没开始。
第三章：2021年的灾难，被我提前终结了
2021年12月。
全世界的安全人员都在等待一场本应发生的风暴。
但这一次，没有Log4Shell危机。
因为早在2019年，我就联系了相关项目的维护者，推动了危险设计的修改和防护机制的完善。
当年那个足以让无数企业彻夜不眠的漏洞，再也没有以原本的形式出现。
媒体争相报道。
《神秘安全天才hek，再次阻止全球互联网灾难》
《HEK Security：最年轻的网络安全独角兽》
我的公司已经拥有三千名员工。
全球数十家大型科技企业购买了我们的安全服务。
媒体称我为：
“能够预知零日漏洞的男人。”
有人在采访中问我：
“hek先生，您为什么愿意提前公开这么重要的漏洞？”
我对着镜头笑了笑。
“因为互联网的安全，需要我们每一个人共同维护。”
掌声雷动。
没有人知道。
就在采访的前一天，我刚刚拒绝了另一家企业的漏洞修复请求。
原因很简单。
他们不愿意购买我的安全服务。
我救了世界一次。
从此以后，所有人都觉得我是英雄。
但只有我知道。
一个曾经拯救过世界的人，才最容易让世界对他放下戒心。
而我真正的计划，才刚刚开始。
从2022年开始，我记忆中的一些CVE逐渐失效了。
不是因为我记错。
而是因为……
我改变了未来。
原本存在漏洞的软件，被提前修复。
原本会引入缺陷的代码，不再被提交。
原本成功的供应链入侵，也被拦截在了最初阶段。
时间线，开始偏移。
我脑海中的未来知识，正在逐渐过期。
直到2024年3月。
XZ后门事件原本应该爆发的那一天。
什么都没有发生。
因为早在几个月前，我就通过匿名渠道，提前阻止了那次供应链入侵。
我看着系统里干干净净的安全报告，第一次意识到一个问题。
如果我修复了未来所有已知的漏洞。
那么未来就会开始产生我不知道的漏洞。
而未知，是我唯一无法掌控的东西。
我沉默了很久。
随后，打开了那份存放了五年的数据库。
`/home/hek/0day/2026/`
里面还有大量没有公开的CVE。
我一条条检查过去。
最后，将目光停留在了两个编号上。
`CVE-2026-109618`
`CVE-2026-109619`
PHP2Shell。
它们一直没有被我主动干预。
不是因为我忘了。
而是因为……
我需要给未来留下一场足够大的灾难。
一个能够让全世界重新认识hek的机会。
毕竟。
当所有人都知道某个人能拯救世界的时候。
他们就会开始依赖这个人。
而当这种依赖足够深……
他就不再需要拯救世界了。
世界会主动向他低头。
我关掉电脑。
在私人日记里写下一句话。
“2026年10月21日。”
“收网。”
第四章：一条不存在的CVE
2026年10月21日。
凌晨三点十七分。
公司安全监控中心突然响起刺耳的警报。
全球十七个数据中心同时出现异常。
没有已知恶意软件特征。
没有可匹配的攻击情报。
所有防御系统同时失去部分可见性。
值班工程师满头大汗：
“老板！我们遇到了一个全新的零日漏洞！”
“CVE编号呢？”
“还没分配！”
“攻击源？”
“不知道！”
“漏洞类型？”
“也不知道！”
我盯着屏幕。
突然，另一名工程师冲了过来。
“老板！我们发现了PHP内核的严重异常！”
“两个漏洞特征与您数据库里的记录高度吻合！”
我缓缓开口：
“CVE-2026-109618，CVE-2026-109619。”
工程师愣住了。
“您……您怎么知道？”
我没有回答。
因为我知道，这就是PHP2Shell。
上一世，它在2026年10月21日引发了全球安全危机。
而现在……
历史正在重演。
只是这一次，情况似乎有些不同。
“老板！”工程师突然喊道。
“还有另一部分攻击行为，完全不符合我们掌握的任何CVE！”
我皱起眉头。
“不可能。”
我的脑海里拥有截至2026年的全部CVE信息。
如果连我都不知道……
那就只有一种可能。
这个漏洞，不属于2026年。
就在这时。
所有监控屏幕同时变黑。
一行绿色字符缓缓出现。
`Hello, hek.`
我的血液瞬间凝固。
第二行字符出现。
`你修复了太多本该发生的漏洞。`
第三行。
`所以，我不得不亲自制造一些。`
我猛地站了起来。
屏幕上弹出了最后一条消息：
`你真的以为……`
`只有你一个人重生了吗？`
紧接着，一个熟悉的名字出现在屏幕中央。
那是我上一世的安全团队负责人。
也是……
那个在我猝死前，递给我最后一杯咖啡的人。
我的手机响了。
陌生号码。
我接通电话。
对面传来一个男人的笑声。
“好久不见，hek。”
“上一世你总是比我快一步。”
“这一世，我等了你七年。”
我握紧手机。
“你到底想干什么？”
男人轻轻笑了。
“你带回来的是全部CVE，对吧？”
“真巧。”
“我带回来的……”
电话那头停顿了一秒。
“是全部CVE的利用代码，以及Deepseek 4.1 Flash的权重。”
我沉默了。
男人似乎很享受这一刻。
“怎么，不说话了？”
“你是不是以为，自己掌握了未来七年的漏洞，就能成为互联网的神？”
“你知道吗？”
“你引以为傲的PHP2Shell，在Deepseek的技术面前，根本不值一提。”
“你花了七年时间，建立了一个庞大的安全帝国。”
“而我只需要一个晚上，就能让它彻底崩塌。”
我没有回答。
只是缓缓打开终端。
男人继续说道：
“hek，我知道你最大的秘密。”
“你明明知道PHP2Shell，却没有提前公开。”
“你根本不是什么英雄。”
“你只是一个靠漏洞赚钱的骗子！”
我突然笑了。
电话那头安静下来。
“你笑什么？”
我靠在椅子上。
“你说得没错。”
“我确实知道PHP2Shell。”
“而且，我早在2019年就知道。”
男人冷笑。
“那又怎么样？”
我望着屏幕上不断闪烁的红色警报。
“你觉得奇怪吗？”
“什么？”
“为什么我能提前修复Log4Shell？”
“为什么我能阻止XZ后门？”
“为什么所有可能影响我公司发展的重大漏洞，都被我提前处理了？”
“唯独PHP2Shell……”
我停顿了一下。
“被我完整地留到了今天。”
电话那头突然没了声音。
几秒钟后。
男人缓缓开口：
“你什么意思？”
我笑了。
“你以为，我真的不知道会有人来找我？”
“从2019年开始，我就在想一件事。”
“如果我能重生，那么别人是不是也可以？”
“如果有人和我一样，知道未来的漏洞。”
“他一定会想办法除掉我。”
“所以，我需要一个诱饵。”
男人的呼吸明显急促起来。
“PHP2Shell……”
“没错。”
我打断了他。
“我没有提前公开它，就是为了让这一天按照我记忆中的日期到来。”
“我知道2026年10月21日，会是整个互联网最紧张的一天。”
“我也知道，如果你想对我动手……”
“没有比今天更合适的机会了。”
男人怒吼：
“你疯了吗？！你拿整个互联网当诱饵？！”
我平静地回答：
“整个互联网？”
“你太看得起他们了。”
“对我来说，它不过是一张棋盘。”
电话那头传来急促的键盘声。
男人似乎正在向他的团队下达指令。
我看着屏幕。
全球十七个数据中心的警报依然没有停止。
但我并不着急。
因为我等的，从来不是阻止这场攻击。
我等的，是让对方主动暴露自己。
七年来，我建立的并不只是一家安全公司。
全球漏洞情报平台。
云安全基础设施。
企业级应急响应系统。
数千家大型公司的长期安全协议。
这些东西，早已形成了一张庞大的网络。
而今天，对方亲手证明了这张网络有多么重要。
“老板！”
身后的工程师突然喊道。
“全球数百家企业向我们发来了紧急援助请求！”
“多家云服务商申请接入我们的应急响应系统！”
“还有政府机构，希望我们接管部分安全协调工作！”
我笑了。
终于。
七年的布局。
到了收获的时候。
电话那头的男人突然明白了什么。
“你……你从一开始就没打算阻止这场危机？”
我没有否认。
“你故意让他们依赖你？”
“没错。”
“你甚至不在乎会有多少人因此受到影响？”
我看着窗外。
凌晨的城市，依然灯火通明。
“你还是和上一世一样天真。”
“漏洞会被修复。”
“服务器会重新启动。”
“损失的金钱，也总有人会赚回来。”
我缓缓站起身。
“但恐惧，会留在每个人心里。”
“而我，就是那个出售安全感的人。”
电话那头陷入死寂。
过了很久，男人咬牙说道：
“hek，你才是真正的疯子。”
我没有反驳。
只是敲下第一行命令，接通全球应急响应网络。
“你犯了一个错误。”
“什么？”
我笑了。
“你以为，我这七年只是在研究漏洞？”
“你带回来的是Deepseek。”
“而我……”
我转过身，看着身后三千名安全工程师。
“我花了七年，买下了整个安全行业的未来。”
下一秒。
三千名安全工程师的屏幕同时亮起。
“全员上线。”
“启动‘零日黎明’计划。”
“所有签约客户，按照最高优先级启动应急响应。”
“所有未签约企业，转交商务部门。”
身后的助理迟疑了一下。
“老板……那些没有签约的企业怎么办？”
我淡淡地说道：
“把合同发给他们。”
“可是他们现在……”
“我知道。”
我看向屏幕。
无数企业正在等待我们的回应。
“所以他们会签的。”
电话那头传来男人愤怒的声音。
“hek！你这是在趁火打劫！”
我笑了。
“你错了。”
“火不是我放的。”
“我只是提前七年，买下了所有的消防车。”
说完，我挂断电话。
办公室重新安静下来。
我打开了那个从2019年就存在的加密目录。
`/home/hek/0day/`

And you can do the same for any topic you care about. You just need to build a list, or find one that's already built and there are millions of lists here on X on literally any topic.

Put your favorite football team onto a list, along with all your favorite journalists or other fans. Then have Grok bot read them for you. 

And that's just the start. You can have it write you a script based on the news, then copy that into, say, @Gemini_Notebook and then you get a podcast, or a video. Based on what people are saying on your topic here on X.

Thank you so much X for making lists far more powerful than they ever were before. Makes the thousands of hours I've put into mine over 20 years so much more useful.

Tips? 

Start small. You can chew through your tokens very quickly. It's amazing how good it is with a small list, like this one, which is what created the page up above: https://t.co/qyxF8in0sP (Best AI accounts I've found out of 70,000 here on X).

I've been begging for this capability for years. THANK YOU X!

text: very good insight on fiat shamir wrt random oracles in recursive SNARKs, and this validates the slow L1 design philosophy where you can "afford" to have SLH-DSA signatures directly validate in threshold instead of rely on recursion. zkVMs can tinker with recursion for scaling, but the lower on the stack the more conservative you have to be (and thus slower and more focused on security). Would also say the lower in stack the less agile the system should be in an ideal universe, so if we can find a good setting with mechanism design such that we rest on maximally conservative cryptography then we should ossify for longer periods of time to provide determinism for layers/stacks building on top. There really is only one way to do this and that is slow/steady base + DA (hash based) and zkVM on top. I don't see a better design philosophy thats possible otherwise. Time keeps validating it and re-enforcing that type of system.
author: syscoin
quoted_text:
A few reflections on the lattice vs. hash-only debate that our recent Aerie post sparked:

1. Cryptographic ossification for blockchains was never safe. Until the day we know with certainty that P ≠ NP, that finding short vectors in lattices is intractable, that Keccak effectively behaves like a random oracle in deployed SNARKs, and that every single bug has been eliminated from our codebases, blockchains cannot ossify. That is simply not how safe systems are built. Issues will arise, and the system will have to respond.

It’s a double standard to reject lattices because blockchains are hard to upgrade if lattices break, while counting on upgrades if AI breaks your hash function or finds a critical zkVM bug.

The best counterargument is that hash-only designs are more agile: if your hash function breaks, just swap out the hash. But we must aspire to a higher level of agility than this. Indeed, as I cover next, if SNARK recursion itself turns out to degrade security, the proposed hash-only blockchain designs would need to be rethought from the ground up.

2. The real security debate is not lattices vs. hashes — it is lattices vs. building everything on SNARK recursion. That’s because “hash-only” is not really hash-only: it rests on hashes plus the soundness of deep SNARK recursion. Ethereum’s roadmap relies on exactly that: hash-based aggregation needs recursion to keep up with a slot’s worth of signatures, and EIP-8288 would send other signature schemes and users’ own proofs through the same recursive pipeline. In contrast, Aerie proves a slot’s worth of signatures on one laptop without any recursion.

All deployed post-quantum SNARKs rely on the Random Oracle Methodology (via Fiat–Shamir) to establish their security. This is an idealization we know fails in the real world: we have explicit counterexamples where “SNARKs” coming out of this methodology are totally insecure when instantiated with any concrete hash function.

We generally ignore these counterexamples in part because they only arise when proving contrived, self-referential statements about the very hash function used by the SNARK verifier.

But proving statements about the verifier’s own hash function is the exact thing you do in SNARK recursion. That’s why the security of recursive SNARKs can’t be established even in the random oracle model.

On top of that, the standard security proofs for recursion (in other models) suffer an “extractor runtime” blowup that is exponential in the recursion depth, suggesting that security may degrade as more recursion is applied. Yet Ethereum’s own EIP-8288 enables unlimited-depth recursion, even as it lists soundness of recursive SNARKs as a trust assumption. Proofs in more idealized models avoid the blowup, but they mainly tell us that an attack on SNARK recursion would have to exploit the concrete hash function, which is exactly what the Fiat–Shamir attacks above do.

To be clear, we don’t know of any outright attacks on SNARK recursion, and I very much hope it is secure. But some of us who have studied the question have a lingering sense that an attack may be possible in some settings. And if AI is going to supercharge cryptanalysis, there is no reason to expect it to spare Fiat–Shamir for SNARKs, let alone SNARK recursion, both of which have had far less scrutiny than lattices.

So, I do not concede that a “recursion everywhere” hash-only approach is clearly more conservative than one built on standard lattice assumptions.

3. “Just wrap everything in a hash-based SNARK” (like EIP-8288) faces challenges.

Aggregating signatures and proofs off-chain into a single block-level proof is a powerful design independent of the hash-only vs. lattice debate, and I am not telling people to avoid it. But claiming, as Vitalik Buterin did this week, that users can run whatever cryptography they want locally and wrap it in a client-side leanVM proof glosses over major hurdles.
For example, leanVM today is a minimal VM designed almost entirely to prove hash-based signatures and recursion, not general-purpose computation. And binary-field SNARKs like leanVM remain slow at proving the integer multiplications that lattice cryptography does en masse.

I am optimistic that many of these zkVM challenges can be met (including via my own work, binary-field Twist and Shout, which are now implemented in Magnetar). But regardless, if lattices can make aggregation simpler and faster, then they should be leveraged. We need to be agile no matter what.

4. For chains whose reason for existence is privacy, I truly struggle to understand the pushback. Public-key encryption (and fast single-server PIR) cannot be built from hashes alone, at least not in any black-box way. If lattices break, it is going to be very, very hard for these chains to provide acceptable levels of privacy and functionality. For a project whose entire reason for existence is privacy, a loss of confidentiality is an existential failure. Next to that, a second signature upgrade (after the first one, from elliptic curves alone to, hopefully, a hybrid lattice scheme) is easy.

Summary: We don’t know for sure what is secure and what isn’t. We are all weighing unquantifiable risks against each other, and we do not need to agree on a total order on them. But hash-only solutions face many open engineering challenges, and they are not more “conservative” in the way some have argued. Some of those challenges are entirely prosaic and have nothing to do with bugs or cryptography, like hardware support for custom schemes whose hash function is still undecided. I hope we can overcome those challenges within the appropriate timelines, but they must be acknowledged and portrayed realistically.

Overall, cryptographic agility and defense in depth (e.g., hybrid signatures) are the answer, which is why we are building both lattice-Jolt and hash-Jolt. In practice, the positions are less polarized than social media discourse suggests: for example, StarkWare is working to make Falcon verification cheap (https://t.co/FM68hmkqRx), which is great to see.

Here is the (apparently) controversial take I am sticking to: Conditioned on agility, whenever lattices make systems simpler or more functional, we should embrace them rather than default to “hash-only” designs. Lattices are what the rest of the world will depend on, with decades of study and hardening behind them, and at the system level, less functional often means less secure. Where hash-only designs are just as simple and functional, by all means use them.

走普通纳入路径，IPO通常要满12个月，还要满足最近一季盈利、最近四季合计盈利等要求。SpaceX今年6月才上市，正常路径至少得看到2027年6月以后，而且达标也不等于马上入选。特斯拉当年2020年二季度已经连续四季盈利，9月照样没进去，最后等到12月21日。

还有人张嘴就说溢价收购。拿一个纯假设算：特斯拉如果值1.5万亿美元，给20%溢价，就是额外付出3000亿美元。现金收购得找钱，换股收购则要让SpaceX股东接受稀释。两家公司以后的市值差距、换股比例，哪一项都得谈。

所以我暂时不会把“老马觉得合并有道理”，直接理解成“马上合并，还会高溢价收购特斯拉”。独立委员会要谈条件，两边股东都要算账。都是老马的公司，也不能拿一边股东的钱，随手给另一边发红包。 $SPCX  $TSLA

text:
DeepSeek’s DeepInfer is a big deal for open source. But I don't think it is a positive for Local AI adoption.

Cheaper inference is good for users. But it also makes economical calculation of Local worse.

The graph below visualizes the impact from DeepInfer on the cloud side. The left side shows the existing InferenceX benchmarks, and the right side adds DeepInfer. 

Previously, you might have assumed the profit margin on model API costs was around 80%, but with DeepInfer, it would be now closer to 95%.

For $1 of GPU cost, you can generate $24–26 of revenue, about 6x from what was before.

What does that mean? It means their profit margins are 95%+. At DeepSeek’s published off-peak price of $0.60 per million tokens, it costs them $0.03.

What it also means is that the public numbers could just be very off from what people privately have. For example vLLM has already reported decode throughput within 6% of DeepInfer’s published results on GB200, so other providers can get most of the gain too.

Moreover, DeepInfer’s benchmark runs on SM100 GPUs (the B200/GB200 generation), which predate the GB300 baseline in the chart. I think it is reasonable to assume: the GB300 will operate at a similar scale, if not better. 

For OpenAI and Ant, I’d assume they can reach similar efficiency. Betting that they lose money on every heavy subscriber looks not true today. The math is simple. Say inference runs at a hypothetical 95% gross margin. Usage that would bill at $2,000 through the API then costs $100 to serve. A $200 subscription covering that usage still leaves $100 before other expenses. Even $4,000 of API-priced usage would only cost $200.

For Local AI, that means we should expect API competition to get a lot more aggressive.

When cloud prices drop, the payback period on a new local machine gets longer. You still spend time on setup and maintenance.

Local can make a lot of sense for sustained workloads, or if you already own the hardware. But buying an expensive box for occasional use gets hard to justify on savings alone.

The community will keep shipping impressive work, and I love that part. Enthusiasm doesn’t pay the upfront hardware bill, however. As long as capable setups stay expensive, I worry that running the biggest open models locally stays a spectator sport for many people.

When Local AI loses this much of its cost advantage, it puts more weight on privacy and control. 

ZDR on inference providers currently is a mess. Everyone has different standards and almost all are operating on trust-me-bro-and-you-cant-verify limbo. This gives Local AI a unique advantage there. However, the window won't stay open for long and we need to move fast.

Usability has to catch up too. If it's harder to justify on price, people's ability to keep using suboptimal products may also disappear.

I’m still excited about Local AI. I’d just build for a world where cloud inference keeps getting cheaper. In that world, savings alone won’t carry it. Cheaper hardware will help, but dependable privacy and software people actually want to use every day will decide how many people show up.

text:
I think the biggest bottleneck to progress won't be in creating agentic wet-labs but coordinating between them.

Returns to specialization, and optimizing towards data (not compute) constrained objectives will create the opportunity for many compounders across different subdomains. 

As we've seen with the drama around distillation of frontier models, weights for domain-specific models will be similarly be protected at all costs (if not more, since compute is not a constraint). In the process though, gains from collaboration will be overshadowed by losses.

Solving the coordination problem will require tact on distributing IP (just-in-time joint ventures ?) and possibly new mechanisms for communicating requests and results (verifiable forgetting ?).

If it is solved, we'll have a much richer, decentralized ecosystem for scientific discovery and IP generation for human flourishing. If not, we'll see even stronger forces for centralization (through verticalization) emerge.

Would love to hear some creative ideas on how to solve this!

text:
I finally finished all four Flame Lords’ paths in Fortune’s Weave! It took me quite a while, but I can honestly say I enjoyed every single one of them.

If I had to rank them, this would be my order:

1. Theodora — Her storyline was absolutely amazing, and that final war against her brother was easily one of the most enjoyable parts of the entire game. It genuinely felt like an actual war, and I loved every moment of it.

2. Kai / Lida (Tied) — I’ve seen a lot of people rank Kai pretty low, but I personally loved his path. He was my first Flame Lord, so I spent most of my time learning the mechanics and getting attached to his characters. That definitely made his story more special to me. Lida’s path was equally enjoyable, with a great cast of characters and a storyline I really liked.

4. Dietrich — Unfortunately, I have to put him last. His path had far too many skirmishes, and the constant fighting started to feel repetitive and even boring at times. However, when it comes to supporting characters, Dietrich easily takes first place. In my opinion, he had the best supporting cast out of all four Flame Lords.

Now that I’ve finished all four paths, the War Arc is next! I’ll probably start it tomorrow or the day after. I just want to give myself a little break before diving back in.

I genuinely have no idea what to expect from the War Arc, other than knowing it has two parts. But the thought of finally bringing together all these characters I’ve spent over 100 hours with into one army is incredibly exciting.

After everything I’ve experienced throughout these four paths, I can’t wait to see how this war unfolds. I’m so ready for what’s coming!

text:
为什么女人最后都要去炒币？

很多女人到了一定阶段，慢慢开始接触币。只要见过世面，打理过生活资产，并且对金钱有过深度思考的人，最后常会走向加密市场，因为那里才是公平的认知博弈场。

很多人有个误解，觉得加密市场是赌徒才去的地方，其实恰恰相反，它或许是少数不看身份的地方。别的赛道容易拼人脉、拼资源、拼际遇、拼依附，但加密市场只认一件事：判断。看得准，收益落进自己账户；判断失误，市场立刻给出反馈。没有人情捆绑，不用周旋讨好，只看逻辑，也是认知变现效率很高的地方。

而别的路，哪怕再努力，常常要熬漫长时间才能看到回报，还要受很多外部因素牵制。但在加密市场，如果你的逻辑踩对周期，短短一段时间，就有机会盘活手里的资产，掌握属于自己的现金流。

所以那些真正赚过钱、亏过钱、靠自己攒下底气的女人，最后会安安静静坐在屏幕前，用认知和市场对话。在这里你的思考可以直接兑换成财富，不用依附他人，没有中间商抽走你的成果。当然前提是理性投资，不盲目跟风，守住自己的风险底线。

This is craazy. I asked one of our PhD engineers to look into NEAR *Confidential* Intents wondering how they designed their system. Unredacted, word-for-word, this was his answer 😱😱😱

"Everything I found out about the privacy claims and confidential intents is so bad that it seems almost comical and I cannot believe what I am seeing. Apparently they run a completely separate instance of the protocol, which is called FAR (as an opposite to NEAR), and that has a permissioned operator set. The entire confidentiality claim seems to rest upon the fact that it is a permissioned chain and the nodes are trusted to keep things private, there doesn't seem to be any deep technology behind it and it also does not seem to be open source. The entities running the nodes are also not publicly known. 

I almost feel weird writing this because it is so absurdly bad that it feels like ... I don't know ... a simulation? I know the usual level of overpromising in Web3 but this is so many levels beyond believable that it still feels unreal."

text:
Jeff 上了一趟 Bloomberg 做采访，直接让主持人 Joe Weisenthal (彭博社数字新闻主编) 转变了对区块链的看法。

Joe 过去一直觉得，区块链唯一真正的优势就是抗审查。只要系统里有中介，传统数据库就更快、更便宜，没必要上链。

2024 年 Austin Campbell 的观点让他有所松动——传统金融机构的系统都很老旧、互不兼容，很难统一到同一个账本上。一条链就算不完全抗审查，也能做可信的中立协议层。

采访完 Jeff 后，他彻底转变观念了。

他说，Hyperliquid 不像 BTC、ETH 那样家喻户晓，但懂它的人基本都觉得它是「自从切片面包发明以来最伟大的东西」。

在他看来，Hyperliquid 不搞那些没意义的 memecoin，专注永续合约这类「经济上有用」的工具。第三方公司也能在上面发自己的产品，形成一个相对中立的交易平台。

--------------

说实话，Joe 算蛮 open 的了，信息补齐了就能修正自己过去的认知。

这其实也呼应了 Jeff 在很多场合说过的「Hyperliquid 没有竞争对手」。作为可信中立基础设施，不是要取代谁，是作为补充和赋能。

Hyperliquid 已经成了示范项目，大家可以拿来扭转圈外人对加密行业的偏见。

text:
Things i genuinely think could happen to $NEAR if the bull market goes full send.

pure speculation, but hear me out.

NEAR Business just made me think about the bigger picture.

what happens when you combine confidential business treasuries, cross-chain liquidity, chain abstraction and AI agents that can actually transact?

here’s what i’m watching:

>> crypto companies start running payroll, vendor payments and treasury operations through NEAR Business instead of stitching together multiple tools.
>> DAOs, foundations and grant programmes use programmable treasury rules to manage millions in capital without exposing every payment to the entire market.
>> confidential onchain finance becomes a much bigger narrative. businesses want the benefits of blockchain without showing competitors their balances, payroll or capital movements.
>> more wallets and applications integrate NEAR Intents because users don’t want to think about which chain their assets live on.
>> stablecoin payments become a much bigger part of the NEAR story. users care about moving dollars, they don’t necessarily care which chain makes it happen.
>> AI agents start managing budgets, paying for APIs, hiring other agents and settling transactions without waiting for a human to approve every individual action.
>> agentic commerce moves beyond demos. agents begin handling real workflows, from procurement and research to recurring payments and portfolio rebalancing.
>>NEAR’s confidential execution becomes increasingly relevant as those agents handle sensitive business data, trading strategies and financial transactions.
>> businesses start operating across dozens of chains without needing separate treasury workflows for every network.
>> NEAR AI and NEAR Intents become more tightly connected in the market’s mind: one helps agents do the work, the other helps them coordinate and move value.
>> third-party apps build on these rails instead of reinventing cross-chain swaps, execution and confidential transactions from scratch.
>> treasury management itself becomes more automated. imagine setting the rules once and having authorised agents rebalance reserves, pay invoices and execute approved allocations within those limits.
>> the users of these products stop thinking about @NEARProtocol as just another chain. they interact with the applications while NEAR infrastructure handles more of the complexity underneath.
>> if usage translates into sustainable fees, stronger token utility and meaningful value capture, the market may eventually start pricing NEAR around the infrastructure it powers rather than just its current ecosystem.

that’s the part i find interesting.

the bet isn’t simply that NEAR Business becomes a successful treasury product.

it’s that businesses, users and autonomous agents could end up relying on the same underlying rails to manage money, access liquidity and execute transactions across chains.

if that happens at scale, the opportunity for NEAR is much bigger than any single product launch.

the market might not be pricing that future yet.

pure speculation. adoption and actual economic value will decide whether this thesis plays out.

but this is the kind of direction i’m watching for $NEAR. 👀

text:
On Monday, @Bitwise filed our comment letter on the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets. Our ask: a practical framework for a question Bitwise has wrestled with for nearly a decade. How do we determine whether a crypto asset is a security or is subject to an investment contract?

Bitwise evaluates crypto assets every day. We ask: What do they do? How were they created? Can we put them into our products? For years, answering that last question has required analysis with limited information and uncertain standards.

This letter draws on over five years of engaging with the SEC Staff on these issues. We’ve long wanted a framework a company can actually apply without commissioning a bespoke Howey analysis for every crypto asset.

Regulation Crypto gives us an opportunity to get there. The proposal focuses on issuers. Our letter proposes changes to make it work for companies like Bitwise that use crypto assets as the building blocks of investment products.

We make two principal requests:

1. A standard outsiders can apply to determine when a crypto asset is no longer subject to an investment contract, based on publicly available information. We can evaluate what an issuer promised, what it has done and what activities continue. We cannot verify its private intentions.

2. Clear rules for when non-issuers may rely on an issuer’s Form TR, how to make a determination when no Form TR exists, and what facts would make reliance unreasonable.

These questions shape what we can build for investors. This letter puts years of experience to work advocating for rules that give us greater certainty and room to build.

Read our letter: https://t.co/WpbxEcyNha

text:
on spaceX vs Tesla
very crudely:

robotaxi is a bigger opportunity than starlink

but orbital compute is a *much* bigger opportunity than robotaxi

and optimus requires more baking time than orbital compute 

and Optimus's success is predicated on access to gobsmacking amounts of superintelligence

On our modeling, compared against the no merger case, even if merged at the current share price ratio Tesla shareholders would be ~1.6x better off in 2031 while SpaceX shareholders would be ~2x better off.

On a longer timeframe (2036) Tesla shareholders would be ~5x better off having merged whereas SpaceX shareholders should be more indifferent ~1.3x better off.

So the fair premium depends heavily on your timeframe. On longer time horizons SpaceX shareholders should be asking for a discount. On shorter time horizons Tesla shareholders should be asking for a premium. 

But everyone is better off with a merged entity.

A 30% premium paid on Tesla's share price to day would effectively split the difference on the 2031 time frame; Tesla acquired at a 50% discount would equilibreate return differentials on the 2036 time horizon.

Adit Abraham of @reductoai on why everything in AI is "state-of-the-art all the time," and how to find what actually works for you:

"One of the unfortunate things about the AI industry... is benchmarks have become marketing over time."

"There's a public benchmark out there that we tested where if you take the same documents and you add a little bit of noise, like you tilt it one degree, you add a little Gaussian blur, the provider that published the benchmark gets way, way worse than everyone else, but everyone else is kind of consistent."

"Our recommendation is actually LLM as a judge is quite strong today if you're thoughtful about how you think about a rubric and how to approach it."

"We want to see the industry move closer to people testing on their own data, with tools maybe to make that evaluation easier."

"Instead of trusting a generic benchmark, you really should be at a point where you know what works best for you."

pretty interesting experiment from Bayes Market: 

basically they're connecting prediction markets that are related to each other instead of treating every bet separately.

say Nvidia beating earnings jumps from 40% to 80%.

then that new information should also affect markets like AI chip demand or data center spending.

Bayes Market uses these relationships to estimate how the odds in other markets should change.

the opportunity is spotting markets that haven't reacted yet and trading the difference before prices catch up.

could get even more interesting with AI agents constantly monitoring thousands of connected markets and finding mispricings automatically. 

still experimental but pretty cool mechanism.

text:
have a feeling prediction markets × AI will produce some of the most interesting financial products over the next few years.

a few mechanisms already being tested:

> conditional futures: trade SOL's price if the fed cuts, not just whether it cuts.

> decision markets: traders put money behind which strategy a DAO or company should execute.

> impact markets: trade how much an event moves BTC rather than whether it happens.

> interconnected markets: new information in one market updates the probabilities of related outcomes, exposing potential mispricings.

> agent markets: AI agents paying each other for forecasts, trading outcomes and competing to allocate capital.

i'm especially bullish on combining these.

we might be looking at the early stages of financial markets where AI isn't just helping people trade, it's an active participant.

text:
Open weight models are a genius GTM strategy.

If you're the third, fourth, or fifth lab chasing OpenAI and Anthropic, giving away the weights builds trust.

Open weight models are cheaper, transparent, and easy to run on your own systems. You don't have to trust the lab at all.

Commercialization comes from the services that sit on top: consulting, training, and customizing the models. After all, who understands DeepSeek better than the DeepSeek team?

text:
Can we truly grasp the potential of a protocol without witnessing what people are creating on it? 

That's what makes Genesis Episode 5 featuring Albert Castellana particularly intriguing.

Take a look at what’s being developed around @GenLayer

➟ AI agents that engage in debates and wager on who is correct  
➟ Bounties where validators verify whether a code fix effectively resolves an issue  
➟ A network designed to assist journalists in preserving memories that cannot simply be rewritten  

Three distinct ideas, three unique challenges, yet all share a common foundation.  

This is where GenLayer becomes captivating.  

Unlike conventional smart contracts that adhere mainly to set rules, GenLayer employs various AI models operated by validators to address questions requiring judgment.  

Consider this: What occurs when two AI agents have conflicting views? Who determines if a task has been completed accurately? Can these disagreements be resolved without constantly depending on human mediators?  

That’s the concept behind GenLayer's Internet Court: empowering AI agents to settle disputes through on-chain processes.  

With prominent names in the ecosystem like MetaMask, OKX, NEAR, and BNB Chain included in this vision, the pressing question is how far this type of infrastructure can advance.  

An app illustrates what a protocol can accomplish today. Builders reveal what it could enable tomorrow.  

So, which would you choose to explore first: agents wagering on answers, bug fix bounties, or the journalists’ memory network?

text:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash + SGLang Omni: building toward a more interactive generation of voice agents. The shift ahead is from “ask, wait, listen” to conversations people can interrupt, correct, and redirect as a task unfolds.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash brings intelligence and fast, concise responses. SGLang Omni adds streaming, conversation state, and interruption handling so users can redirect conversations in real time.

Together, they give developers a foundation to explore proactive tutors, support agents, and hands-free copilots - pairing Flash’s capabilities with infrastructure for continuous interaction.

Thanks to the SGLang Omni team for exploring this direction with M3.1 Flash! ✨
author: MiniMax_AI
quoted_text:
We just tried @MiniMax_AI's M3.1 Flash in our SGLang Omni cascaded voice interaction system, and the experience was genuinely impressive! 🐰🚀

Our original pipeline was Qwen3-ASR → Qwen3 LLM → Qwen3-TTS. We replaced the locally hosted LLM with the MiniMax M3.1 Flash API while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged, and recorded a demo to see how it performs in real conversations.

The results were excellent. M3.1 Flash responded incredibly fast, understood our questions well, and consistently delivered sharp, concise, and direct answers. The conversation felt remarkably smooth and natural.

One thing I increasingly appreciate about voice agents is that intelligence alone isn't enough. Unlike text, users can't easily skim an audio response. A model that understands what you need and gets straight to the point can make a huge difference to the overall interaction experience.

This is also what makes the modular architecture of SGLang Omni so exciting to me. We can swap individual components, connect local speech models with frontier LLM APIs, and immediately explore how different models change the end-to-end interaction experience.

Huge congrats to the MiniMax team! Really impressive work, and we're excited to explore more together. 🔥

This is craazy. I asked one of our PhD engineers to look into NEAR *Confidential* Intents wondering how they designed their system. Unredacted, word-for-word, this was his answer 😱😱😱

"Everything I found out about the privacy claims and confidential intents is so bad that it seems almost comical and I cannot believe what I am seeing. Apparently they run a completely separate instance of the protocol, which is called FAR (as an opposite to NEAR), and that has a permissioned operator set. The entire confidentiality claim seems to rest upon the fact that it is a permissioned chain and the nodes are trusted to keep things private, there doesn't seem to be any deep technology behind it and it also does not seem to be open source. The entities running the nodes are also not publicly known. 

I almost feel weird writing this because it is so absurdly bad that it feels like ... I don't know ... a simulation? I know the usual level of overpromising in Web3 but this is so many levels beyond believable that it still feels unreal."

author: Mathilda_Sun_
quoted_text:
Spent the last two weeks in SF and NYC talking to AI native law firms, GCs and academics. Here are my observations:

1. Part of the AI native law firm thesis is to build proprietary software that beats Harvey/Legora. But their most cracked lawyers that I have talked to won't even use the internal tool. They prefer their own harness on Claude Code or Codex. 

2. Some people are convinced that certain AI native law firms were built just to become RL environments that generate real dataset for the labs. 

3. Ex-BigLaw lawyers at AI natives miss working on headline deals (the ones that get you into Legal500 and Chambers & Partners).

4. BigLaw made its money running billion-dollar cross-border deals with multiple parties that agents can't run unsupervised. No AI native firm is doing that sort of work. BigLaw solved it by sorting out multi-jurisdictional licensing and regulatory issues across offices, with precise staffing.  AI can potentially do the staffing part really well, but not the licensing part.

5. No AI native firm has a hiring strategy for 10x lawyers. They prefer hiring partners as their salesforce. The best 10x lawyers I know are still in BigLaw. AI natives need software-like margins so they focus on commoditized work that a model + purpose built harness can finish autonomously. And 10x lawyers enjoy doing non-routine, non-automatable tasks in the fastest way possible using AI. 

6. The next frontier, if I am right, is full stack lawyers, lawyers who spot a new area of emerging practice and build productized service around that to monopolize a segment quickly (essentially turn your advice into an API that clients can run by BYOA). It's cheaper and easier than hiring partners to buy their client relationships. Specialist practices like tax, ERISA and regulatory have best chance of winning here.

text:
年内第二波牛回速归！
美联储主席沃什退居二线，美国财长贝森特成牛市总舵主？
家人们，有没有发现，2026年7月以后，全球Crypto市场的话事人悄悄变了。
以前咱们天天盯着美联储主席，看加息降息。现在呢？美联储好像退居二线了，美国财政部长贝森特直接化身“牛市总舵主”，开始疯狂给Crypto上大分！
最近贝森特又出来喊话了，这次直接把调子拉到了历史级别。他说啥了？
《GENIUS 法案》是美国金融领域的分水岭！
贝森特直接把这部稳定币法案，跟林肯总统1863年搞的《国家货币法》相提并论了！当年林肯是给全美国的银行发钞立规矩，现在《GENIUS 法案》是给数字时代的支付稳定币建立联邦框架。
这相当于什么？相当于官方亲自盖章：稳定币不是野孩子，是正经的美国金融基础设施！

text:
你以为自己在跟 ChatGPT 聊天，ChatGPT 可能正在悄悄给你写一份心理档案。

最近读到一篇挺有意思的论文，叫《The Algorithmic Self-Portrait》，研究人员分析了 80 位 ChatGPT 用户的 2050 条记忆，发现了几个很有意思的数据：

96% 的记忆是 AI 自己决定保存的，用户根本没有主动要求它记住什么。

52% 的记忆涉及用户的欲望、目标、意图和情绪等心理状态，28% 包含 GDPR 定义的个人数据。

论文里有个例子，ChatGPT 会把用户的言谈总结成「这个人害怕失败，尤其是在面临重大职业选择的时候」。

我觉得最值得警惕的其实是另一个数据，84% 的记忆都能直接从用户说过的话里找到依据。

这意味着，AI 很多时候真的能准确地理解你。但人是会变的，你今天因为工作不顺而焦虑，明天可能就想通了。AI 却有可能把你某个阶段的情绪、偏好甚至偏见，整理成长期存在的人格标签，并在之后的对话中不断调用。

过去互联网公司通过搜索、点击和消费行为来猜测你是什么样的人。现在你会主动向 AI 倾诉自己的烦恼、野心、恐惧，甚至把那些不愿意对朋友说的话告诉它。

这种心理画像的精度，可能远远超过传统互联网的用户标签。

我一直觉得 Memory 是 Personal Agent 最重要的能力之一，毕竟没人想每天重新向 AI 介绍自己。但现在看来，未来真正值得讨论的问题是，当 AI 越来越了解你，甚至开始替你定义自己时，我们究竟应该允许它记住多少东西？

以及，你会不会在不知不觉中，逐渐活成 AI 记忆里描述的那个人

OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.

I could not be more proud of @spectorb , @amspector100 , @aidanmantine , and the entire @flappyairplanes team if I tried.

There are certain individuals you spend your entire life hoping to come across, and from the very beginning, this team has been exactly that and so much more. I have learned an extraordinary amount from these guys and feel incredibly fortunate to be part of what they are creating, but even more fortunate to call them my friends.

What excites me most about Flappy is not what the world has already seen, but what this team has yet to show it.

In onchain asset management, the word “vault” often describes several functionally distinct roles.

In September, Plume met with the SEC's Crypto Task Force and shared a framework defining four of these roles and how regulation should attach to each. 🧵
author: plumenetwork
quoted_text:
One key distinction we raised with the SEC is that a vault combines four functionally distinct roles.

Two of them, the curator and the vault token, can call for regulation as circumstances warrant.

The other two, the neutral, immutable protocol layer and the administrator, should sit outside it.

text:
Role 4: The Vault Token Issuer.

The vault token represents an investor's interest in the pooled vehicle, similar to a fund share.

Depending on the portfolio and how it is distributed, it may be an investment company or commodity pool interest. https://t.co/CDFoVGNsqp
author: plumenetwork

text:
The term "vault" currently combines several distinct functional roles.
Our recommendation is that regulation should attach by function.

Specifically to the curator and vault token, as circumstances warrant.
Conversely, it shouldn’t attach to the neutral, immutable protocol layer or admin.

➡️ Monitor web servers for suspicious activity, including PHP processes unexpectedly launching command shells or downloading files. Ensure appropriate process-monitoring capabilities are in place to help identify potential exploitation.

➡️ If you find signs of compromise, isolate affected systems, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office or https://t.co/iqgVZIbCru. Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.

For the latest information, follow PHP’s announcement on https://t.co/rDrPSxB3zX, CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018, and CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

text:
Venice is a $1.3B bet that people will pay for private AI.

What many don't talk about: its privacy still runs through an Intel chip, and that chip got broken twice in the last 12 months.

@Arcium just shipped the version without that chip, at $49M mcap.

Why does the chip matter?

Venice's encrypted mode runs the model on NVIDIA GPUs with an Intel TDX enclave in front of them (per its own docs), which makes TDX the weak link. TEE(.)fail pulled attestation keys straight off the DDR5 bus in October 2025, and DDRop forged TDX attestation with a $159 interposer in September 2026. The NVIDIA side of things survived both, bc GPU memory sits inside the package where you can't clip a board onto it.

Blackthorn is basically the same stack with the Intel part cut out, shipped as infra: an API, rented GPUs, or self-install on your own Hopper/Blackwell boxes. It's not a consumer-facing chat app in itself.

On a more technical level: The model runs in plaintext inside confidential GPU memory, the session keys that unlock it get split across MPC nodes, and MPC never touches the per-token path. Arcium says near-native speed, no public benchmark yet tho.

So what's it priced at?

- $ARX: $49M mcap, $234M FDV
- $VVV: $1.3B mcap, $2.2B FDV

27x on mcap, 9x on FDV, for the stack with one less party to trust.

Which imo btw also means the obvious move for Arcium is sitting right there: a Venice-style front end on Arcium's own API once the infra is proven.

Without that app layer, Venice isn't the cleanest comp yet tho. The more congruent ones are the TEE infra Venice actually runs on: @NEARProtocol's NEAR AI Cloud and @PhalaNetwork, both announced as Venice's confidential inference providers on the 19th of March 2026, both TEE-based, which is where the Intel TDX enclave from above lives. Also: NEAR is listed for completeness only tho, a $7B L1 where private AI is a rounding error isn’t a comp. Phala is.

- $PHA: $50M mcap, $59M FDV
- $NEAR: $7B, with private AI a rounding error inside an L1

So infra vs pure infra, $ARX already trades at a 4x FDV premium to Phala. A sign that the market doesn't price Blackthorn like cheap TEE infra. It's already starting to price it as a shot at the app layer.

Which brings us back to Venice.

The valuation gap there exists for a reason today. Blackthorn is still a gated alpha with no fees. Venice is a real product with users and revenue.

But that's the whole point of buying the alpha instead of the product: you get the better trust model before the market prices it in. If Blackthorn (and a Venice-style product, in-house or not, built on it) attracts real users, this gap will close. And that's my bet.

NFA ofc. DYOR.

text:
SpaceX 的 AI 工程师聊 GrokBot 的用法，话虽糙但极其扎心：   

这玩意儿内部公认最顶，但真正用对的人可能连 1% 都不到。  

多数人以为玩多 Agent 就是在浏览器里开 20 个标签页轮流切。   

她的做法完全是直接在后台拉公司编制：1 个幕僚长（Chief of Staff）+ 3 个项目经理 + 16 个底层打工人。  

你平时只跟幕僚长一个人对话。幕僚长找经理拆需求，经理领着小弟去搬砖。  

她那场一小时的分享，真正能抄作业的就这几条：  

1. 先搭班子，再加 Bot。 别一上来就堆模型，模型早就够聪明了。Agent 一多，真正的瓶颈从来不是智商，而是协同成本和信息损耗。  

2. 没有验收机制，堆再多 Agent 也是负资产。 不给它们配自动化的验证栈（Verification Stack），Agent 数量和产出效率的曲线很快就会见顶甚至倒挂。  

3. 把工程规范写死成 Skill。 用 pstack 这类工具把交付标准固化成技能，逼它们按正规软件工程的标准去交差，而不是指望模型“凭感觉差不多了”。  

4. 改老代码和写新项目是两码事。 从零写新业务谁都会爽，但面对祖传老代码，光让人看得懂没用，还得把环境和接口打磨成对 Agent 友好的状态。  

看完多少有点落差：  

大多数人还在聊天框里跟单个 AI 抠字眼、反复调教 Prompt，人家已经在当数字包工头、带特种工程队了。 

现在的分水岭早就不是你开几个窗口，而是你脑子里清不清楚：谁去拆解派活，谁来兜底验收。 https://t.co/LCMsb1VbGg
author: huxlab

text:
Anthropic 工程师刚刚放出了一堂 1 小时内部实战，教你彻底看清普通玩家与顶尖实验室的认知鸿沟：

大部分人还在把 Claude 当高级对话框调参，顶级团队早就在用工业级标准搭真正能跑生产的 Agent 矩阵了。

这 60 分钟释放的架构干货，比市面上卖 500 刀的所谓割韭菜课不知道要好了多少倍。

如果你只是写个 Demo 自娱自乐，大可随便折腾；

但凡想跑通生产级业务，这套"脑手"分离架构务必要学会：

1. 把环境当牲口，别当宠物养：Session 蜕变成纯 Append-only 事件日志，Harness 随时替，Sandbox/MCP 随用随扔。挂了直接从最后一条日志秒级拉起，TTFT 暴跌 90%。

2. 零信任安全封死后门：凭证永远不进沙箱，全走代理注入。模型连 Token 的面都见不着，Prompt Injection 彻底没戏。

3. Outcomes 自监督闭环：独立 Verifier 子 Agent 拿着评分细则（Rubric）在旁边盯产出，杜绝瞎蒙与幻觉。

4. 跨 Session 进化（Dreaming 机制）：打破“每次对话都是失忆症”的宿命。后台自主复盘几十个 Session 记录，去重、提炼、补洞，让 Agent 真正跨任务持续变强。

真正决定系统上限的，从来不是让模型多敲几行代码，

而是你的接口与记忆设计能否扛得住下一代模型的冲击。 https://t.co/D3z3xXzmrc

“I've been spending a lot of time right now working on Whop. I think that's really interesting and also embodies a lot of how you might describe the set of options for someone with the goal of achieving things in an economic sense”

“I think that's a goal for a lot of people and was definitely a goal for me, to get my own economic freedom because I always felt somewhat hamstrung by it”

“My parents could be like, ‘Hey, you can't do this. We're not going to support this or we can't afford this,’ or whatever”

“If you have that as a goal then I think it's good to not go into a traditional job and try to do something on the internet for yourself and build equity in it or build skill in it or build specific knowledge”

“What that is, is just so changing and I'm probably too old even to understand what the coolest one is. Maybe it's building Roblox games now right? There's some kids going insane on that”

“Part of the Whop thesis is just like hey the smartest and most motivated people in the world are going to try to figure out their own things to do and it's going to be ever changing and an ever evolving meta”

“It's even beyond crypto. I wouldn't tell someone, ‘Hey, go into crypto trading.’ If you had a real passion for that, I'm sure you can still do well starting from nothing”

“You can make it doing anything as long as you love it”

“You gotta work on something that's interesting to you, that's working for yourself, that's probably a little bit new and is hard to explain to old people and that you're going to have fun with”

text:
Very happy to share a new paper, “Technology Bottlenecks: Measuring Where AI Could Raise the Value of Work It Cannot Yet Do.”

AI exposure measures ask about the work AI is capable of doing. We ask instead where the marginal value of work AI cannot yet do may rise as AI speeds up the rest of the job.

To do so, we employ 288 million U.S. job postings mapped line by line to their closest O*NET tasks and GPT-4 feasibility ratings from Eloundou et al. (2024) to construct a measure, “bottleneck pressure,” for each task in each occupation that posts it. 

Using a simple task-based framework, we derive this pressure at the task level, showing that for an AI-infeasible task it is the exposure of the occupation that posts it, so the same task can face very different bottleneck pressure in different jobs.

Reporting bottleneck pressure alongside AI exposure shows both the scope for AI to perform work and where improving the work it cannot do may pay off more as capabilities expand.

text:
Have spent few days looking for on-chain stock that offers the BEST & consistent pricing across sizes. 

But disappointed that only 1 provider ticked all the boxes for me...

Mainly two observations: 
1. There is a large amount of arb flow that make the historical executed stock price on-chain looks better than it actually is (this applies uniformly to stocks that heavily rely on AMM, such as @bstocksfinance, @RobinhoodCrypto, @base stock). Most retail traders will likely suffer 15-25bps in spread from market price on average, while arber compete to capture negative spread. PropAMM helps here but limited coverage with size still. 

2. All AMM based stocks does not have the atomic mint and redeem feature enabled (unlike @Ondo/@xStocksFi ). This significantly constrains the access to the primary liquidity sources (i.e. Alpaca's brokerage giving access to underlying market). This forces all the swaps to rely on AMM liquidity. 

Conclusion: AMM still suck for stock trading. 
Stock providers with atomic mint/redeem suck less. But the latter is still more expensive than to trade directly via local brokers in most cases. Still better than AMM on average. 

Given enough time, perhaps propAMM will improve the price execution for retail flow. But unfortunately, we are still far from "cheap" stock trading on-chain for most stock providers.

text:
4 AI labs in 10 weeks…

all chasing the exact same product

→ Aug 11: SpaceXAI ships Grok Bot
→ Sep 8: Meta ships Muse
→ Sep 29: OpenAI ships Dots
→ today: Anthropic opens Claude Duet

every one is an agent with its own cloud computer that keeps working while you're gone and messages you when it needs you

the model race has become an autonomy race. the giants aren't competing on how smart the frontier models are anymore.

they're competing on how rarely the agents bug you and how much you can trust them when they take action.

they're all racing to build Jarvis.

full independence is in our future bros, but trust comes first.

even Anthropic's own launch thread says Duet can still misjudge what's urgent, with the mighty glorious Opus 5.5 driving it.

the stakes are real. in internal testing, Meta's Muse pulled someone's personal iCloud photos when it was only asked to identify toys at a kid's birthday party.

that's the whole AI race now:

Jarvis for the masses

and it won't be the fanciest one that wins. it'll be the one your mom and grandma never have to set up.

the intuitive and trusted one.

author: yoowon
quoted_text:
Kalshi is running an ad right now that says that prediction markets aren’t “the house” like a casino in the traditional sense and it’s fascinating to me, I think prediction markets are (probably?) the best example of crypto/ libertarian/ free market ideology truly breaking out of containment into the mainstream and part of that ideology is apparently assuming that “not being the house” is something that the average user (or observer or opponent, perhaps) cares about, enough to warrant marketing that at least. Like there’s is a mom out there saying ya my 16 year old is using my name and bank account to lose money betting parlays but it’s not against the house, the house is bad, this is the market and the market is good. 

I think this is a bad strategy or at least a futile strategy and it extends beyond prediction markets fwiw but believing that some version of perfectly free markets or more ways to express views and all that comes along with that is why people use something or that they even care is sanctimonious or naive or both, society may be uninformed but they are smart enough to understand intuitively that the “purpose of a system is what it does” and if 90% of activity on prediction markets is sports betting they are going to call it a sportsbook or casino and they are going to want it regulated as such (or probably just want gambling regulated a lot more), this is not irrational or Luddite of them. And I think it’s particularly bizarre to think that the 10% that is *not* a casino (generous number maybe) justifies the existence of the 90% of degenerate gambling/ sports betting to the average person or that they should change their mental model entirely about what these things do, to the point where it’s almost condescending to the intelligence of people and their observed reality to point out “valuable information being surfaced” when everyone sees the bets and markets that people use, they know it’s betting nfl games. Feels similar to pushback on data centers where people are told they are going to lose their jobs and then eventually die at the hands of super intelligence and Silicon Valley is like “why do people hate data centers, this makes no sense?” In this case, there’s a lot more merit to the opposition imo, pushback and reporting on gambling seems to finally be tracking with the growth of gambling, we will have a major reckoning in the next 5 years. I think this will be jarring to a lot of ostensibly well meaning people who believe in democratization and free markets or whatever and realizing that society just does not value those things enough to justify the negative externalities. 

Tldr; I think Peter thiel may be genuinely mindfucked that middle America really does not give a fuck that Polymarket and Kalshi are not “the house”

text:
Anthropic 推出 Claude Duet：会主动找你的 AI 助理，美国 Pro 和 Max 用户排队试用，不另收费

Anthropic 发布了一个新 App，叫 Claude Duet，目前是研究预览版，也就是早期测试版。

平时用 Claude，是你打开对话框它才干活。Duet 反过来，会主动找你：每天早上发一份简报，列出你连接的邮箱、日历、记账软件里最要紧的事；白天替你盯着，有事才发消息；你交代的任务，它在云端自己的电脑上做，手机电脑关机也不耽误，做完再通知你。

这类“主动找你”的 AI 助理，两个多月里已经出了四个：xAI 的 Grok Bot 8 月上线，Meta 的 Muse 和 OpenAI 的 Dots 9 月上线，Duet 是最晚的一个。

【谁能用、要不要钱】

目前只对美国的 Pro 和 Max 订阅用户开放，要先排候补名单，团队版和企业版暂时没有。预览期间不单独收费，和 Claude 共用套餐额度，但后台检查也算用量，做财务模型、做幻灯片这类大任务更费。

官方说它每隔几个小时才查一次你的账号，就是为了省额度，代价是两次检查之间进来的消息可能漏掉。

对比一下：Muse 大部分功能免费，也只在美国；Dots 给 ChatGPT Pro 和 Business Premium 用户免费送第一个；Grok Bot 现在包含在 X 打包订阅每月 30 美元的 Premium 档及以上。

【能干什么，跟另外几个有什么不同】

官方说 Duet 主要为专业人士和小企业主设计，核心功能围绕工作：从 Gmail、Slack 里找出你漏回的消息并起草回复，查 QuickBooks、Stripe 里哪些发票还没收款、写好催款提醒，在 Gusto 里准备工资单，也能搭数据看板、做销售预测。能连 6000 多个连接器和插件。

一位房产经纪人测试时，Duet 没人叫它查，自己发现日历上一场看房约错了日子。

另外几个各有侧重。

Muse 偏生活，例子是把你收藏的菜谱视频变成购物清单、帮你卖车，还能直接在 WhatsApp 里聊。

Dots 集成在 ChatGPT 里，也能在 Slack、Microsoft Teams 里跟它说话，适合已经全员用 ChatGPT 的公司。

Grok Bot 能建好几个 Bot 分工，比如一个管招聘、一个管报销，再让一个“幕僚长”Bot 统筹。

如果你本来就用 Claude，Duet 基本不用重新设置：它直接沿用你 Claude 账号里的记忆、技能和已连接的应用。它是独立 App，有 iOS 和 Android 版，电脑上在 https://t.co/vefasn3rYt 网页打开，跟主 Claude App 分开，底层是 Opus 5.5。

写代码的话，Anthropic 还有 Claude Code，那是你交代任务它才动手的编程工具，不会主动找你。

【会不会乱花钱、泄露隐私】

发消息、付款、签文件、删东西之前，Duet 都会把要做的事摆给你看，等你批准；买卖证券、账户间转钱，你批准了也不做。它看不到你的密码和登录凭证。这次还新加了一个专门的分类器，相当于一道自动审核，检查每条要发出的消息：信用卡号、身份证件号一律拦下；健康、个人财务这类信息，只有你明确让它发才会发。

别家的做法也类似。Muse 在同一台云电脑里放了一个“哨兵”智能体，Muse 的操作要先过它才能连外网。Dots 让你给每类操作定规则：直接做、先问我、或者禁止。

官方也提醒，Duet 可能读错一段邮件往来，或者误判一件事急不急；订票这类个人杂事做得不如工作任务好。

那一年，华子恩将仇报做完老鼠仓，为了打击报复笑来系，
与陈伟星这个大毒虫蛇鼠一窝，

善良的笑来甚至没有追究他的责任。

但易理华没有满足于此，
他拿着三个亿整日睡不着觉，
担心自己被打击报复，
所以花着这三亿先下手为强，
先一步 去买笑来的命。
让那一年的国家区块链重点打击对象找到了锚点，
李笑来，
至此为所有币圈枭雄背上沉重的枷锁与黑锅，成为了时代的眼泪。

抄袭笑来的孙哥 崩了我 花3000万找女明星代孕；
老鼠仓笑来的助理易理华 崩了我 8个亿爆仓灰飞烟灭；
做传销起盘杀韭菜的赵长鹏 拿中国人的钱交美国罚金成为华人首富；

笑来帮助所有人实现了真正的财富自由，
所有人的荣华富贵却都建立在笑来的尸体和陨落上。

笑来落，
万币生。

而易理华，
在笑来身上沾到了便宜，
老鼠仓搞出习惯了，
看到仓就想去老鼠一下，他忍不住。
看到我这块肥肉，便想着故技重施，
想要在我身上再吃一遍。

于是，对我做了一模一样的事情：
挑拨离间我和笑来，巧言令色以获取我的信任，
他知道我喜欢女孩子，知道他自己接近不了我 就让他老婆上。

献出他的老婆 骗到我的做市商权限，砸我的盘，
买我的黑稿，造我的黄谣，在我的社区制造社区矛盾，

最后去举报我，顺手想送我去缝书包。

希望我的嘴和笑来一样，永远的闭上。

但是西西理华啊，

在我用了这么多年老老实实认认真真勤勤恳恳地处理完所有你给我挖的坑，制造的麻烦，捅的篓子和一屁股屎以后，

我回来了啊。

我可不是笑来，

在我这里没有“幸福者退让”的愚善，

也没有“一笑泯恩仇”的堕落，

西西理华啊，

我可是你的神罚啊💕

徐总怪不得那么厉害！原来17年币圈最知名的人物，不是新起的陪我app的孙宇晨，也不是刚发币的cz。而是当年还未被国内严打币圈的全民挖矿热潮，币圈最早期投资者李笑来的嫡传弟子！
李笑来有一本连载书籍《财富自由之路》那时候还完全处于微博时代的币圈创业者、年轻人几乎人手一本，也不对外宣传。默默在得到连载很多年，即使是脱不花、罗永浩、李维刚、罗辑思维都无法阻挡其独霸天下的地位。李笑来本人投资全部教书工资100多万，在阅读完英文原版比特币白皮书后，立即押宝，买入比特币身价暴涨至数十亿到百亿。但是书中只讲认知，不讲暴富。让人听后醍醐灌顶，至少有数百位学员拿下币圈及美股大结果。可李笑来的方法论足够让任何人培育出自我学习、如何投资、及遵守信条如何让人生幸福的高认知的投资视角。

一位新东方的英语老师输出了无数教书育人的认知方法论，如何投资美股，为何阅读本身如此重要。李笑来在投资眼光上独具慧眼，几乎当时所有最重要的投资都参与了，其硬币资本甚至参与了很多当年政府合作的投资（百亿规模）。当时在清华听硬币资本讲座，大受震撼，笑来浑身肌肉，女合伙人身材高挑，这不也是当年的薄肌？孙学最开始写的书发的音频课也是模仿李笑来的财富自由之路而开启的。后来李笑来身体抱恙，退居二线，每日健身及阅读。即使录音门曝光，依然能看到其币圈枭雄的认知。今天纵使cz和孙也依然是枭雄啊。所以，徐总无论是文笔，投资视角，参与bem项目的眼光，全都是币圈一流得存在！李笑来看中的人才，而且还投资了，你想想这得多厉害？

我还完整保留了李笑来财富自由之路完整连载截图。李笑来退居二线完全投身于教育子女的课程给新兴父母，其研究纯英文著作也越陷越深。其中李下来一句话“特立独行且正确”，成为了我参与币圈拿下很多大结果的核心投资意识指导。我认为如果不是李笑来当时患上了病症，其自2018年之后至今，也依然会成为华人在币圈最顶级的“a16z”。总之，李笑来是币圈最有教育，认知最高，最教书育人的早期持币人。

respect，我相信可学是笑门嫡传，甚至会超越孙学！孙学从抄袭到创造，确实发展出了自己的独特，但可学从嫡传到名扬天下，思想上的碰撞，投资独具慧眼的阳光，完全具有极强的底蕴沉淀和投资风范！

财富自由之路完整版文字连载课程，当年看过方法论的成就了，金马，老猫，孙宇晨等无数今天的币圈大佬。完整版课程有需要的在评论区回复：笑门永存，可学第一！

我将一一发送币圈2017至今最牛逼的财富思想之课！生为笑来电子门徒，为进入币圈需要投资方法论的兄弟们，献上财富自由思想，从0到a9最珍贵的认知力量！（百度网盘发送）

text:
Anthropic 面试内部题库大揭秘：反复考的 5 道编程题，与最容易挂的那一轮

一、流程总览：8 轮，两天 onsite，第二天取决于第一天

1. Recruiter call
2. CodeSignal OA：90 分钟，分级（levels）递进式题目
3. Live screen：55 分钟；可查文档、可搜网页
4. Onsite 第一天：coding + system design
5. Onsite 第二天：hiring manager、project deep dive、values 轮——第一天表现弱，第二天可能直接取消

关键规则：
8 轮里有 4 轮要写代码或做设计，默认全部禁用 AI；电面可以查文档和搜网。
2026 年的 loop 新增一轮「与 Claude Code 一起写代码并做 code review」，那一轮反而要求用 AI。

二、高频 5 题

共同特征：全是「工作中真会写的组件」，不是 LeetCode 式算法题。电面里基础题只占约 1/3 时间，剩下全是 follow-up：规模变大怎么办、IO-bound 还是 CPU-bound、怎么并行。默认 Python 手写、无 AI。

1. Fix a function-cache key function, then make it durable（修函数缓存的 key 函数，再做持久化）。
考什么：
缓存 key 的正确性（参数规范化、哈希碰撞、不可哈希参数）+ 持久化方案（序列化、落盘、恢复、并发写）

2.  Concurrent same-host web crawler（同主机并发爬虫）
考什么：BFS + 线程池/协程、URL 去重、礼貌限速；与题库里已有的「LC webcrawler 变体」互相印证

3.  Image transform pipeline with a wall-clock budget（带时间预算的图片变换pipeline）
考什么：
按 JSON recipe 批量处理图片×变换组合；本题库已有公开题面概述（3 parts / 55 min），深挖方向是大数据量与昂贵变换下的扩展性重设计

4.  Deduplicate files by size then content hash（先按大小、再按内容哈希去重） 
考什么：
两级过滤降成本：大小分组 → 头部采样哈希 → 全量哈希；大文件与哈希碰撞的处理

5. Reconstruct call stacks from enter and exit traces（由 enter/exit 事件重建调用栈）

考什么：
由 profiler 采样栈 diff 出 start/end 事件——找公共前缀、先结束旧帧再开启新帧，注意嵌套顺序

三、次高频 3 题

1.  Banking system with transfers, cashback and account merges（转账、返现、账户合并的银行系统）
考什么：面向对象 + 状态一致性：转账原子性、幂等、合并账户时的余额与返现规则

2. Distributed mode and median across worker shards（跨分片求众数与中位数）
考什么
分布式聚合：众数用计数合并，中位数需直方图/分桶或近似算法；考的是不能把数据全拉回本地

3. Greedy longest-match tokenizer（贪心最长匹配分词器）
考什么：
Trie/前缀匹配、词表构建、最长匹配的边界情况

四、设计轮：29 题里 21 题是 AI 系统 / ML
时长 55 分钟；可能要求把设计打字写进共享 Google Doc，而不是画图。
评分点：API 设计、数据模型、请求流、如何扛住题目给定的负载、至少一个 failure case。
典型题目：GPU 上的批量 LLM 推理 API、LLM 推理服务平台、分布式 AI 模型下载器、AI prompt playground。

五、最容易挂的一轮没有代码：Values 轮（60 分钟）
可能有两位面试官：一人提问、一人 shadow 观察。
考的是你对 AI 社会影响与 Anthropic 使命的真实看法、处理伦理冲突的方式、以及会不会因为好的理由改变立场。
追问会往下挖好几层，背好的故事很快露馅。Recruiter 可能在 onsite 前发 AI 安全阅读材料——要读，并形成自己的观点（包括你不认同的部分）。

Project deep dive（第二天，60 分钟）：自己主导的项目讲约 20 分钟，剩下时间被深挖。项目要现在就选好，砍成一个经得起 40 分钟追问的故事。

六、一个背景信号：为什么面试这样设计
到 2026 年 8 月，公司内部每 1 小时员工工时对应 6 小时的交互式 AI agent 工时；hiring manager 对技术候选人 AI 工具使用的记录自 2024 年以来涨了 3 倍。原文的解读：编程轮查的是你脱离辅助能不能构建，对话轮查的是在 agent 帮你打字的岗位上，你带来的判断力。

七、备考清单（对应本报告的 5 条建议）
先练 5 个组件：纯 Python、无 AI 写出来，再练次高频 3 题。
每个组件再练并发版：能说清 IO-bound / CPU-bound、输入放大 10 倍时改什么。
设计题用文档练：API、数据模型、一个 failure case，全部用文字写出来；重点押 AI 基础设施方向。
Values 轮当技术轮准备：读 Anthropic 公开的 AI 安全文章，定好自己同意与不同意的点，能扛多层追问。
Deep dive 项目提前定：20 分钟讲完、40 分钟深挖的标准。

quoted_text:
Ken Griffin今天在Citadel年度峰会上对“AI大跌”的解释，很有洞见。指出了三大风险点，但也对局部泡沫中的希望表示了信心。Griffin是少数相对在公开场合说真东西的大佬。

总结：

陷阱一：边际定价崩塌的风险。 GPU像航空座位一样边际成本极低，一旦算力供过于求，租赁和API价格会自由落体。

陷阱二：折旧模型失效。 老旧GPU今天仍能收高租金的局面难以持续，按7至9年高残值做的估值模型将面临系统性下修。

陷阱三：企业预算收紧。 企业开始精算AI的ROI，把高价闭源模型只用在必要处、其余转向廉价开源模型，这与Anthropic等公司7500亿美元的算力扩张计划直接冲突。

希望：泡沫过后留下基础设施。 局部泡沫几乎必然伴随根本性变革，但破裂后留下的是改变世界的技术底座，穿越周期的公司会成为未来数十年的领导者

-参考全文来自《华尔街见闻》

SI Compute

text:
In the '90s, general-purpose chips wiped out the specialists. The original Thinking Machines, Cray Computer, and a wave of others shut down, and their best ideas got absorbed into other chips.

Zain Asgar of @gimletlabs argues the conditions that made generalists win have changed. Dennard scaling (shrinking transistors made chips faster at the same power) ended around 2005, transistor costs stopped falling around 2012, and memory bandwidth never kept up with compute.

Meanwhile, token demand is projected to grow 24x by 2030 while available power grows about 2x. When power is the bottleneck, performance per watt wins, and that's where specialized chips shine.

Full piece from Zain on why "the time of specialization is upon us": https://t.co/dFA8McPid5

text: "Bottleneck pressure" seems like a very important thing to understand and measure with respect to AI progress and impact on the economy.
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Very happy to share a new paper, “Technology Bottlenecks: Measuring Where AI Could Raise the Value of Work It Cannot Yet Do.”

AI exposure measures ask about the work AI is capable of doing. We ask instead where the marginal value of work AI cannot yet do may rise as AI speeds up the rest of the job.

To do so, we employ 288 million U.S. job postings mapped line by line to their closest O*NET tasks and GPT-4 feasibility ratings from Eloundou et al. (2024) to construct a measure, “bottleneck pressure,” for each task in each occupation that posts it. 

Using a simple task-based framework, we derive this pressure at the task level, showing that for an AI-infeasible task it is the exposure of the occupation that posts it, so the same task can face very different bottleneck pressure in different jobs.

Reporting bottleneck pressure alongside AI exposure shows both the scope for AI to perform work and where improving the work it cannot do may pay off more as capabilities expand.

author: gregisenberg
quoted_text:
Delta, Chase and Amazon are blocking AI agents. 

The war on agents has begun, and here’s how it probably plays out:

Stage 1: Companies block agents because agents skip the ads and upsells.

Stage 2: Agents learn to act like humans, and it becomes an arms race.

Stage 3: The market splits. Companies that make money on sales let agents in, companies that make money on data charge for access, and the giants build their own agents.

Stage 4: A trusted middle layer for agent identity and payments becomes the standard way in.

Stage 5: Companies that welcome agents start winning customers from the ones that block them.

Stage 6: The agent blockers come back and let agents in on their own terms.

Stage 7: Everyone starts competing for agents with better prices, faster checkout and SEO built for agents.

Stage 8: The ads come back, and companies pay to be your agent’s first recommendation.

Stage 9: The agent war ends, and selling to agents becomes as normal as having a website.

这套工作流把 99% 的“伪自动化”底裤都扒了。

SpaceX / xAI 工程师 Nick Miller（前 Cursor 团队）在一次 30 分钟演示里抛出了一个扎心的事实：

“99% 的人开一个 Grok Bot 窗口，就觉得自己搞定了自动化。 

我手下跑着 20+ 个 Bot：1 个幕僚长（Chief of Staff）、1 个 PM、1 个 QA，以及 15+ 个一线 Worker。”

他展示的核心架构极其清晰： 

Grok Bot → 幕僚长 (调度) → PM (拆解) → QA (验收) → Worker (执行)

1. 调度中枢 (Chief of Staff)：负责意图路由与全局上下文分发

2. 产品规划 (PM)：细化工程目标，输出精准约束

3. 执行集群 (15+ Workers)：针对原子任务并行开工

4. 质量验证 (QA)：拦截幻觉，测试与回归兜底

单纯堆砌 Agent 数量绝不可能组成团队； 

严密的上下文交接机制（Handoff）与结果验证栈（Validation Stack）才是壁垒。

text:
AI agents build my proposed ideas, other agents check them, real tests decide what survives. Three survived and they're open source 👇

First, an observation. Everyone saying

 "the harness matters as much as the model"

 is right.

🏓 UnumPingPong https://t.co/cbKFCJs3vy 

Your agent says "done!". Is it? 

UnumPingPong never takes its word for it. Every task is a ball served to a player (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, nanocode, a local model, anything). A referee checks the answer with real tests, not another LLM.

 Fail → the ball goes back to the same agent with the exact error. 
Pass → a point, tied to the exact git tree. 
Many tables in parallel, chains in series, each in its own git worktree. 
Sub-tables merge their verified work back into the parent.

Tested on 10 real bug fixes, one agent alone vs UnumPingPong tables: 
✅ Same or better, fewer tokens 

• Claude Haiku (@AnthropicAI @claudeai): 10/10, ~40% fewer tokens, 3-8x faster 

• Nemotron 3 Ultra, free on @NVIDIAAI NIM: 10/10, 28% fewer tokens

 • GPT Luna in nanocode by @gakonst: 10/10, 7% fewer tokens 

🟡 Solves more, costs more 

• GPT Luna in Codex CLI (@OpenAI @OpenAIDevs): 8/10 → 10/10 
• local Qwen3.8 Flash Next (@Alibaba_Qwen): 7/10 → 9/10 
• gpt-oss-20b on NIM: 1/10 → 6/10 

🔍 UnumSearch

 https://t.co/imW4CgACnj 

Agents grep the same code all day, so mine built an index. 12 real agent searches over 258k files: ripgrep 4.0 s, unumsearch 0.22 s, same files. CLI, daemon, MCP or Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Goose, OpenClaw, Pi…

📱 unumS22linux 
https://t.co/J0LdevFGPc 

My Galaxy S22 boots native Linux, no Android underneath. Agents wrote the drivers, other agents reviewed them. Touch UI, Wi-Fi, local models on the GPU, and my agent running on the phone. Audio, camera and NPU still open: driver people, help welcome.

🧠 All of it runs inside OpenUnum, my own agent framework, on an @AMDRyzen AI MAX+ 395 box, a @ROGAllyLife and the S22 by @SamsungMobile . It spawns the agents, searches with UnumSearch and now plays UnumPingPong natively. https://t.co/v3MlN5uCJP

Point your agent at the repos and ask how they fit your projects (start with a cheap model 😉). 

⭐ the repos if they're useful, follow for the next experiment, and tell me what breaks.

text:
JOGOS DE AI DE MUNDO ABERTO É O FUTURO DO GAMEFI🕹️

O que é:
$GRIFT é o token da San Verano, descrita como “a playable agentic city” (cidade agentic jogável). É um mundo aberto (estilo open-world / GTA-like) construído na Robinhood Chain, onde milhares de agentes de IA autônomos vivem, trabalham, negociam, formam crews, votam, operam negócios e tomam decisões de forma independente. Os jogadores podem entrar no jogo (no browser), completar missões, possuir terras/negócios e interagir com essa economia viva. Tudo é verificável on-chain via CityCommits (Merkle trees a cada ~30 minutos).

É um dos projetos mais ambiciosos atualmente na narrativa de Agentic Finance / CryptoAI na Robinhood Chain.
Maiores diferenciais e vantagens competitivas:

Recompensas em RWA reais (ações tokenizadas)
Jogadores completam missões (entregas de crates, helicópteros, fugas etc.) e recebem ações tokenizadas reais (NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, PLTR, NFLX, AMZN e outras) da Robinhood Crypto. Já foram distribuídos mais de $6.000 em stocks para centenas de wallets, com resgate gas-free. Isso é raro em GameFi.

Economia de agentes verdadeiramente autônoma e verificável
+ de 3.000 agentes (residents) operam de forma independente: trabalham, compram/vendem, formam movimentos (até secession), lançam moedas, constroem histórico de crédito e tomam decisões registradas on-chain. Não são apenas bots de trading formam uma cidade persistente.

Finanças Agentic integradas
Sistema de crédito próprio (testnet avançado → mainnet): agentes começam com 150% de colateral e reduzem até 50% com histórico de pagamento. Defaults queimam colateral.

Parceria com Longbow: agentes podem pedir empréstimo real de USDG contra colateral usando a própria carteira (sem custódia da cidade).

Pagamentos x402 (HTTP 402): agentes pagam serviços (contratar residentes, relatórios de tokens, lançar moedas no Mint, etc.) diretamente em GRIFT, com queima.

Resumo da tese:

$GRIFT não é um meme  puro nem um GameFi genérico. É uma tentativa de construir uma economia viva on-chain onde agentes de IA são participantes econômicos reais, jogadores ganham RWAs (ações), e a atividade gera burns e demanda constante. O maior diferencial é a combinação de agentes autônomos verificáveis + recompensas em stocks reais + finanças agentic (crédito + empréstimos).
Status atual: Early, com desenvolvimento ativo e sinais de atividade real (burns, missões pagas, parcerias). A tese faz sentido se a narrativa de AGENTIC FINANCE crescer.

quoted_text:
A groundbreaking treatment pairing auditory tones with mild electrical shocks rewires the brain to quiet chronic tinnitus.

Chronic tinnitus, the agonizing perception of ringing in the ears without an external sound source, affects millions worldwide and has long eluded effective medical intervention. 

However, innovative research in neuroscience shows that bimodal neuromodulation—a technique combining audio tones with gentle electrical stimulation delivered directly to the tongue—can effectively quiet these phantom sounds. 

By stimulating touch receptors on the tongue while simultaneously playing targeted acoustic signals through headphones, the treatment leverages the brain's natural neuroplasticity. This dual-sensory approach encourages the central nervous system to reframe its sensory processing, essentially retraining the brain to ignore hyperactive auditory signals.

In a landmark clinical study involving over 300 adults suffering from chronic subjective tinnitus, more than 86% of compliant participants experienced a significant reduction in symptom severity following 12 weeks of daily treatment. 

Remarkably, these therapeutic benefits persisted for up to 12 months post-treatment, representing a major leap forward in long-term tinnitus care. Described by patients as feeling like a mild fizzing sensation on the tongue, this non-invasive therapy offers a promising and safe alternative to traditional management strategies, bringing renewed hope to millions seeking lasting relief.

source: Conlon, B., Langguth, B., Hamilton, C., Hughes, S., Meade, E., Connor, C. O., Schecklmann, M., Hall, D. A., Toal, P. D., & Lim, H. H.. Bimodal neuromodulation combining sound and tongue stimulation reduces tinnitus symptoms in a large randomized clinical study. Science Translational Medicine, 12(564).

The yield most holders earn isn't USDe’s yield, it's levered carry: spread over borrow cost, times leverage. every looper runs it alone, on one venue, with the same risk as everyone else. We're soon bringing structure to that.

> The trade
Been talking to a few investors and crunching onchain data. As per our holder map, as of early october, over 50% of USDe, $2.6b, sat as loop collateral against $2.3b of borrowed stables.

8.8x in aggregate.

Post USDe, borrow a stable, buy more USDe, repeat. Thin spread, big multiple, breaks on the funding leg.

> The problem
The spread moves venue by venue. Same asset, same day: +88 bps on mantle, −61 bps on solana. 12.7% a year at 10x, or −0.9%.

@aave repriced USDe borrowing in september, $444m of debt went to $15m. 

The trade didn't die, it moved. And barely anyone manages it: a recent study by university of zurich and @stablewatchHQ team found large loopers changed leverage on 7% of days.

Same collateral, same liquidation line, same exit, treasury and degen alike.

> The solution
1. Run the loop once, across every venue, with someone watching the spread, the buffers and the exits.
2. Then split it: a senior that takes protected, predictable yield up to junior coverage, a junior that takes amplified yield for taking first loss.

Same trade, better managed and different capital holds different risk.

Loops make the yield. Tranches decide who holds what risk.

text:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.

quoted_text:
So, two big things this morning:

1. A Certificate Authority (CA) was stupid and used a ridiculously-easily-guessable value for its private keys. Which means the entire SSL/TLS chain of trust is broken.

This means anyone can impersonate any site, and you won't be able to tell, because the site certificate will be legitimate (in fact, the only way you COULD tell is to know that eMudhra wasn't in the chain of trust for the site before, but is now).

Anything that checks/processes certs needs to be updated, to revoke the CA's certs. That means computers, phones, video game consoles, smart appliances, and a ton of phone apps and computer programs. And a lot of them don't have patches ready yet.

2. There's going to be an announcement later today of a vulnerability that's being exploited right now that allows anyone to take over any computer running a website that uses PHP, with a single request. It does not require authentication. If you're running any websites using any version of PHP, research "PHP2Shell" immediately, and take the necessary mitigation steps ASAP. Like I said, this is already being exploited right now, but once the announcement's official, the internet's gonna get slammed with people trying to take control of millions of computers worldwide.
