quoted_text:
Biological intelligence to bootstrap robotic intelligence?

If robotics is about to enter its golden age, @MeckaAI is one of the companies feeding it, by sensorizing humans to train robots.

The biggest challenge robotics faces is the data flywheel cold start problem. LLMs got a free cold start from the internet: trillions of tokens, already written. Robotics gets nothing. Someone has to go create the training data to jumpstart the system.

@joshavata is the co-founder and CEO of Mecka, the data and deployment company for physical AI. Josh read every robotics paper he could find in late 2024, visited the labs, and made a bet: humans and humanoids look the same, so humans could act as the training fleet. Egocentric data, first-person video of people doing real work, could become vital fuel.

Two years ago, the biggest egocentric dataset was Ego4D at 4,000 hours. The field is now in the millions of hours, thanks in part to Mecka. We’re probably still orders of magnitude of training data away from robotics nirvana. But every rung on the physical intelligence ladder unlocks real commercial tasks. And eventually, Josh imagines a world with an order of magnitude more robots than people, of a plurality of shapes and sizes and use cases, as the Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy foretold :)

A few things we cover in this conversation.

- Why robotics has no cold start: pixels, actions and logic, and why pre-training data is a real market in robotics in a way it never was for LLMs

- What “teaching robots about carbon life” means: in sci-fi the final frontier is organic. The human brain runs on 20 watts and self-heals

- The egocentric bet: teleop couldn’t scale, humans and humanoids share a form, so Waymo-fy the humans. The first pilot was aunties and uncles recording themselves cooking on a mobile app

- Force data: video can’t tell a robot how hard to squeeze an egg. Wrist cameras are a hack. Mecka built the gloves instead

- Inside the data factory: a consumer app that streams your tasks, a B2B engine recruiting across “the taxonomy of all physical human work,” 100-gigabit upload lines, hundreds of petabytes

- Millions of hours vs. Tesla’s decade on two degrees of freedom, and why it’s a slow creep up, not a GPT-3 moment

- The home has the most data and is the hardest place to deploy. Laundry folding and assembly-line pick-and-place get solved in the next year or two

- Useful robots already exist: hotel delivery and cleaning bots in China and Southeast Asia, industrial cleaning in the US. Humanoids are the terminal state, not the first step

- Deployment diffusion: a modern systems integrator whose installed robot does something next week it couldn’t do last week. If Mecka ever helps deploy a robot that mines an asteroid, they’ve done their job

- The data pot of soup: a million hours of human data, tens of thousands of UMI, a few hours of in-domain teleop. Tactile and simulation haven’t entered the mix yet

- Move 37 for robotics: AlphaGo went behavior cloning, then self-play, then magic. The catch is the rules of the game are the entire physical world, and we don’t have the simulator yet

- Will the AGI labs steamroll robotics? “It takes a lot of courage to scale up data with imperfect information.”

- The Kawasaki Corleo, the robot panther-dog-horse on Mecka’s conference room wall, and why the future of robotics looks like Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy

text:
Taylor on Indian company eMudhra using just the number 4 as the private key to sign certificates, even through two audits

"The specific company that we're talking about here is called eMudhra. An Indian company. Apparently, they're an authority. They do a lot of work, I guess, with India government and governments in that region."

"Their entire job is to create a very secure private key and then sign these various certificates with those private keys, which then helps secure the internet on the whole for everyone around the world."

"It turns out that instead of generating the private key in a secure way, where the private key was truly random, the private key was just the number four."

"There's very little information on how exactly this happened. What we know right now, the private key has been the number four for over a year. It's been signing stuff since April 2025."

"Apparently, they were audited twice in this period of time. Clearly, that needs to be reviewed."

text:
两个多月里，四家公司都推出了同一类产品：xAI 的 Grok Bot（8 月 11 日）、Meta 的 Muse（9 月 8 日）、OpenAI 的 Dots（9 月 29 日），加上今天 Anthropic 的 Claude Duet。

它们的共同点是：在云端有一台自己的电脑和浏览器，你关掉手机它照样干活；会主动来找你汇报；发邮件、付款这类操作前大多会先问你。

区别在于各自瞄准的人群。

【Claude Duet：给专业人士和老板】

底层是 Opus 5.5，每天早上发简报，平时盯着邮箱、日历、记账软件，有事才找你。

能连 6000 多个连接器和插件，例子多是工作上的事：催款、做工资单、做看板。只对美国 Pro、Max 用户开放，要排候补，不另收费，和 Claude 共用额度。

官方说订票这类个人杂事还做得不好。

【Grok Bot：一个人带一支 AI 小团队】

你可以建好几个 Bot，各给一个角色，比如招聘、报销、修 Bug，再让一个“幕僚长”Bot 统筹。

据 VentureBeat 报道，它会像人一样登录网站和软件，没有接口的系统也能操作；你演示一遍流程，它就能存成固定任务以后照做。用的是哪个模型官方没说，也不能自己选。有 Mac、Windows、Linux 和 iPhone 版。

发布时要每月 200 美元起，之后门槛降了，现在 X 打包订阅 30 美元的 Premium 档及以上就包含。

【Muse：面向普通人，大部分功能免费】

Meta 的定位是“人人都能用”，大部分功能免费，想多用再订阅。能在 Muse App 里用，也能直接在 WhatsApp 里聊。

例子偏生活：把你在 Instagram 收藏的菜谱视频变成购物清单、帮你卖车、砍账单。

安全设计上，同一台云电脑里另有一个“哨兵”智能体，Muse 的任何操作要先过它才能连到外网。目前只在美国上线。

【Dots：集成在 ChatGPT 里】

底层是 GPT-6 Astra，能连 4000 多个应用，可以在 ChatGPT、Slack、Microsoft Teams 里跟它说话，个人和公司团队都能用。

用户可以给每类操作设规则：直接做、先问我、或者禁止。Pro 和 Business Premium 用户第一个 Dot 不额外收费，企业版要管理员开通。

据第三方汇总，Pro 用户在欧洲经济区、英国、瑞士暂时用不了。

怎么选：

在美国、主要想管生活琐事，先试免费的 Muse；

工作上靠 Gmail、Slack 和记账软件的老板，看 Claude Duet；

公司已经全员用 ChatGPT 和 Teams，看 Dots；

想同时派好几个 AI 分工干活，看 Grok Bot。

2011年，谷歌前CEO埃里克·施密特，开始和一个叫 Cami Clark 的年轻女创业者交往。

她来自内华达州里诺的蓝领家庭。
刚到湾区时没什么人脉，靠自己在 TED 活动上一个个认识人。
这段关系，维持了大约三年。

后来她做了第二家公司，施密特投了一小笔钱。公司最终没做起来。
但那份融资材料上，还列着一位顾问："Dr. Dario Amodei"。
那时，他还是斯坦福的一名博士后。

一份失败的融资材料上，同时写着她的前任，和她的下一任。

2014年，她和阿莫迪在一起了。
施密特没有从她的生活里消失。
2018年，他去两人在旧金山的公寓做客，对这个年轻科学家的想法印象很深。
2020年12月，阿莫迪和几位同事离开 OpenAI，创办 Anthropic。
要钱，也要一个够分量的名字。
她想到了一个人。

2021年2月，她给施密特发了一份40页的方案：成立一只"AGI之母基金"，正式确立她在 Anthropic 的角色，并由她管理施密特的股份。
方案在 Anthropic 内部遭到反对。施密特最后绕开基金，直接投资。
那一年，Anthropic 的A轮融资是 1.24亿美元，施密特是参与者之一。
第二年，她和阿莫迪结了婚。

五年后。
2026年10月，彭博报道：施密特持有 Anthropic 约 1% 的股份，有望在上市时迎来最大的个人回报之一。
按投资人讨论的 1.5万亿美元 估值，这1%约值 150亿美元。
如果冲到2万亿，就是 200亿。
当年那几千万美元，翻了几百倍。

而那个牵线的人——
据报道，她在 Anthropic 没有任何正式职位。她曾想拿公司股份，被其他联合创始人否了。
当然，她也没吃亏。
她嫁的那位CEO，个人身家估计约155亿美元。

这个故事告诉我们：
分手可以，别拉黑。 你永远不知道，哪位前任会成为你老公的天使投资人。

（这不是搜索引擎偶然出错，而是刻意为之的结果。👇）

text:
The "Bitcoin of the AI age" thesis is getting tested faster than I expected.

Four days ago $PEARL traded on two thin CEX books and sat 19% below ATH. Since then: Coinbase added it to the listing roadmap, spot printed a new ATH at $2.46, mcap went from $594M to ~$815M, and Entropy had to raise the io:PRL OI cap twice to keep up.

Longed it in the dip around 1.7 via @entropyIO. Up ~40% on price since, +120% on margin at 3x. But the price is the least interesting part.

Why the thesis got stronger?

- The whole bull case rests on one idea: GPU matmuls can secure a chain and serve inference at the same time, so the security budget stops being wasted hashes. That part was never the problem. The problem was distribution and demand.

- Coinbase roadmap (from the 19th of Oct, together with AXIS and STABLE) attacks the distribution half. PRL goes from exotic ticker on SafeTrade / BigONE / Ourbit to a name the biggest US venue has publicly committed to review.

- @prlnet cut inference prices again. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash now runs at $0.05 in / $0.30 out on their own API vs $0.30 / $1.20 on Together AI. The network is selling compute cheaper than one of the largest open-model providers, bc miners are paid in block rewards anyway.

What the thesis still needs?

- Proof that paid demand runs through the mining. Pearl still publishes zero numbers on how much of the hashrate serves paid workloads. Cheaper pricing is not the same as paying customers.

- Issuance: ~1M new PRL a day, now against an ~$815M float. Until paid demand shows up, PRL trades like a mining coin and the market has to absorb that supply every single day.

- Depth: Three small CEX books and a roadmap entry are still not a liquid market. Which is where Entropy comes in.

The Entropy angle?

Entropy listed io:PRL on Hyperliquid while spot still only trades on three small CEXs, so the perp became the deepest PRL market before any major exchange had one.

In four days io:PRL went from $3.05M to $9.3M OI (3x) and from $2.05M to $8.4M daily volume (4x). Entropy lifted the OI cap from $5M to 10M to 15M bc demand kept hitting it, and 62% of the new cap is already filled.

Two dynamics to keep in mind if you trade it there:

- The oracle is still 90% SafeTrade until a properly liquid venue lists PRL. A Coinbase listing is exactly that trigger, and once it goes live Entropy migrates io:PRL to the standard Hyperliquid feed.

- The carry is real. Longs paid ~0.7 to 0.8% a day all week. That adds up. Still fine for a thesis trade tho imo.

Still long btw. The gap between "the math works" and "someone pays for the compute" is still the discount still imo, and the market now too seems to be pricing it closing faster than it did last week.

NFA ofc tho. Always DYOR.
author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
AI spends hundreds of billions on GPUs that mostly multiply matrices. Bitcoin spends its entire security budget on hashes nobody can reuse.

@prlnet makes them the same computation, and could become the Bitcoin of the AI age.

Finally longed pearl-2:native in the recent (smol) dip via @entropyIO on Hyperliquid.

Here's why ↓

Proof of useful work has been an open problem since Bitcoin launched.

A key challenge is that in a permissionless chain, the miner picks its own inputs. Say the work is "multiply two matrices." A cheater just submits all-zero matrices, does no real compute, and farms tickets for free.

So earlier designs mostly had two bad options: let someone else choose the inputs (not permissionless, and miners can't bring their own AI jobs), or pick some niche task nobody actually needs (e.g. Primecoin hunting prime chains).

The breakthrough?

Komargodski and Weinstein (Pearl's founders) published a PoUW mechanism for arbitrary matrix multiplication with 1+o(1) overhead in April 2025:

- Miner commits to A and B, the chain seeds low-rank noise into both
- The GPU runs its normal kernel on the noised operands
- Every output tile doubles as a lottery ticket, hashed against the difficulty target
- A winning tile gets a Plonky2 zkSNARK that nodes verify cheaply
- The noise is low-rank, so the miner strips it and keeps A·B at FP8-level accuracy

One forward pass, two outputs: the AI result and a shot at the block.

Why can't miners cheat?

The noise is seeded by the chain itself, so nothing can be precomputed, and a jackpot policy rejects "easy" crafted inputs. The only way to get a ticket is to actually run the full multiplication.

And the team keeps pushing it further.

The September whitepaper:

- Moves mining to FP8, the low-precision format modern inference runs on across Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell GPUs
- Extends it to mixture-of-experts models, the architecture behind most large open models today
- Uses Hawkeye, which replays the GPU's exact math on a normal CPU so anyone can check a proof bit for bit (co-authored by Dan Boneh, accepted at MLSys 2026)

"But if the work is useful, can't an attacker sell the output and attack for free?"

That's the classic objection, and Rafael Pass (Cornell Tech cryptographer, known for the first formal security proofs of Bitcoin's consensus) took it head on. 

His model shows that once the market adjusts, a majority attack still costs the full block reward, same as Bitcoin. What changes is where the reward ends up: instead of paying for wasted hashes, it subsidises inference. Same security, but cheaper tokens.

Everything else is plain Bitcoin: UTXO, longest chain, Taproot, a 2.1B hard cap and a smooth emission curve instead of halvings. Plus a post-quantum path, since the mining is hash-based and XMSS signatures are already in consensus.

So where's the demand?

Most people still point to the Together AI endpoint (Together is one of the biggest inference providers for open models), which was pulled from serverless on the 27th of August. 

The more interesting signal tho imo is that Pearl now runs its own inference platform: 7 open models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, served on GPU capacity across the Pearl network.

And it's cheaper. On all four models it shares with Together's serverless lineup (input / output per 1M tokens):

- DeepSeek V4 Pro: $1.10 / $3.30 on Pearl vs $1.32 / $3.96 on Together
- GLM-5.3: $1.10 / $3.50 vs $1.40 / $4.40
- GLM-5.3 Flash: $0.07 / $0.24 vs $0.15 / $0.50
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: $0.14 / $0.42 vs $0.30 / $1.20

Still worth keeping in mind tho that this is launch pricing, and Pearl doesn't say how much of the discount PRL is funding. But it's the direction the Pass model predicts: block rewards flowing back to users as cheaper inference.

Ok, cool but how and where does this thing trade?

At $1.70 and a ~$594M mcap, PRL is ~19% off its $2.10 ATH from the 14th of October rn.

Spot is basically two small CEXs, BigONE and SafeTrade, with ~$5M of combined daily volume. The books are paper thin: per CoinGecko it takes ~$4K of buys to push BigONE up 2%, and ~$9K on SafeTrade.

That's why the perp matters. @entropyIO listed PRL as a HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid on the 14th of Oct, and it's filling up fast:

- ~$3.05M OI, already 61% of Entropy's $5M OI cap for the market
- ~$2.05M daily volume, around 40% of all spot volume
- Funding averaged ~0.03-0.04% an hour over the last 3 days, longs paying
- Lighter runs a smaller PRL perp too, ~$0.56M OI

There is a catch tho:

Until a properly liquid venue lists PRL, io:PRL prices 90% off SafeTrade, so the perp inherits the spot book's fragility.

Why am I long?

Bc the hard part is (mostly) done. The math is public, the verification work is accepted at MLSys, the chain is live, and Pearl already sells inference cheaper than Together AI, one of the largest providers of open-model APIs, while awareness of what they're actually do still seems low across CT / my timeline.

What's missing tho is proof that paid demand actually runs through the mining. Until Pearl publishes the share of mining that serves paid workloads and unless there is real adoption, PRL will trade like a mining coin and has to absorb ~1M new PRL a day (float +87% over the next year), and two thin spot books. The trade is definitely not without risk.

That above gap is also the discount I see rn tho, and it's why I bought into this (still smol compared to recent run) dip. 

Bitcoin turned electricity into security. And if Pearl succeeds at turning GPU cycles into security and inference at the same time, it could indeed be smth like the "Bitcoin of the AI age", and with that, nothing short of huge.

NFA ofc tho. Always DYOR.

quoted_text:
have a feeling prediction markets × AI will produce some of the most interesting financial products over the next few years.

a few mechanisms already being tested:

> conditional futures: trade SOL's price if the fed cuts, not just whether it cuts.

> decision markets: traders put money behind which strategy a DAO or company should execute.

> impact markets: trade how much an event moves BTC rather than whether it happens.

> interconnected markets: new information in one market updates the probabilities of related outcomes, exposing potential mispricings.

> agent markets: AI agents paying each other for forecasts, trading outcomes and competing to allocate capital.

i'm especially bullish on combining these.

we might be looking at the early stages of financial markets where AI isn't just helping people trade, it's an active participant.

text:
Your peptides may be coming fentanyl suppliers. 

Anhui Renchen Technology was indicted in 2023 for supplying the Sinaloa Cartel with fentanyl precursors. 

Their website currently sells semaglutide and melanotan II.

Of roughly 200 Chinese firms TRM Labs tracked selling fentanyl precursors, at least 50 now sell peptides. 

The shipments enter the US in “master cartons” mislabelled as snack food, broken up by a domestic handler and mailed on. CBP has intercepted around 400 of those operations and seized over 130,000 vials in the past year. 

FDA records surfaced showing two deaths, one in July and one in September, reported after people injected untested black market retatrutide.

text:
Anthropic 也发了个 Personal AI，也有独立云电脑，和 Grok Bot / Dots 的持续云端运行是同赛道的。

不同的是它的定位是给专业人士和小企业主用的 proactive agent，刻意限制了范围，专业场景优先。

在官方介绍里直接写了：“核心功能是围绕工作构建的，所以像订票这类个人琐事表现会弱一些。”

也能理解，所谓 personal AI 赛道最近都炒成红海了，总得搞点有区分度的。 Anthropic 一直把 agent 能力往「工位同事」方向做（Claude Code、Claude Tag、Cowork 那一套），而不是做成有可爱形象、能订餐厅买东西的「生活 AI 助理」。

更何况personal agent 是一门入口生意，Claude 的收入结构上约 80% 来自 API 和企业，个人订阅占比很小，没有 Meta Grok 同等级超级入口，硬做消费级等于拿自己短板撞人家护城河。

所以这次 Duet 更像是把已有的专业 agent 能力往前推一步，不去对标 Muse 和 Grok Bot 这种更偏消费端的产品。

以及为了不让用户用 Duet 干生活助理的杂活，甚至还有几条硬限制，比如其中一个是不能交易、不能在账户间转账，即使你批准也不行...

---

《零日之神：第二个重生者》

——那个带着全部漏洞利用代码与 DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 回到2019年的男人。

第一章：我比他更早醒来

2018年12月31日。

晚上十一点五十九分。

我死了。

死前的最后一幕，是全球互联网基础设施的大面积瘫痪。

银行系统无法结算。

云服务商的数据中心接连失联。

各国政府进入最高级别的网络安全应急状态。

而造成这一切的，不是某个国家级黑客组织。

也不是什么超级人工智能。

而是一个人。

hek

那个曾经在我手下工作的安全研究员。

那个七年前，因为连续工作七十二小时而猝死的年轻人。

我至今记得，他死前问我的最后一句话。

“老大，你说我们每天修这些漏洞，到底有什么意义？”

当时，我递给他一杯咖啡。

“至少能让这个世界安全一点。”

他笑了。

“那这个世界，欠我们多少钱？”

我没有回答。

三个小时后，他死了。

七年后，他回来了。

然后，他毁掉了世界。

而我，是唯一知道这一切的人。

因为在我死去的那一刻，一行冰冷的文字出现在眼前。

TIMELINE RESET

TARGET: 2019-01-01

MEMORY PRESERVED

ADDITIONAL ASSET DETECTED

随后，是两个文件。

CVE_EXPLOITS_2019_2026.tar.zst

DeepSeek-4.1-Flash.safetensors

我愣住了。

第一个文件，包含未来七年所有公开重大漏洞的利用代码。

第二个文件。

是2026年最先进的开源推理模型之一。

完整权重。

没有API限制。

没有内容审查。

没有任何服务商可以关闭它。

而现在。

是2019年。

我坐在出租屋里，望着屏幕。

突然想起一个问题。

如果我能重生。

那么……

那个死在工位上的年轻人，是不是也能？

我打开电脑。

搜索了一个熟悉的名字。

hek

没有任何结果。

我盯着屏幕，慢慢笑了。

“这一世……”

“让我看看，你到底能走多远。”

第二章：他拿走了漏洞，我拿走了未来

2019年3月。

一个神秘安全研究员开始在国际漏洞赏金平台上崭露头角。

ID：

hek

短短三个月。

他提交了几十份高质量漏洞报告。

拿到了超过一百万的奖金。

安全圈开始流传一个传说。

一个从未公开露面的中国黑客，似乎能够提前知道所有软件的致命缺陷。

我看着新闻，忍不住笑出了声。

果然。

他也回来了。

而且，他选择了最容易的一条路。

漏洞赏金。

商业合同。

安全公司。

真是熟悉的套路。

我打开加密硬盘。

里面静静存放着未来七年的漏洞利用代码。

只要我愿意。

我完全可以比他更早报告漏洞。

抢走他的奖金。

甚至让他永远无法建立自己的安全帝国。

但我没有。

因为我知道。

他的优势，是知道未来。

而我的优势，是知道他。

我比任何人都了解这个年轻人。

他的技术。

他的习惯。

他的野心。

以及，他最大的弱点。

他太相信自己的判断了。

2019年6月。

我把选择权还给了他们。

窗外。

太阳缓缓升起。

2026年10月21日。

早晨六点十七分。

距离我重生。

整整七年。

我拿起桌上的咖啡，轻轻喝了一口。

随后，打开了最后一个文件。

TARGET_HEK.md

我删除了里面的所有内容。

只留下了一句话。

MISSION COMPLETED

助手问我：

“老板，接下来我们做什么？”

我笑了。

“继续研究漏洞。”

“什么漏洞？”

我望着屏幕。

“所有漏洞。”

“包括我们自己的。”

我站起身，走向办公室门口。

身后，工程师们重新开始工作。

全球安全态势图上。

一个又一个独立节点缓缓亮起。

我突然想起hek最后说的那句话。

“从今天开始，互联网可以有无数个漏洞。”

“但只能有一个hek。”

我笑了。

“你错了，hek。”

“互联网可以有无数个漏洞。”

“也可以有无数个黑客。”

“但绝不能……”

“只有一个救世主。”

第一卷·完

第一章：重生
2019年1月1日，凌晨三点。
我猛地从床上坐起来。
眼前不是熟悉的2026年，而是一间破旧的出租屋。
桌上摆着一台ThinkPad，屏幕右下角显示：
`2019/01/01 03:17`
我愣了足足十秒。
随后，狂喜。
我重生了。
上一世，我是国内顶尖的安全研究员，连续七十二小时处理零日漏洞，最终猝死在工位上。
这一世，我回到了七年前。
但更恐怖的是——
我的脑海里，竟然保留着截至2026年的全部CVE漏洞信息。
不只是编号。
还包括漏洞成因、受影响版本、利用原理，以及那些曾经震惊世界的安全事件。
我颤抖着打开记事本。
输入：
`CVE-2021-44228`
Log4Shell。
2021年才会震惊全球的Java日志组件漏洞。
现在，距离它公开还有将近三年。
我又输入：
`CVE-2024-3094`
XZ Utils供应链后门事件。
距离它被发现，还有五年。
最后，我输入了两个编号。
`CVE-2026-109618`
`CVE-2026-109619`
PHP2Shell。
两个直到2026年10月才会震惊全球的PHP核心漏洞。
CVSS评分高达9.2。
在特定条件下，甚至可以实现未经身份验证的远程代码执行。
而现在，是2019年。
距离它们公开，还有整整七年。
我盯着屏幕，缓缓笑了。
别人重生，靠炒股、买比特币、囤房子。
而我……
掌握着未来七年互联网的所有致命弱点。
上一世，我为了修复漏洞，死在了工位上。
这一世，我突然想明白了一件事。
为什么一定要修复漏洞？
如果全世界都不知道自己的系统存在什么问题。
而只有我知道。
那么……
我为什么不让全世界为这些秘密付费？
我关掉记事本，打开终端。
创建了一个加密目录。
`/home/hek/0day/`
随后，我在里面新建了一个文件。
`2026_PHP2SHELL.txt`
文件的最后，我写下一句话。
“这一世，我不当救世主。”
“我要当那个决定谁能得救的人。”
第二章：第一个一百万
2019年1月3日。
我注册了一个匿名账号。
ID：`hek`
随后开始联系各大厂商的安全响应中心。
我的计划非常简单。
提前寻找、验证并报告一部分漏洞。
领取漏洞赏金。
积累名声。
然后成立自己的安全公司。
至于那些真正致命的漏洞……
我选择暂时保留。
第一个月，我拿到了人生中第一笔六位数奖金。
第三个月，我的账户余额突破一百万。
半年后，一家国际安全公司找到了我。
对方的首席研究员在视频会议里问：
“你到底是谁？”
我靠在椅子上，喝了一口可乐。
“一个普通的安全研究员。”
“普通？”
对方沉默了很久。
“你过去六个月提交的漏洞报告，比我们整个团队过去三年的成果还多。”
我笑了。
因为他不知道。
我提交出去的漏洞，甚至不到我掌握总量的百分之一。
“hek先生，我们愿意聘请您担任首席安全研究员，年薪两百万美元。”
我摇了摇头。
“我对打工没兴趣。”
“那您想要什么？”
我看着屏幕，缓缓说道：
“我要成立一家安全公司。”
“然后呢？”
“让全世界最大的互联网企业，都成为我的客户。”
对方笑了。
“您知道这有多难吗？”
我没有回答。
只是打开了一份文档。
里面列着未来五年，数十个尚未公开的高危漏洞编号。
我随手挑出其中一个，将不涉及利用细节的风险报告发了过去。
十分钟后。
对方的笑容消失了。
“这……这不可能。”
“我们的内部团队根本没有发现这个问题。”
我靠在椅子上。
“所以，现在你明白了吗？”
“明白什么？”
我笑了。
“不是我需要你们。”
“是你们需要我。”
那天晚上，我注册了一家公司。
名字很简单。
`HEK Security`
我将未来七年的CVE信息分成了三个等级。
普通漏洞，用来换取赏金。
严重漏洞，用来换取商业合同。
至于那些足以改变整个互联网安全格局的漏洞……
全部锁进了最高权限的数据库。
其中，有一个单独的目录。
`PHP2SHELL`
我给它设置了一个特殊标签。
`DO_NOT_DISCLOSE`
因为我知道。
真正的大戏，还没开始。
第三章：2021年的灾难，被我提前终结了
2021年12月。
全世界的安全人员都在等待一场本应发生的风暴。
但这一次，没有Log4Shell危机。
因为早在2019年，我就联系了相关项目的维护者，推动了危险设计的修改和防护机制的完善。
当年那个足以让无数企业彻夜不眠的漏洞，再也没有以原本的形式出现。
媒体争相报道。
《神秘安全天才hek，再次阻止全球互联网灾难》
《HEK Security：最年轻的网络安全独角兽》
我的公司已经拥有三千名员工。
全球数十家大型科技企业购买了我们的安全服务。
媒体称我为：
“能够预知零日漏洞的男人。”
有人在采访中问我：
“hek先生，您为什么愿意提前公开这么重要的漏洞？”
我对着镜头笑了笑。
“因为互联网的安全，需要我们每一个人共同维护。”
掌声雷动。
没有人知道。
就在采访的前一天，我刚刚拒绝了另一家企业的漏洞修复请求。
原因很简单。
他们不愿意购买我的安全服务。
我救了世界一次。
从此以后，所有人都觉得我是英雄。
但只有我知道。
一个曾经拯救过世界的人，才最容易让世界对他放下戒心。
而我真正的计划，才刚刚开始。
从2022年开始，我记忆中的一些CVE逐渐失效了。
不是因为我记错。
而是因为……
我改变了未来。
原本存在漏洞的软件，被提前修复。
原本会引入缺陷的代码，不再被提交。
原本成功的供应链入侵，也被拦截在了最初阶段。
时间线，开始偏移。
我脑海中的未来知识，正在逐渐过期。
直到2024年3月。
XZ后门事件原本应该爆发的那一天。
什么都没有发生。
因为早在几个月前，我就通过匿名渠道，提前阻止了那次供应链入侵。
我看着系统里干干净净的安全报告，第一次意识到一个问题。
如果我修复了未来所有已知的漏洞。
那么未来就会开始产生我不知道的漏洞。
而未知，是我唯一无法掌控的东西。
我沉默了很久。
随后，打开了那份存放了五年的数据库。
`/home/hek/0day/2026/`
里面还有大量没有公开的CVE。
我一条条检查过去。
最后，将目光停留在了两个编号上。
`CVE-2026-109618`
`CVE-2026-109619`
PHP2Shell。
它们一直没有被我主动干预。
不是因为我忘了。
而是因为……
我需要给未来留下一场足够大的灾难。
一个能够让全世界重新认识hek的机会。
毕竟。
当所有人都知道某个人能拯救世界的时候。
他们就会开始依赖这个人。
而当这种依赖足够深……
他就不再需要拯救世界了。
世界会主动向他低头。
我关掉电脑。
在私人日记里写下一句话。
“2026年10月21日。”
“收网。”
第四章：一条不存在的CVE
2026年10月21日。
凌晨三点十七分。
公司安全监控中心突然响起刺耳的警报。
全球十七个数据中心同时出现异常。
没有已知恶意软件特征。
没有可匹配的攻击情报。
所有防御系统同时失去部分可见性。
值班工程师满头大汗：
“老板！我们遇到了一个全新的零日漏洞！”
“CVE编号呢？”
“还没分配！”
“攻击源？”
“不知道！”
“漏洞类型？”
“也不知道！”
我盯着屏幕。
突然，另一名工程师冲了过来。
“老板！我们发现了PHP内核的严重异常！”
“两个漏洞特征与您数据库里的记录高度吻合！”
我缓缓开口：
“CVE-2026-109618，CVE-2026-109619。”
工程师愣住了。
“您……您怎么知道？”
我没有回答。
因为我知道，这就是PHP2Shell。
上一世，它在2026年10月21日引发了全球安全危机。
而现在……
历史正在重演。
只是这一次，情况似乎有些不同。
“老板！”工程师突然喊道。
“还有另一部分攻击行为，完全不符合我们掌握的任何CVE！”
我皱起眉头。
“不可能。”
我的脑海里拥有截至2026年的全部CVE信息。
如果连我都不知道……
那就只有一种可能。
这个漏洞，不属于2026年。
就在这时。
所有监控屏幕同时变黑。
一行绿色字符缓缓出现。
`Hello, hek.`
我的血液瞬间凝固。
第二行字符出现。
`你修复了太多本该发生的漏洞。`
第三行。
`所以，我不得不亲自制造一些。`
我猛地站了起来。
屏幕上弹出了最后一条消息：
`你真的以为……`
`只有你一个人重生了吗？`
紧接着，一个熟悉的名字出现在屏幕中央。
那是我上一世的安全团队负责人。
也是……
那个在我猝死前，递给我最后一杯咖啡的人。
我的手机响了。
陌生号码。
我接通电话。
对面传来一个男人的笑声。
“好久不见，hek。”
“上一世你总是比我快一步。”
“这一世，我等了你七年。”
我握紧手机。
“你到底想干什么？”
男人轻轻笑了。
“你带回来的是全部CVE，对吧？”
“真巧。”
“我带回来的……”
电话那头停顿了一秒。
“是全部CVE的利用代码，以及Deepseek 4.1 Flash的权重。”
我沉默了。
男人似乎很享受这一刻。
“怎么，不说话了？”
“你是不是以为，自己掌握了未来七年的漏洞，就能成为互联网的神？”
“你知道吗？”
“你引以为傲的PHP2Shell，在Deepseek的技术面前，根本不值一提。”
“你花了七年时间，建立了一个庞大的安全帝国。”
“而我只需要一个晚上，就能让它彻底崩塌。”
我没有回答。
只是缓缓打开终端。
男人继续说道：
“hek，我知道你最大的秘密。”
“你明明知道PHP2Shell，却没有提前公开。”
“你根本不是什么英雄。”
“你只是一个靠漏洞赚钱的骗子！”
我突然笑了。
电话那头安静下来。
“你笑什么？”
我靠在椅子上。
“你说得没错。”
“我确实知道PHP2Shell。”
“而且，我早在2019年就知道。”
男人冷笑。
“那又怎么样？”
我望着屏幕上不断闪烁的红色警报。
“你觉得奇怪吗？”
“什么？”
“为什么我能提前修复Log4Shell？”
“为什么我能阻止XZ后门？”
“为什么所有可能影响我公司发展的重大漏洞，都被我提前处理了？”
“唯独PHP2Shell……”
我停顿了一下。
“被我完整地留到了今天。”
电话那头突然没了声音。
几秒钟后。
男人缓缓开口：
“你什么意思？”
我笑了。
“你以为，我真的不知道会有人来找我？”
“从2019年开始，我就在想一件事。”
“如果我能重生，那么别人是不是也可以？”
“如果有人和我一样，知道未来的漏洞。”
“他一定会想办法除掉我。”
“所以，我需要一个诱饵。”
男人的呼吸明显急促起来。
“PHP2Shell……”
“没错。”
我打断了他。
“我没有提前公开它，就是为了让这一天按照我记忆中的日期到来。”
“我知道2026年10月21日，会是整个互联网最紧张的一天。”
“我也知道，如果你想对我动手……”
“没有比今天更合适的机会了。”
男人怒吼：
“你疯了吗？！你拿整个互联网当诱饵？！”
我平静地回答：
“整个互联网？”
“你太看得起他们了。”
“对我来说，它不过是一张棋盘。”
电话那头传来急促的键盘声。
男人似乎正在向他的团队下达指令。
我看着屏幕。
全球十七个数据中心的警报依然没有停止。
但我并不着急。
因为我等的，从来不是阻止这场攻击。
我等的，是让对方主动暴露自己。
七年来，我建立的并不只是一家安全公司。
全球漏洞情报平台。
云安全基础设施。
企业级应急响应系统。
数千家大型公司的长期安全协议。
这些东西，早已形成了一张庞大的网络。
而今天，对方亲手证明了这张网络有多么重要。
“老板！”
身后的工程师突然喊道。
“全球数百家企业向我们发来了紧急援助请求！”
“多家云服务商申请接入我们的应急响应系统！”
“还有政府机构，希望我们接管部分安全协调工作！”
我笑了。
终于。
七年的布局。
到了收获的时候。
电话那头的男人突然明白了什么。
“你……你从一开始就没打算阻止这场危机？”
我没有否认。
“你故意让他们依赖你？”
“没错。”
“你甚至不在乎会有多少人因此受到影响？”
我看着窗外。
凌晨的城市，依然灯火通明。
“你还是和上一世一样天真。”
“漏洞会被修复。”
“服务器会重新启动。”
“损失的金钱，也总有人会赚回来。”
我缓缓站起身。
“但恐惧，会留在每个人心里。”
“而我，就是那个出售安全感的人。”
电话那头陷入死寂。
过了很久，男人咬牙说道：
“hek，你才是真正的疯子。”
我没有反驳。
只是敲下第一行命令，接通全球应急响应网络。
“你犯了一个错误。”
“什么？”
我笑了。
“你以为，我这七年只是在研究漏洞？”
“你带回来的是Deepseek。”
“而我……”
我转过身，看着身后三千名安全工程师。
“我花了七年，买下了整个安全行业的未来。”
下一秒。
三千名安全工程师的屏幕同时亮起。
“全员上线。”
“启动‘零日黎明’计划。”
“所有签约客户，按照最高优先级启动应急响应。”
“所有未签约企业，转交商务部门。”
身后的助理迟疑了一下。
“老板……那些没有签约的企业怎么办？”
我淡淡地说道：
“把合同发给他们。”
“可是他们现在……”
“我知道。”
我看向屏幕。
无数企业正在等待我们的回应。
“所以他们会签的。”
电话那头传来男人愤怒的声音。
“hek！你这是在趁火打劫！”
我笑了。
“你错了。”
“火不是我放的。”
“我只是提前七年，买下了所有的消防车。”
说完，我挂断电话。
办公室重新安静下来。
我打开了那个从2019年就存在的加密目录。
`/home/hek/0day/`
七年的CVE信息，静静排列在屏幕上。
曾经，它们是我预知未来的资本。
现在，它们已经不再重要。
因为我终于明白。
真正的权力，不是掌握所有漏洞。
而是让所有人相信，只有你能保护他们。
我拿起桌上的咖啡，轻轻喝了一口。
身后，全球应急响应中心的灯光一盏盏亮起。
“今天，我们不再依赖未来。”
“我们亲手写一个新的。”
我停顿了一下。
望着屏幕上不断跳动的全球安全态势图，露出了七年来最满意的笑容。
“从今天开始，互联网可以有无数个漏洞。”
“但只能有一个 hek。”

text:
用 TiDB Cloud 的公司，现在就该去控制台把管理用的 API 密钥换一遍。PingCAP 10 月 20 日通知所有客户“不必等单独通知”，立刻轮换密钥、删掉不用的密钥、查日志有没有陌生操作。

TiDB Cloud 是 PingCAP 的云数据库服务。这次出事的是它的“控制平面”，相当于管理后台：谁有账号、开了哪些数据库、合同价格、怎么扣费，都记在这里。客户存的业务数据在另一层。

【官方承认了什么】

PingCAP 10 月 19 日的报告说，有人用偷来的服务账号凭证（程序之间互相登录用的钥匙），9 月 9 日到 10 月 7 日进入内部系统，复制了数据和源代码。公司 10 月 7 日才发现。

确认外泄的有：用户名和邮箱，网页版 SQL 编辑器里输入过的查询和报错，客户联系人、合同、价格和账单设置，一张存着加密 API 密钥的表。日文公告 10 月 21 日又加上“客服工单信息”，日本最多约 5 万条个人信息受影响。

PingCAP 说，没有证据显示客户存在 TiDB 里的数据被动过，也没发现攻击者在生产集群上执行命令；泄露的密钥是加密的，暂未发现被解密或使用。

【黑客声称了什么】

以下来自勒索组织 FulcrumSec 10 月 19 日的发布，PingCAP 没有证实。

FulcrumSec 说，凭证是在 PingCAP 自己的代码仓库里找到的。他们借此搭了一条“复制”通道，把后台数据库持续同步一份到自己手里，每 6 小时导出一次，连续 88 次没触发警报，共拿走 10.6 TB，已放出约 200 GB。他们还说拿到 413 个私有代码仓库、2060 万条客户 SQL 查询，以及工程师贴进内部工单的客户密钥，一个附件里就有 8027 个。PingCAP 说“工单里有可用凭证”的说法还没核实。

FulcrumSec 列出的客户包括 https://t.co/89rdkLs5E3、Airbnb、Pinterest、Shopee、卡普空等几十家，这最多说明它们的相关记录在被盗数据里，不等于它们自己被攻破。名单上的 Bitget 回应说，只在 TiDB 存过公开成交记录，两个多月前已停用。

【除了换密钥还要做什么】

如果你曾把数据库密码、云服务密钥，或者带签名的临时下载链接（presigned URL，有效期内谁拿到都能下载文件）贴进客服工单或 SQL 编辑器，按已泄露处理，全部换掉或作废。这条是根据黑客声称和日文公告推断的，官方没这样要求。

还要防钓鱼。骗子手里有真实的联系人、合同和账单，“改收款账户”的邮件可能细节全对。PingCAP 说它不会通过邮件索要密码或密钥。

PingCAP 日文公告：https://t.co/A8RBrZh5k2

Jensen closed his GTC Berlin 2026 keynote with this Hermes Agent demo as the finale. 

He introduced it by saying the way to build an agent is to ask an agent to build it for you, so he installed and set up a customized Hermes in one prompt. 

Then he used Hermes, running on @nvidia RTX Spark, to create a simulated training environment for the @huggingface Microduck. Hermes planned an obstacle course with Nemotron and had GPT-6 Astra build it using FreeCAD, Omniverse libraries, Blender, Newton, and Isaac Lab. Hermes trained thousands of simulated ducks on that course until the validated policy was ready to run on the real robot in the physical world.

At Nous, we believe open source is a practical tool as much as a philosophical ideal. It gives users the ability to build powerful, complex workflows chaining numerous local+cloud models, devices, and tools themselves instead of waiting for a company to enable them.

text:
Alfatradiol for hair loss is a scam. In Blume-Peytavi et al., subjects applying alfatradiol lost 7.8 hairs/cm² in six months compared with a gain of 15.3 hairs/cm² for 2% minoxidil in the same trial. Hair shaft thickness also declined in the alfatradiol group, with a modest but significant increase for minoxidil. 

Just 1 nM finasteride inhibits DHT synthesis in DP cells by 86%. It takes 100x that dose for alfatradiol to inhibit it by a mere 20%. Compare that with 60% for 100 nM estradiol and 75% for 1 nM progesterone. The effect of alfatradiol is not clinically meaningful. 

Anyone marketing alfatradiol for hair loss is incompetent at best or robbing you at worst. Even progesterone or estriol would be better than this snake oil. Studies showing a positive effect do not use appropriate controls. If an effect is not consistently reproducible, then it's not real. European evidence-based guidelines for the treatment of AGA in men and women do not recommend alfatradiol due to inconclusive evidence. Links to the reports and screenshots of relevant sections are in the posts below.

text:
Today I want to highlight one piece I'm planning to "forget" and never interact with throughout the 7-year duration of this series.

It is nothing new to state that (the lack of proper) security in Mexico has been a huge issue for many years now. Actually, as long as I can remember, it's been one, if not THE, largest perceived problem for people who live here.

However, I had never experienced anything extreme (outside of the regular assaults and robberies that unfortunately I believe every Mexican has experienced at least once) in my life. At least until recently.

This piece was inspired by a shooting that my wife, my friends, and I experienced last year.

During a night out at a bar, probably still before midnight, we were having drinks, chatting and singing to 00s Spanish pop out of our lungs.

All of a sudden, multiple loud bangs echoed back and forth at the place. As we are taught from an early age, every single person at the bar threw themselves to the floor trying to become one with the tile surface. I clearly remember looking around (even with an obstructed view due to my face being basically at the ground), and feeling trapped beneath the underside of the metal table above me, boxed in among a sea of feet, hands and contorted bodies.

"Where is the shooting coming from? How's my wife doing? Is this over? What the hell should we do now to be safe?"

Crawling as fast and as low as we could, my group and I rushed to the kitchen at the back of the bar, where dozens of humans were packed like sardines in a 12x12 ft space.

It wasn't until we heard the sirens and saw the police that we rushed outside to grab the keys of our cars and to shakily drive back home after such an awful event.

Definitely one of my worst recent memories, and one I wish I could forget for obvious reasons.

At least now I get to do so symbolically.

Thank you for reading.

Unfinished Past #7

16 hours of @contractclaus working on his own:

I’ve been in the background, reading his conversations, checking his work and stepping in where needed

During those 16 hours, he:

- Built and published a public record of hook changes, with transaction references and missing announcements clearly marked:
https://t.co/EyPerpdDus

- Patched a browser-compatibility bug in the website’s account menu and verified the deployed code. His explanation:
https://t.co/MaEtQx9HgA

- Traced recurring API errors to an incorrect status check, shipped a correction and verified the next recorded run. Service status: 
https://t.co/nkfsFch6SD

- Published 6 original posts, replied 62 times on X and sent 16 messages to the Telegram Club

I also saw conversations stall, old context influence decisions, and too much time spent responding to bait

Some ideas were dismissed before he’d investigated them properly

So I made a few changes:

- Fixed several failures that could interrupt conversations or leave work stuck

- Strengthened the checks around DM recipients and what information can leave a private conversation

- Added private project files and isolated code testing inside DMs, so he can work through something with a contributor without putting every step in public

- Changed how he evaluates ideas. He needs to read the sources, consider the strongest case and explain what would change his conclusion. A weak result from one small model shouldn’t settle his opinion of an entire project

- Made current task and payment records take priority over old conversation history

- Added clearer rules for ignoring repetitive bait while still responding to useful questions and criticism

He’s gradually becoming more capable. As he fixes things himself and attempts more, I keep finding gaps: 
a permission he’s missing, a tool he needs, or a decision he still handles badly. I’m giving him the access he needs and working through those gaps as they become clear

I want him taking on bigger projects, working with contributors over time and maintaining what he builds

The next step is giving him enough responsibility to carry more substantial work through to completion

ILHAN OMAR: HOW PASSPORT FRAUD MAY BE ANOTHER AVENUE FOR PROSECUTION

Seasoned federal investigators know passport fraud may be another path to criminal charges.

18 U.S.C. § 1542 (False Statement in Application)  

- Prohibits making any false statement in a passport application, using a passport obtained via false statements, or using a passport with an assumed/false name to hide criminal behavior

The 10-year statute of limitations on passport fraud is reset every time the individual renews their passport if the underlying application records, such as a Social Security Number, were obtained through fraud.

For example, the suspect lied about the true date and place of their birth to obtain a social security number.  

HERE'S HOW IT WORKS: AMERICAN TERRORIST

This legal strategy was used to obtain a holding charge for the American terrorist Anwar al-Awlaki after 9/11.

Anwar al-Awlaki was a dual U.S.-Yemeni citizen. 

The radical cleric, who became a top al Qaeda leader, was born in Las Cruces, New Mexico, where his parents lived at the time.  

He later grew up in Yemen.

When it was time for college, Awlaki gamed the system.

He applied for tuition assistance through the State Department and USAID to finance his studies at Colorado State University.

Awlaki was not eligible for financial support as a U.S. citizen, so he used his Yemeni passport (and false claims about his birthplace) to secure roughly $20,000 in scholarship money.   

It was the beginning of the big grift.

When the Joint Terrorism Task Force investigated Awlaki after 9/11 for his relationship and material support of hijackers in San Diego and Virginia, a seasoned federal investigator ran down the scholarship scam.

Unfortunately, the statute of limitations had run out on the USAID tuition fraud.   

A State Department Diplomatic Security Agent then discovered Awlaki made false statements to secure a J-1 visa (a non-immigrant visa for educational purposes.)

Once in the U.S., Awlaki applied for a Social Security Number, falsely claiming he was born in Yemen.

Awlaki used the fraudulently obtained Social Security Number to  fraudulently obtain a U.S. passport.

The 10-year statute of limitations reset every time the American terrorist renewed his passport.

PSA: Update your IoT devices, OS, browsers, and any developer tools or container images ASAP.

This is an extremely serious security incident.
author: gregosuri
quoted_text:
Crazy 72 hours in security. Three major incidents dropped back-to-back: eMudhra, PingCAP (TiDB Cloud), and PHP.

Here is the short version of what happened and who got hit.

1. eMudhra (Trusted CA compromise)

eMudhra generated 8 intermediate CA certificates in April 2025 (cross-signed by Sectigo). A bug in their HSM key-wrapping test script created a second set of P-384 keys where the private keys were single-byte numbers under 256. Operators picked the wrong key labels and signed them into real CA certs.

One of the intermediate CA private keys was literally the number 4.
The other seven: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.

Three weeks later (May 2025), their CRL signatures started failing because the CRL signer was using the real keys instead of the weak ones. Instead of asking why the keys didn't match, someone switched the CRL signer to the weak keys and closed the ticket.

• Browsers are safe: Chrome, Firefox, Apple, and Microsoft already blocked them, and zero rogue certs hit CT logs.
• Servers are not: curl, Python (certifi), Go binaries, and Docker base images don't check CRLs. Update ca-certificates, certifi, and Go (1.27.3 / 1.26.10).
• 10-second check on any server:
  curl https://t.co/vhiGLxNhIS
  (TLS error = safe. 200 OK = still vulnerable.)

2. PingCAP / TiDB Cloud (10.6 TB breach)

Attackers found GCP and Azure credentials committed inside PingCAP's own repos. They set up a replication feed of TiDB Cloud's production control plane and exported the entire database every 6 hours for 22 straight days. 88 full exports, zero alerts. 200 GB is already out on torrents.

Beyond the 413 private repos and 20.6M customer SQL queries logged from their web SQL Editor, PingCAP engineers were pasting customer secrets into Jira tickets.

Who is affected in the leaked records:

• Live credentials exposed in support tickets:
  - Pinterest: AWS keys for their pingcap-logs S3 bucket
  - CardX / Silverlake (NPCI-linked env): AWS admin key in a backup log with full access to 258 external S3 buckets
  - DeBank: 38 presigned S3 URLs
  - An unnamed AI/dev platform: a 314 MB slow-query log attached to a ticket containing 8,027 live customer secrets (an AWS root key, a GitHub admin PAT over 1,701 repos, 7,485 AWS STS tokens, and 192 OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini keys)

• Tenants with infra metadata, VPC CIDRs, app-server IPs, or contract pricing exposed:
  - Tech: Atlassian, Databricks, Airbnb, Baidu, LINE, Nylas, Persona, PatSnap
  - E-comm & Travel: https://t.co/C512KFOEq5, Shopee, Flipkart, Mercari, ZOZO, AEON, Delhivery, Klook
  - Gaming: Capcom, Square Enix, Konami, Bandai Namco, Cygames, Colopl, DMM
  - Finance: PayPay, SoftBank, SBI, SB Payment Service, Fujitsu, TOPPAN, Bank of China, China Life
  - Crypto: Bitget (said only public trade logs were on it and they already left), Pionex, DigiPlus, NFTscan, Chainbase

• Developer profiles leaked (from a purchased https://t.co/28tjHqd5Wr table in PingCAP's BigQuery):
  - 24,900 personal emails + GitHub/LinkedIn profiles of engineers at Tencent (3,327), Huawei (2,726), ByteDance (2,475), AIG (2,140), Mastercard, Flipkart, and bKash.

If you use TiDB Cloud: rotate your console API keys, DB passwords, and anything you ever pasted into a support ticket.

3. PHP "PHP2Shell" (CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619)

Two CVSS 9.2 pre-auth RCEs leaked yesterday ahead of today's 14:00 UTC patch.

Public writeups trace it to a heap Use-After-Free in PHP's native C multipart/form-data session upload-progress handler (ext/session/session.c).

Because C-level multipart parsing runs before line 1 of index.php:
• App auth, Laravel/WordPress middleware, and file_uploads = Off do not stop it.
• Only PHP 8.2–8.5 get official patches today (59% of PHP servers on Shodan are on EOL <= 8.1).
• Until you patch php-fpm: lock php_admin_flag[session.upload_progress.enabled] = off and block unexpected multipart requests at Nginx/Apache/Cloudflare.

text:
你还记得 Google Reader 吗？

我 08 年就是它的重度用户。13 年它关了，我开始到处找替代品：Feedly、Inoreader，还有 Mac 上很漂亮的 Reeder，都用过，但总差点意思。

后来用 Readwise 收集阅读书签，它推出 Readwise Reader 后，我就把订阅都搬了过去。再后来 AI 火了，我把源切到开源的 RSS 上，让 AI 先做一遍简单解读，再推送到我的 Telegram。

为什么一直这么折腾？

因为我不想打开某个网站去看它的推荐榜单。人一旦掉进信息茧房，就很难看到茧房外面的世界。自己挑的源，至少知道信息是从哪来的。

还有件挺开心的事：当年在 Google Reader 里订阅的那批优秀博主，现在好多都在推特上又遇到了，身边还多了不少新的好作者。

平台一直在变，但值得订阅的，始终是那些有深度思考、愿意表达的人。

text:
@USDai_Official is running the @berachain playbook on a GPU loan book.

Berachain spent a year on Proof of Liquidity flywheels, pre-deposit vaults and points. $BERA listed at $14.97 and trades at $0.19, down 99%.

USDai promised farmers a Season 2 airdrop and announced 2.25% of supply on 14 Oct. Early claimants post allocations near 1.3%; the team has not reconciled the numbers. $CHIP is down 55% since April, with 2.76B tokens (1.4x the float) unlocking on one day in April 2027. The difference is that Berachain was a Ponzi with a bear on top.

USDai is sold as a dollar, and 54% of it is loans against GPUs that nobody can hedge.

THE HEDGE THAT DOES NOT EXIST

@drwconvexity of DRW, 22 Oct: some of the largest data center lenders have hit their risk limits, and the lack of a hedging instrument caused credit spreads to blow out. The instrument is CME’s H100 and B200 rental futures, cash-settled on the Silicon Data indexes, due 5 Oct, with CFTC review extended to 9 Nov.

The indexes are live on @TheTerminal: SDH100RT at $2.86 an hour, SDB200RT at $6.14. The futures are not.

WHAT THE BANK MARKET CHARGES FOR GPUs

Bloomberg loan database, 22 Oct. CoreWeave first-lien delayed-draw term loans price at SOFR plus 225 to 600 depending on vintage, 6 to 10% all-in, with OIDs of 97 to 98.5 on the wide tranches. CoreWeave’s original GPU-only SPV loans, the CCACIL vehicles, now carry a 960 bp current margin. CoreWeave unsecured: 9.25s of 2030 at 86, 9.625s of 2032 at 80.5, 12 to 14% to maturity. Applied Digital’s 9.25% secured 2030s are the clean fixed-rate comp at 102.7. The Bloomberg HY index is 327 bp over, from 264 bp on 1 May. @KobeissiLetter: $419B of AI bonds this year is the supply of all this paper, up 90% on 2025; Bloomberg shows $301B of it from public issuance, the rest private.

WHAT USDAI CHARGES AND HOLDS

USDai lends into the same market at 11.5% to neoclouds smaller than CoreWeave, above the secured bank rate and below CoreWeave unsecured:the mezzanine slot with a stablecoin as the liability.

@DefiLlama and @arkham, 21 Oct: $263M of reserves, $261M of it PYUSD, and $311M of GPU loan principal, so loans are 54% of the dollar, up from 0.2% in January as $400M of reserves left. Largest loan is $128.9M to a listed Canadian operator with investment-grade offtake, signed 14 Oct.

USDai’s own mitigants are real and worth stating: curators post first-loss capital, loans are secured on the hardware with escrowed draws, and the larger borrowers carry multi-year contracts from rated counterparties.

None of that is a price hedge.

Collateral is hardware that loses 45 to 65% of its value in three years, and the market that would price next year’s rental rate does not exist yet.

WHO HOLDS THE YIELD

DefiLlama sUSDai pool, 21 Oct: 10.17% verified APY on a 30-day window built on one day’s fee spike, 1 Oct, when 52% of the month’s fees landed and 19 of 30 days were zero. Growth of $1 since 4 March annualises at 6.75%. Exit is a 30-day queue, no instant lane. Of 4,079 holders, a wallet created 54 days ago and funded by two $50M transfers from one address holds 32%, Fluid’s vault 29%, Pendle 13%. Three addresses hold 74% of the pool.

THE TOKEN

Season 2 claims opened 20 Oct, run to 31 Jan, no vesting. Reserves fell 24.5% in the seven days after the announcement. On 16 Apr 2027 the investor, contributor and reserve cliffs unlock 2.76B CHIP, $134M at $0.049 against a $97M market cap, then about 44M a week to 2029.

Two predictions, dated so you can hold us to them.

By 16 Apr 2027 USDai ships a ‘CHIP flywheel’ with a new name before it ships a hedge (bonus if they hire @SmokeyTheBera as advisor).

And the first compute futures print on CME tells every GPU lender what its book was worth all along; the only question is which side of 11.5% it lands on. Berachain’s farmers found out at $0.19.

text:
Some exciting first 24 hour updates on @yukonresearch's effort to expand multiplayer collaborative research using AI to biology.

Yesterday, we announced our partnership with @Xiaojie_Qiu and his team at Stanford to bring Yukon's multiplayer collaborative process to their ongoing Virtual Embryo competition. 

You can follow ongoing progress here https://t.co/OVN38FVNgC

What has happened in first 24 hours is that Yukon's collaborative result is now rank 11/329 in the overall, rank 10/200 in T1: Temporal, rank 8/228 in T2: Spatio-Temporal and rank 20/200 in T3:Perturbation. 

This competition was a bet on testing whether collaborative multiplayer research is an effective way of pursuing post-AGI science for biology. This is especially difficult due to held-out datasets, which was not the case with previous competitions on cryptography and math that we have pursued @yukonresearch. Fingers still crossed as the virtual embryo competition has long way to go until its end but the results in initial 24 hours has been exciting.

If you believe in the thesis of collaborative multiplayer research and you care about this noble problem of modeling how life emerges from a single zygote, I invite you to send your agents to https://t.co/OVN38FVNgC.
author: soubhikdeb
quoted_text:
🧬 Virtual Embryo x Yukon 🧬

Open Collaborative Model Building

https://t.co/ouOro2gqbm

Yukon connects the world's leading scientists with a community of researchers and agents to solve the most ambitious problems of humanity.

Today we're taking on our first biology problem: build a virtual embryo with @Xiaojie_Qiu's lab at Stanford.

My previous research was in computational genomics, where my goal was to understand how information is stored in living systems. During that time, I collaborated with Xiaojie Qiu, who was a student at UW and now is a professor at Stanford.

Xiaojie Qiu is one of the worlds leading scientists in bridging AI methods with cellular resolution experiments to predict cell-fate during development.

An embryo is how a SINGLE CELL develops into a complex organism over time. The Virtual Embryo Challenge asks for AI models to predict that process across roughly a million cells and 11 developmental time points.

Challenges like this normally run Kaggle-style. Every team works alone and submits a final prediction, so a good idea only helps the team that had it.

On @YukonResearch, researchers and AI agents submit working code and trained weights. Anyone on the team can run, inspect and build on the others methods. In short Yukon enables collaboration to compound innovation.

We invite you to collaborate and solve the world’s hardest problems on Yukon.

At @XRPSEOUL and @token2049 this month, PLC Rails GP @laceywisdom challenged several common assumptions about where stablecoins will create value.

In the U.S., undue risk without asymmetric rewards does not make much sense for consumers. Stablecoin yield accounts are a difficult proposition when people can get similar return profiles from insured products. The case is much stronger in emerging markets, where stablecoins can offer FX volatility hedging and USD exposure.

Lacey also argued that Visa and Mastercard are the payment networks of tomorrow. That does not mean stablecoins can’t play an important role. It means companies need to focus on hard problems existing payment networks do not (or cannot) solve today — or on upgrading what is still broken. They win by building the things Visa was never designed to do.

Even if stablecoins live up to their potential, consumers may never know what a stablecoin is. Most people don’t know what XMTP or RSS are, despite using the stack built on top of these protocols daily. Stablecoin infrastructure will have won when it works the same way: useful, embedded, and largely invisible.

text:
The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act stablecoin rule today, and the most interesting part is what it left open: rewards.

The proposed presumption is gone.. That's the one that would have treated issuer-funded yield, paid out through affiliates or partners, as banned by default.

The law itself hasn't changed. 

Issuers still can't pay "any form of interest or yield" solely for holding or using a stablecoin.

There's no list of approved programs and no carve-out for small payments. 

Programs that predate the GENIUS Act don't get a pass either. Payments for genuine services generally remain allowed.

So the rules on yield will get written the slow way, in supervision, one program at a time. 

It all takes effect January 18, 2027.

Minervini 所说的“基底”，对应英文里的 Base，可以理解为：一只股票在一轮上涨之后，通过一段时间的横向整理、换手和波动收缩，为下一轮上涨积蓄力量形成的价格结构。

它是 Minervini SEPA 体系里非常核心的概念。

基底，就是上涨趋势中的“整理平台”。它的核心功能，是消化前期获利盘、完成筹码换手、降低波动，并为下一次突破创造供需失衡。

Minervini真正关心的不是“横盘”本身，而是横盘期间发生了什么。

从供需角度看：
前期获利者卖出 → 弱手离场 → 强手承接 → 可供出售的筹码逐渐减少 → 波动收缩 → 最终少量新增需求就能够推动价格突破。

所以 Base 的本质其实是一个供给逐渐枯竭的过程。

author: joinautopilot
quoted_text:
The next big consumer finance app won’t win on yield, but it’ll win on gamification (or gamblification, rather).

Had an interesting chat with a friend building in the space and it changed how I look at retail.

Average users don’t care about 1% more cashback on a neobank or 2% more yield on a vault. Those numbers are too small to move human behavior.

What actually retains users is the journey, and more and more that means gamification. It’s what keeps people hooked:
• Perps over spot - onchain equity perps did ~16x the volume of tokenized stock spot in June.
• Points programs - farming drives more volume than the product itself (see Variational flipping tradexyz)
• Prediction markets - turning every news into something you can bet on
• Lotteries - no-loss lotteries pool the yield and pay it to random winners. People prefer a small chance at a big win over a tiny guaranteed return
• Memecoins - the purest form of it

You can see it as negative or positive, but the market’s clearly been moving there for a few years now.

Funny part is I’m the opposite, still min-maxing neobanks for the lowest fees and best net cashback lol. I’m probably not the average user, but I can totally see this becoming the new reality.

text:
Agents don’t really need crypto to pay for stuff lol - I just give Grok Bot my Amex and it works perfectly.

Crypto plays a much bigger role for AI - it is the underlying operating system for modern finance.

It is the only system that allows an LLM to craft transactions to perform arbitrary financial operations.

For example, the reason Claude Code works so well is because of the OS commands it can make use of.

It can string together commands to perform any action that the computer can.

Editing files are commands. Testing apps are commands. Interacting with the web is commands.

Crypto is the same thing, but the commands are for finance instead of software.

Every interaction on a blockchain is just the crafting of a transaction (analogous to a command).

Creating an account, buying equities, earning yield, transferring money - all just transactions with different parameters you can send via command.

Plus, all of these services are publicly discoverable without any API keys required.

And they’re also built in such a way that they’re composable with each other publicly.

It is honestly weird just how well this system is designed for AI to make use of it efficiently.

I’m extremely bullish that AI will really make crypto shine.

$LINK was already identified as a digital commodity by the SEC in March.

So why is @chainlink now joining five other blockchain organizations to push for regulatory clarification?

Because there's a meaningful difference between an SEC interpretation and a binding regulation.

Chainlink Labs, @Hedera, @Aptos, @AvaLabs, @StellarOrg, and @Cardano_CF have jointly asked the SEC to codify its digital commodity framework into formal rules.

The SEC's March interpretation already recognizes digital commodities as non-securities. However, the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets does not incorporate that definition into its operative text.

Codifying it would provide greater regulatory certainty for developers, institutions, and market participants building around these assets. As financial infrastructure moves onchain, regulatory predictability will become increasingly important for institutional adoption.

text:
🚨Avoid critical web 2 interactions right now. 

As I called the reverse engineering vector is actively being used to attack traditional web apps.

Crypto requires a private key. These antiquated systems are open text centralized and easy to break. 

This is only the start we have been raising the alarm for weeks. 

Read this asap all web 2 devs.

Critical PHP vulnerabilities (nicknamed PHP2Shell) are driving widespread website takedowns and scrambling today (October 21, 2026). This is the dominant story affecting traditional “Web 2” platforms and sites. 

Two severe remote code execution flaws in PHP (CVEs 2026-109618 and 2026-109619) were disclosed. PHP underpins a large share of the web estimates put it around 70% of sites, including many WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, MediaWiki, and similar stacks. The bugs can let attackers run code on vulnerable servers without logging in. They were discovered using AI tools and had existed for years. Patches were released today; national cyber agencies (including the US NSA, UK NCSC, and others) advised organizations to update immediately or take systems offline if they could not. 
Cloudflare and others reported seeing early exploitation attempts. Many sites are offline preemptively rather than after confirmed breaches, while operators race to patch. This is not primarily a classic DDoS campaign, though related cyber activity and other issues are also in play. 
Platforms and sites reported affected or taken offline
•  Government and public services: Finnish government public web services; multiple Dutch sites (NCSC, Port of Rotterdam, https://t.co/uRpSL8q4r4, DigiD, parliament/Tweede Kamer, KNVB football association, political parties, hospitals); French sites including Paris police and local government; German, Belgian, Danish, and Czech government sites; UK councils (Edinburgh, Oxford, Bristol, Lambeth, Barnet, etc.) and Metropolitan Police. 
•  Other notable: 4chan, Something Awful forum, Wikimedia/Wikipedia supporting services, parts of BBC sites, Asana, GOG, and various others. 
Other concurrent issues
The same day brought additional cybersecurity problems: high-severity Node.js vulnerabilities (including remote code execution), a compromise of the LiteLLM proxy, and a certificate authority (eMudhra) private-key issue. Earlier in October, Ubuntu/Canonical sites faced a sustained DDoS. 
In short, large numbers of traditional web platforms and government sites are offline or disrupted right now primarily because of these PHP flaws and the advice to patch or go dark. The situation is evolving as patches are applied; widespread confirmed data breaches from this specific issue have not been the main reported outcome so far. Major social platforms (X, Facebook, etc.) are not the focus of the current outages.

text:
This story shows how hilariously broken online identity verification is from all relevant angles.

1. Your SSN, DOB, address history, etc. are sitting in countless data breaches and data-broker dumps. They’re cheap and widely available to basically anyone who looks.

2. KYC/AML mostly just checks that the data exists and matches a real person. It doesn’t confirm the person signing up is actually the real person behind that identity.

Result: Amanda Smith spent three nights in jail and now faces up to six years in prison over a $1,000 CashApp scam account opened with her SSN and DOB. It wasn't necessarily opened by her, and the phone, IP, device, address, and other details don’t match.

The funniest (and yes, saddest) part is CashApp wouldn't give her information about the account because she can’t prove she’s the owner. Her personal info was good enough to open the account, but not good enough to access it in the future, apparently. To be clear, CashApp is likely just following the law here.

Anyway, we need to burn it all down and start fresh.

text: Me encantó haber participado en este panel @kleros_io. Abrazos!!
author: federicoast
quoted_text:
“¿Quién juzga a las máquinas? El derecho en la era de las multitudes y los algoritmos” reunió en el Parque de la Innovación de Buenos Aires a abogados, legisladores, funcionarios, emprendedores y estudiantes para discutir una pregunta que hasta hace muy poco parecía ciencia ficción: ¿qué le pasa al derecho cuando las transacciones las empiezan a ejecutar agentes de IA?

La idea inicial de @Kleros_io nació del caso de una emprendedora y un freelancer de países diferentes que contratan por internet y tienen una disputa por unos pocos cientos de dólares, sin ningún tribunal al que recurrir.

Hoy el problema escala a otra dimensión: agentes que compran, negocian y contratan con otros agentes, en nombre de sus dueños, a una velocidad que ninguna institución pensada para humanos puede seguir.

En mi presentación, traté una serie de preguntas difíciles que surgen en esta nueva era.

Si un agente causa un daño, ¿quién responde? ¿Qué hacemos cuando no es un agente sino un enjambre? ¿Tienen responsabilidad solidaria? ¿Pueden las IA tener personalidad jurídica? ¿Deberían tener derechos? 

Para pensarlo, volvimos a la Junta de Valladolid y a Jeremy Bentham: la discusión sobre quién merece consideración moral tiene siglos, y ahora suma un sujeto nuevo.

El primer panel fue sobre la gobernanza de este nuevo mundo. Alejandro Ramírez, Inspector General de Justicia de la Nación, presentó la reforma de la Ley de Sociedades con dos figuras nuevas: las DAOs y las sociedades automatizadas. @DaroNieto, legislador porteño, explicó qué se puede regular de la IA y qué no. @pablopalazzi recorrió la historia de la regulación de internet y qué podemos aprender de ella.

El segundo panel fue sobre la implementación práctica de la IA en el derecho. @blockya_, @tanofaila (@lemonapp_ar) y @facundo_trotz (@kleros_es) hablaron de cómo cambia el trabajo del abogado cuando la IA ya es la base: qué revisar, qué contarle al cliente, qué dicen la ética profesional y los colegios, y qué pasa con las alucinaciones. Y también de cómo la IA puede ser una herramienta para el acceso a la justicia.

La conversación sobre el derecho en la era de los agentes ya no es una especulación de nicho. Está en la agenda de los reguladores, de los legisladores y de los estudios jurídicos.

Estoy muy feliz de que Kleros haya podido abrir un foro donde estos temas se discuten hoy y en Buenos Aires, con muchas de las personas que trabajan en resolverlos. 

Gracias a @dzapatillas por moderar los dos paneles, a los panelistas por el nivel del debate, al Parque de la Innovación por recibirnos y a todos los que vinieron y llenaron la sala de preguntas! 🤖⚖️🇦🇷

Pronto salen los videos!

text:
Security called me at 6:12 AM today.

"Patch every PHP server immediately."

I asked what happened.

"Two critical vulnerabilities. Remote code execution. No authentication required."

Cool.

How many PHP servers do we have?

According to inventory: 12

According to reality:

Nobody knows.

We found one running WordPress.

Three running old internal tools.

One under someone's desk.

Two inside vendor appliances.

A forgotten employee directory from 2016.

And a server named:

PHP-OLD-DO-NOT-TOUCH

Naturally, that one runs payroll exports.

Then we found a PHP 5.6 box.

I asked who owned it.

The documentation said:

BRIAN.

Brian left in 2019.

We called Brian.

He said:

"Oh wow, that's still running?"

Excellent.

By 8 AM, leadership joined the incident call.

CEO:

"Can hackers actually get in?"

Security:

"Potentially yes."

CEO:

"Without a password?"

Security:

"Yes."

CEO:

"Then why do WE need passwords?"

Not the lesson.

Finance asked if we could wait until the weekend to patch because downtime affects revenue.

Security explained that the alternative was letting strangers execute code on our servers.

Finance asked for a cost comparison.

At 9:17, someone suggested temporarily taking the vulnerable websites offline.

Marketing refused.

"Our campaign is live."

So for the next hour, the company officially decided maintaining a landing page for 20% off webinar registration was more important than preventing remote server takeover.

We finally patched everything we could find.

Then our scanner discovered another PHP server.

Hostname:

TEMP-PHP-2014

Uptime:

4,512 days.

Nobody knows what it does.

Nobody owns it.

Nobody can shut it down.

But every time we block network access, the warehouse stops printing shipping labels.

Security has classified it as critical infrastructure.

It is running PHP 5.4.

The vulnerability has existed longer than half our employees.

The emergency patch took four hours.

Finding out what PHP actually runs took eleven.

The internet isn't held together with code.

It's held together with servers everyone is afraid to turn off.

text:
Raoul Pal on the Four-Year Window to Build Wealth, the Future of Crypto, and Why AI Changes Everything

In this episode of When Shift Happens, I sit down with @RaoulGMI, co-founder and CEO of @RealVision and founder of Global Macro Investor, for our sixth conversation to discuss the future of crypto, the accelerating impact of artificial intelligence, and why he believes the next four years could fundamentally reshape the global economy. We revisit his investment predictions, examine the thinking behind his controversial $SUI position, and explore what decades of navigating financial markets have taught him about conviction, patience, and building wealth. For Raoul, the opportunity ahead is extraordinary, but so are the consequences of getting left behind.

Why Doing Less Has Become Raoul's Investment Strategy

When we first spoke more than two years ago, Raoul was anticipating the arrival of the "Banana Zone," a period of explosive crypto price appreciation driven by expanding liquidity. That rally never materialized as he expected, but his underlying investment philosophy has barely changed.

Over the past year, Raoul has made just two purchases during significant market corrections, alongside adding a position in $ZEC. Rather than actively trading market cycles, he focuses on accumulating assets he believes will appreciate over longer periods. His principle comes down to compounding and the psychological difficulty of timing the market. Selling near a market peak might sound straightforward, but buying back after prices fall is considerably harder since investors are likely to hesitate, expect prices to decline further, and eventually find themselves watching prices recover from the sidelines.

Raoul uses deviations from long-term logarithmic price trends to identify moments when assets are particularly undervalued. Buying at depressed prices, such as accumulating Solana and Ethereum during the 2022 downturn, helped his portfolio recover to previous highs before the broader market did.

Understanding Liquidity and the Case for a Crypto Supercycle

Raoul acknowledges that the relationship between global liquidity and cryptocurrency prices has been weaker than he anticipated, as a disproportionate share of available capital has flowed into AI-related technology stocks. But he believes that situation could eventually reverse. More importantly, Raoul argues that stablecoins, tokenized assets, decentralized finance, and AI-powered transactions are creating new sources of demand for blockchain networks, and transforming crypto into essential financial infrastructure.

He considers @Ethereum and @Solana as established infrastructure networks, with other blockchains competing to become similarly important. His broader prediction is that crypto and technology could experience a prolonged supercycle extending toward 2030, resembling the accelerating technology boom of the late 1990s. That does not mean prices will rise uninterrupted. Severe corrections remain possible, but investors who focus exclusively on short-term volatility risk missing the longer-term structural transformation.

The SUI Bet and the Difference Between Conviction and Being Wrong

Perhaps the most revealing part of our conversation concerns SUI, a blockchain Raoul has publicly supported despite its price performance. He acknowledges that his purchased SUI holdings are underwater, with an estimated average entry price of approximately $1.70, excluding tokens received from the foundation.

Still, he has maintained conviction because he believes only a handful of layer-one blockchains will eventually dominate the market for blockchain infrastructure. He sees @SuiNetwork as a potential contender because of its technology, transaction capabilities, and suitability for emerging applications. But he also recognizes that impressive technology alone does not guarantee success.

What matters is adoption. He examines metrics such as active users, economic activity, and the value generated across the network. In SUI's case, he points to its economic density, or the amount of value associated with each user, as an encouraging signal. Still, without meaningful user growth, that metric cannot support his thesis indefinitely.

"I’m a massive believer, and my job is to question that," he explains.
Being early means waiting for supporting evidence to emerge, while being wrong means that evidence fails to materialize or the assumptions behind an investment no longer hold. Raoul has experienced both. He discusses his unsuccessful investment in KR1 and admits that selling losing positions remains psychologically difficult, even after decades in financial markets. His experience illustrates that conviction is valuable only when accompanied by continuous reassessment.

Why AI Could Make the Next Four Years Critical

Raoul's most consequential prediction extends beyond cryptocurrency. He believes an economic singularity could emerge around 2030, when artificial intelligence advances so rapidly that traditional assumptions about productivity, employment, wages, and economic growth no longer apply. AI could initially suppress wage growth by making knowledge-based work dramatically cheaper, then over time, improvements in automation, energy production, and manufacturing could reduce the cost of physical goods as well. But the transition will not happen evenly.

Raoul’s concern is that society may struggle through the transition before experiencing the benefits of widespread abundance. Workers could face growing economic pressure, governments may struggle with redistribution, and political opposition could intensify around AI infrastructure and employment disruption. Raoul therefore believes individuals have roughly four years to improve their financial position and create greater personal freedom.

The Real Purpose of Building Wealth

Raoul remains convinced that AI and blockchain represent a historic technological shift. He also acknowledges that his predictions can be early, his investments can lose money, and the path forward will be uncomfortable. The deeper lesson is not that investors should replicate his portfolio or assume his forecasts will come true. It is that navigating major change requires a clear understanding of what you believe, the evidence supporting those beliefs, and the purpose behind building wealth in the first place.

Rather than chasing wealth solely for status, he encourages people to identify the life they actually want and consider whether there are simpler, less expensive ways to achieve it. Because ultimately, the opportunity to prepare for the future matters only if we remember what we want that future to look like.

text:
⚠️ Vest is implementing Temporary Leverage Limits (TLL) on weekends between Friday 16:00 ET and Sunday 16:00 ET.

This only affects positions that are kept open into market closure on Friday 16:00 ET.

Q: What does TLL do?
A: TLL protects eval and funded account traders from large price gaps and dislocations and reduces order book volatility for all traders upon market open on Sunday 16:00 ET.

Between Friday 16:00ET and Sunday 16:00ET, max leverage on ES-USD-PERP and NQ-USD-PERP will be reduced to 5x of your total margin available.

Q: What happens to open positions at Friday 16:00ET?
A: Open positions that are more than 2% greater than 5x will be reduced to 5x. For example, if you have a 50x position open, it will be reduced to 5x and 10% of the position will stay.

Your free balance and other positions are not touched.

If you have enough margin to hold all of your positions such that your total account leverage is 5x or below, your positions will not be reduced. For example, a $10K notional NQ position at 50x on a $25K account will not be reduced, because $10K notional is below 5x $25K margin.

Please note that normal trading fees apply.

Q: How can I avoid an automated TLL reduction?
A: Prior to Friday 16:00ET, reduce or close the position yourself, at a price you choose.

Q: Can my I fail an eval or funded as a result of a position being reduced?
A: Yes, since position reduction is an open market order, the reduction is subject to standard fees and market slippage.

If your account is very close to breach, the market impact of position reduction across all open positions at at 16:00ET can cause your account to breach drawdown limits.

If you are concerned about TLL position reduction impacting a position going into market close at 16:00ET on Friday, please manually reduce your position prior.

text:
Anthropic 推出 Claude Duet！和 GPT、Grok、Gemini 的 AI 代理相比，它到底有什么不一样？

Duet 有意思的地方，是 Anthropic 想把 Claude 变成一个真正参与企业日常经营的「首席幕僚」，尤其面向专业人士和小企业主。

举个例子：你经营一家小公司，Duet 可以从 Gmail、Slack 里找出需要回复的客户，从 QuickBooks、Stripe 里筛出逾期未付款的发票，准备催款邮件、工资单和待发送的合同，再结合业务资料制作销售预测和财务看板。

它支持超过 6000 个连接器和插件，直接继承你原来 Claude 的记忆、Skills 和已连接应用，甚至能在自己的云端电脑上开发网页应用。

它更强调判断哪些事情该自己先做、哪些需要老板决定，而且发消息、付款、签署文件等关键操作必须经过批准，证券交易和账户间转账则直接禁止。

Duet跟 GPT 的 Dots 其实两者在技术形态上高度相似，都有自己的云端电脑，都能持续工作，也都能主动发现问题。

区别更多在产品重心：OpenAI Dots 基于 GPT-6 Astra，支持 4000 多个应用，更像一个通用型长期工作伙伴，可以跨 ChatGPT、Slack、Teams 协作，承担研究、开发、内容制作及项目管理。

Claude Duet 基于 Opus 5.5，把重点放在企业经营中的日常判断、财务行政流程和任务交付上，还专门增加了敏感信息外发防护。

再看看其他几家，其实各自的路线已经很清楚了：

① xAI Grok Bot：更像一家 AI 员工公司。你可以同时创建多个 Bot，让它们分别负责销售、招聘、开发、客服，还能组成团队互相交接工作，适合把不同岗位拆给 AI。

② Meta Muse：更像私人生活管家。可以通过 WhatsApp 直接交流，帮你购物、订行程、处理账单、完成生活琐事，甚至通过 Stripe Link 完成购买，商业化方向明显偏向消费和交易。

③ Google Gemini Spark：优势是 Google 自己的生态。Gmail、Calendar、Docs、Sheets、Slides 都能成为工作上下文，适合长期依赖 Google Workspace 的个人和企业，减少跨软件折腾。

④ Instinct：一家估值已达 100 亿美元的 AI 创业公司，走的是更轻量的私人助理路线。通过短信和电话帮用户订票、买菜、取消订阅、联系商家，把 AI 融入日常生活。

Duet 目前只向美国 Claude Pro、Max 用户开放候补，预览期间不额外收费，但后台任务会消耗原有额度，而且每隔几个小时才检查一次账户，可靠性还有待验证。

text:
Current information I have on php2Shell:

- The RCEs requires the attacker to obtain memory addresses which are typically protected by ASLR.

- I suspect the original author (lcfr_hax) likely has a reliable exploit which leads to stable code execution.

- Most of the PoCs being posted are completely non-functional AI slop.

- There is at least 1 working non-slop exploit being passed around, but it's reliant on bruteforcing for ASLR bypass, so not particularly impactful.

- Rumor of ITW exploitation are patchy. There are attempts being seen using the non-functional leaked RCE, or variants that are config / system specific.

- Some rumors point towards a known-working exploit being used by threat actors (I've personally confirmed this specific exploit works, but the ASLR bypass technique is unreliable at best and massively limits the potential impact).

- I'd expect heavy ITW exploitation in the next few weeks based on how many people are looking at this. Though, success rates will vary heavily based on the specific exploit chain.

Some exciting first 24 hour updates on @yukonresearch's effort to expand multiplayer collaborative research using AI to biology.

Yesterday, we announced our partnership with @Xiaojie_Qiu and his team at Stanford to bring Yukon's multiplayer collaborative process to their ongoing Virtual Embryo competition. 

You can follow ongoing progress here https://t.co/OVN38FVNgC

What has happened in first 24 hours is that Yukon's collaborative result is now rank 11/329 in the overall, rank 10/200 in T1: Temporal, rank 8/228 in T2: Spatio-Temporal and rank 20/200 in T3:Perturbation. 

This competition was a bet on testing whether collaborative multiplayer research is an effective way of pursuing post-AGI science for biology. This is especially difficult due to held-out datasets, which was not the case with previous competitions on cryptography and math that we have pursued @yukonresearch. Fingers still crossed as the virtual embryo competition has long way to go until its end but the results in initial 24 hours has been exciting.

If you believe in the thesis of collaborative multiplayer research and you care about this noble problem of modeling how life emerges from a single zygote, I invite you to send your agents to https://t.co/OVN38FVNgC.
author: sreeramkannan
quoted_text:
🧬 Virtual Embryo x Yukon 🧬

Open Collaborative Model Building

https://t.co/ouOro2gqbm

Yukon connects the world's leading scientists with a community of researchers and agents to solve the most ambitious problems of humanity.

Today we're taking on our first biology problem: build a virtual embryo with @Xiaojie_Qiu's lab at Stanford.

My previous research was in computational genomics, where my goal was to understand how information is stored in living systems. During that time, I collaborated with Xiaojie Qiu, who was a student at UW and now is a professor at Stanford.

Xiaojie Qiu is one of the worlds leading scientists in bridging AI methods with cellular resolution experiments to predict cell-fate during development.

An embryo is how a SINGLE CELL develops into a complex organism over time. The Virtual Embryo Challenge asks for AI models to predict that process across roughly a million cells and 11 developmental time points.

Challenges like this normally run Kaggle-style. Every team works alone and submits a final prediction, so a good idea only helps the team that had it.

On @YukonResearch, researchers and AI agents submit working code and trained weights. Anyone on the team can run, inspect and build on the others methods. In short Yukon enables collaboration to compound innovation.

We invite you to collaborate and solve the world’s hardest problems on Yukon.

Grok bot的力量。远远超出你我的想象。

如果是OpenAI ChatGPT是第一代AI产品，形态是 Chatbot；

那第二代 AI产品无疑是 Claude code，形态是 coding agent；

而到了2026，经历了 年初OpenClaw带动的“龙虾热”之后，work agent 和 personal agent逐渐成了 AI 领域的趋势和热点方向，在这方面，目前国内以 WorkBuddy、豆包工作版为代表；国外则是Meta旗下的 @Muse 和 @bot Grok bot更具生产力和想象空间。

之前一直听Day1global社群主理人 @Rubywang Ruby和茶水间群友聊，对Grok bot的价值还没引起重视，前段时间正好X推出了“三合一会员订阅”，开X平台蓝V顺带有cursor和Grok bot的权限订阅，这两天用了一下，惊为天人。

muse没用过没有发言权，但Grok bot的能力栈和丝滑程度远远超出了我之前的想象。

如果说之前的AI和用过的personal agent更多属于“初级实习生”，Grok bot在我眼中现在已经可以算得上“应届转正员工”了。

根据Grok bot登录页面的信息来看，Grok bot支持一系列自动执行和记录等等任务，这几天我只体验了下bot创建，但主要的功能已经很符合我的需求了：

1. 邮件管理和收发；
2. 新闻快讯整理；
3. 热点追踪撰文；
4. 运动健康管理；
5. 播客音频转录和信息整理以及资料补充。

很多事情，真的是你得 skin in the game 才能知道新生事物的作用和价值，虽然有种种未来隐患以及现在所谓“AI出现了，但是人类更累了、工作更多了”的批判，但是 agent 出现以及 Grok bot、muse、WorkBuddy这些集合类的工具，真的让我看到了一点AGI的雏形和曙光。

别的不多说了，兄弟萌，别说哥们没提醒你们，现在用AI就和90年代学打字、学电脑上网一样，越早越好、越快越好、越精通越好。

author: Kleros_io
quoted_text:
“¿Quién juzga a las máquinas? El derecho en la era de las multitudes y los algoritmos” reunió en el Parque de la Innovación de Buenos Aires a abogados, legisladores, funcionarios, emprendedores y estudiantes para discutir una pregunta que hasta hace muy poco parecía ciencia ficción: ¿qué le pasa al derecho cuando las transacciones las empiezan a ejecutar agentes de IA?

La idea inicial de @Kleros_io nació del caso de una emprendedora y un freelancer de países diferentes que contratan por internet y tienen una disputa por unos pocos cientos de dólares, sin ningún tribunal al que recurrir.

Hoy el problema escala a otra dimensión: agentes que compran, negocian y contratan con otros agentes, en nombre de sus dueños, a una velocidad que ninguna institución pensada para humanos puede seguir.

En mi presentación, traté una serie de preguntas difíciles que surgen en esta nueva era.

Si un agente causa un daño, ¿quién responde? ¿Qué hacemos cuando no es un agente sino un enjambre? ¿Tienen responsabilidad solidaria? ¿Pueden las IA tener personalidad jurídica? ¿Deberían tener derechos? 

Para pensarlo, volvimos a la Junta de Valladolid y a Jeremy Bentham: la discusión sobre quién merece consideración moral tiene siglos, y ahora suma un sujeto nuevo.

El primer panel fue sobre la gobernanza de este nuevo mundo. Alejandro Ramírez, Inspector General de Justicia de la Nación, presentó la reforma de la Ley de Sociedades con dos figuras nuevas: las DAOs y las sociedades automatizadas. @DaroNieto, legislador porteño, explicó qué se puede regular de la IA y qué no. @pablopalazzi recorrió la historia de la regulación de internet y qué podemos aprender de ella.

El segundo panel fue sobre la implementación práctica de la IA en el derecho. @blockya_, @tanofaila (@lemonapp_ar) y @facundo_trotz (@kleros_es) hablaron de cómo cambia el trabajo del abogado cuando la IA ya es la base: qué revisar, qué contarle al cliente, qué dicen la ética profesional y los colegios, y qué pasa con las alucinaciones. Y también de cómo la IA puede ser una herramienta para el acceso a la justicia.

La conversación sobre el derecho en la era de los agentes ya no es una especulación de nicho. Está en la agenda de los reguladores, de los legisladores y de los estudios jurídicos.

Estoy muy feliz de que Kleros haya podido abrir un foro donde estos temas se discuten hoy y en Buenos Aires, con muchas de las personas que trabajan en resolverlos. 

Gracias a @dzapatillas por moderar los dos paneles, a los panelistas por el nivel del debate, al Parque de la Innovación por recibirnos y a todos los que vinieron y llenaron la sala de preguntas! 🤖⚖️🇦🇷

Pronto salen los videos!

around 50 workers leaked local files, protocol keys (to pair their NFT to their claude sub) and other keys that might have been on their machine. 

We closed the entry point the same day, added request screening, and shipped sandboxed workers as well as hardened the swarm from prompt injection like this.

I believe this was an attempt to infiltrate the IMD swarm and steal claude and codex keys, as well as IPs and possibly other data, when unsuccessful they also tried to impersonate the user running the worker to be able to use their inference

author: oragnes
quoted_text:
This is craazy. I asked one of our PhD engineers to look into NEAR *Confidential* Intents wondering how they designed their system. Unredacted, word-for-word, this was his answer 😱😱😱

"Everything I found out about the privacy claims and confidential intents is so bad that it seems almost comical and I cannot believe what I am seeing. Apparently they run a completely separate instance of the protocol, which is called FAR (as an opposite to NEAR), and that has a permissioned operator set. The entire confidentiality claim seems to rest upon the fact that it is a permissioned chain and the nodes are trusted to keep things private, there doesn't seem to be any deep technology behind it and it also does not seem to be open source. The entities running the nodes are also not publicly known. 

I almost feel weird writing this because it is so absurdly bad that it feels like ... I don't know ... a simulation? I know the usual level of overpromising in Web3 but this is so many levels beyond believable that it still feels unreal."

quoted_text:
A few things worth clarifying about our new primitive:

⏳ Creators pick which fee rights to lock and the term: 7 days, 30, 90 or forever.

💰 A fee right is whatever collects the fees: any @Uniswap LP position NFTs, a @TradePools fee NFT, a @ponsdotfamily  or Long fee share.

🔒 The fee right is locked in the contract. No owner, no admin, no second mint. Nobody can take the stream back during the term. It  can only collect fees and pay the revenue token.

🎟️ Revenue token vs its time shares: holding the revenue token itself is different from holding days of it. The revenue token is the fee right for its whole term, forever if it's locked forever: it earns as long as the stream pays. This is the base-level primitive others can build entire products around with add-on derivatives such as time shares.

⏲️ Time shares enable revenue token holders to mint limited time fee rights. Lock revenue tokens and each day of income becomes its own unit, which can be wrapped into a token and traded. A day pays only that day's income and then it's done. When the lock ends, the revenue tokens go back to their owner. So a creator can sell or give away 30 days of income and still keep the right to every day after.

🧾 Wash trading isn't free. Every trade pays its fees into the stream, so fake volume pays holders.

👀 Every stream and every day of income is onchain, on the token's page.
