text:
Pumpfun has officially lost the plot.

I'm not sure what their endgame is here, but I know for a fact that nobody is going to read “Be the next Kimchi” and suddenly feel an overwhelming urge to sign up for Pumpfun and start buying shitters.

I never thought we'd reach the point where this needs explaining, but absolutely nobody outside CT knows who Kimchi is. And a good chunk of CT knows that the whole “made $40M trading Trump” story is straight up larp and what he was actually doing, was deploying and rugging coins 24/7.

The fact that, out of every ace this multibillion-dollar company could have up its sleeve, they chose to make Kimchi their poster boy speaks volumes about how out of touch they are with the space, the community that made them what they are, and the outside world as a whole.

I'm telling you, there isn't a single normal adult who wakes up in the morning wanting to “trade internet trends.” Not a single one.

Because what the fuck does trading internet trends even mean?

These guys made their bread from memecoins, and whatever name they built for themselves in this industry was a direct consequence of coins that actually went somewhere.

Pumpfun wouldn't have taken off the way it did without  Sharkcat, and it wouldn't have captured the market share it did during AI season without GOAT and Fartcoin launching there.

People buying “internet trends” with a lifespan of 24 hours, only to get thrown into endless PvP against increasingly sophisticated players across a dozen different pairs, is precisely why Pumpfun struggles to break into the mainstream and onboard retail that actually STAYS.

And these absolute idiots have somehow decided to make that their entire selling point.

You genuinely couldn't make this shit up.

The average person Pumpfun is supposedly trying to onboard is drowning in bills, trying to make ends meet, and navigating a society that's becoming increasingly isolated.

He doesn't give a fuck about speculating on internet trends. He probably doesn't even recognize most of them.

What he wants, whether he realizes it or not, is to feel like he belongs somewhere.

A place where he can make internet friends who share his humor, aesthetics, and beliefs. Somewhere he can log in after a shitty day, talk shit with like-minded people, and actually feel like he's part of something.

A fucking community.

And the funny thing is that memecoins, of all things, can genuinely provide that.

I think people massively underestimate how many guys are sitting at their desks right now, aimlessly scrolling the internet, who would happily spend money to be part of an online community where they can make friends, share jokes, and rally behind something together.

Take NEET, for example.

I'm convinced that if you explained the whole “not open to work” movement to a thousand normies, a surprisingly large percentage would find the idea of joining a global community of people who share that attitude genuinely appealing.

Now imagine telling them there's also a coin attached to that movement, and that if enough people rally behind it, they can potentially make money together.

That's a much easier sell than asking them to gamble on whichever celebrity happened to tweet something stupid fifteen minutes ago.

And it's not just NEET.

Think of all the internet subcultures, recognizable characters, aesthetics, and movements that people can actually identify with. Things that give someone a reason to hold a coin, talk about it, make content around it, and bring their friends into it without needing a new catalyst every six hours.

That's how you build something that lasts.

Instead of building their campaign around any of that, Pumpfun decided to spend millions telling people they could become the next Kimchi, a complete nobody to the audience they're supposedly trying to attract, and inviting them to gamble on internet trends.

They actually spent millions of dollars on this stunt.

It's genuinely incredible how disconnected they've become from reality, their own customer base, and seemingly basic common sense.

My father used to always tell me to never attribute to malice what can be attributed to stupidity.

And I'd genuinely love to attribute Pumpfun's incompetence to stupidity, but that's not the case here.

They've made hundreds of millions from coins that people actually wanted to own. Coins that went to hundreds of millions in market cap, made entire communities rich, and brought thousands of new people into the ecosystem.

They know this model works because it's the very model that made them rich.

But if having everyone PvP the same Elon tweet through twelve different pairings and launch modes means they can squeeze another 10% out of trading fees, I'm increasingly convinced they'll happily sacrifice everything else to get it.

And at this point, it's becoming pretty difficult to pretend otherwise.

I think there are fatigue signals everywhere, and every day we're getting a little closer to the end of the Pumpfun dynasty despite a bunch of terminal badges trying day and night to convince you otherwise.

Someone will eventually build a place where people actually want to stay, where communities are worth more than the fees generated from destroying them.

And when that happens, I genuinely don't think Pumpfun will understand why everyone left.

text:
I believe Elon Musk is planning on using the Retaliator strategy to deal with aggression from the Democrats.

The Retaliator strategy is a behavior in evolutionary game theory that begins peacefully but fiercely defends itself if attacked. A Retaliator always starts an encounter acting like a cooperative 'Dove,' but if its opponent escalates the conflict, it immediately switches to an aggressive 'Hawk' tactic to fight back. 

If the opponent backs down and becomes peaceful again, the Retaliator matches that shift and reverts to a Dove. This conditional flexibility allows Retaliators to cooperate efficiently with peaceful neighbors while successfully punishing bullies and predators without being exploited.

It combines a preference for peace with a credible willingness to retaliate, and in competitive terms outperforms both indiscriminate aggression and unconditional submission.

When a Retaliator meets a Bully (e.g., the Democrat Party), the interaction quickly exposes the Bully's empty bluff. The Bully begins the encounter aggressively by playing like a Hawk, which instantly triggers the Retaliator to abandon its peaceful default and fight back fiercely. 

Because a Bully usually retreats when faced with real aggression, it panics and flees when the Retaliator pushes back with sufficient force. As a result, the Retaliator wins the entire resource with a low risk of injury, dominating the Bully and driving it toward evolutionary extinction. 

The Doves benefit by from being around a Retaliator as well, gaining friendly interactions with it, and protection against bullies. 

The Retaliator's strength lies not in seeking conflict, but in making exploitation unprofitable and unfounded agression costly. It cooperates whenever cooperation is possible, fights decisively when fighting becomes necessary, and stops fighting as soon as the threat has passed. In evolutionary terms, its success comes from aligning peaceful intentions with effective deterrence, and a willingness to use extreme measures when necessary. 

It's the right choice.

Because GitLab also dropped a CVSS 10.0, which is the highest score they give out, for a bug that's been there since 2014, so that's every self-hosted GitLab for twelve years, and then LiteLLM 1.107.0 got hijacked and shipped a credential stealer and a remote access trojan in every single wheel and the Docker images, including latest, and you didn't even have to import it, just installing it was enough, and it's the second time this year, and then Railway paused every deployment on the entire platform because someone got into the environment variables, so now everyone has to rotate every secret they've ever stored there, and TiDB Cloud said someone was walking around inside with stolen credentials for basically a month and an extortion group says they took 10.6 terabytes, and Zeabur got breached for the second time in two months and is just shutting down, like the whole company, and Node.js patched remote code execution and a TLS bypass, and CISA says Plex is being actively exploited, and someone took over 300 Tor exit relays to steal SSH passwords, and SafePay ransomware has hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs, and India's biggest bank filed a data loss incident, and Japan has been in an official state of emergency in cyberspace since October 9, which honestly explains the 5:55 AM post. Oh, and eMudhra, a certificate authority that's issued over 60 million certificates, whose entire job is proving websites are who they say they are, was supposed to be using private keys that are random numbers over a hundred digits long, and one of them was 4. text:
Anthropic 正式下场！Claude 也要做一个会主动替你干活的「AI 个人助理」了。

10 月 21 日，Anthropic 发布 Claude Duet，面向专业人士和小企业主开放研究预览申请。

它和普通 Claude 最大的区别是：你不用每次都主动提问，它会主动来找你。

每天早上，Duet 会整理邮件、日历中的重要事项；白天持续检查关联应用，发现会议冲突、待处理账单等问题时主动提醒你。

你也可以直接把工作交给它：整理邮件、安排会议、准备工资单、制作财务预测，甚至开发网页应用。

它在云端拥有独立的虚拟电脑和浏览器，即使你关掉手机，也能继续执行任务。发送消息、付款、签署文件等关键操作，则需要你事先审批。

Duet 基于 Claude Opus 5.5，能够继承现有 Claude 账户的记忆、技能和应用连接。目前通过候补名单向美国地区的 Pro、Max 用户开放，使用额度与原有套餐共享。

值得注意的是，Anthropic 并不是第一个做这件事的公司。OpenAI 有 Dots，Meta 有 Muse，马斯克旗下的 Grok Bot 则探索多个 AI 代理协同工作。

但 Claude Duet 的产品思路很明确：不是等你来使用 AI，而是让 AI 主动管理你的注意力，把需要你做的决定挑出来，把其他工作尽可能提前做好。

AI 个人助理的竞争，已经从「谁回答得更好」，转向「谁更懂你的工作、能持续推进任务，又不会擅自越权」。

英国 FCA 发布 DeFi 指南草案，明确授权边界与风控要求

text:
I agree it’s not great to come out aggressively attacking other builders

But I do want to point out that TEE is not the right technology for a distributed permissionless network due to side channel attacks. Both NEAR and ICP run on whitelisted nodes, though, and until recently IC node operators could read all egress traffic (I believe this has recently been resolved though).

TEE is a centralized technology. At best you can prove which data center the machines run in, and prove they have a contractual obligation to not side channel attack you (of course if Interpol compels them to, they can).

ICP is cool tech, and as a company they have contributed a lot lot lot of open source code onto GitHub that is high quality.

I don’t think it’s a great look to compare market cap and usage to technology, FWIW. His points were not wrong. Just funny since I can’t run a node on their network without KYC, which is the central thrust of their claim.

quoted_text:
We've updated MLCR-AA, our leaderboard for Wisedocs' Medical Long Context Reasoning benchmark, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra now tied for the #1 score

We've updated how MLCR-AA prompts and grades models on @wisedocsai's benchmark, to better reflect how medical record review is done in practice. Models are now prompted as medical record reviewers, and asked to answer each part of a question in one paragraph with their conclusion and the supporting evidence from the record. Answers are graded by a new three-model judge panel, and we reviewed all 60 expert reference answers against their source records, refining 15.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) from @AnthropicAI and GPT-6 Astra (max) from @OpenAI are tied at the top with 41.7%, followed by GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 38.3%. Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B from @Alibaba_Qwen is the leading open weights model at 30.6%.

Key results from the updated MLCR-AA:

➤ Medical record review remains far from solved: an answer passes only when it is both complete and accurate, and no model passes more than 42% of questions and the median model passes under 15%

➤ Anthropic models lead on completeness, reaching the expert's conclusion with the right medical reasoning: Claude models hold the top 18 completeness scores across every model and effort level we tested, led by Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max with fallback) at 64.8%. The best non-Anthropic model is GPT-6 Astra (max) at 42.2%

➤ OpenAI models lead on accuracy, citing the record without exaggeration or hallucination: OpenAI models hold the top 27 accuracy scores, led by GPT-6.1 Sol (max) at 96.7%, but answer fewer questions completely: GPT-6.1 Sol (max) is complete on 40.0% of questions

We would like to thank Wisedocs for building MLCR and for their collaboration in bringing it to Artificial Analysis

text:
用 Node.js 的要升级了：三条版本线都有高危漏洞，最严重的可远程执行代码，eMudhra 那 8 枚坏证书也一并拉黑

用 Node.js 跑服务、写工具的开发者，这周要换版本了。10 月 21 日，Node.js 给还在维护的三条版本线发了安全更新：22.x 升到 v22.23.4，24.x 升到 v24.22.1，26.x 升到 v26.12.1。三条线都修了高危漏洞，最严重的一个，官方说可能被用来远程执行代码。

20.x 在 2026 年 4 月 30 日停止维护，25.x 在 6 月 1 日停止维护，这次都没有补丁。Node.js 在公告里提醒，每次发安全更新，停止维护的版本都会受影响，还在用的只能换到 22、24 或 26。

【最需要注意的几个】

Node.js 自带一个解压 Brotli 格式的组件。Brotli 是网页传输常用的压缩格式，HTTP 里写作 br。这个组件有越界写入的问题，也就是把数据写到了不该写的内存位置，官方说这能导致远程执行代码。公告对它只有这一句描述，没说什么情况下会触发。修法是同步了 Google Brotli 项目的一处改动，让解压程序更早发现并拒绝格式不对的数据。

另外三个漏洞出在 HTTPS 的证书核对上，两个高危、一个中危。Node 连 HTTPS 地址时，会核对证书上写的地址和你要连的地址是否一致，对不上就拒绝连接。这三个问题都和 IP 地址有关：IP 用全角数字写（输入法全角状态下打出的“１２７”这种），或者写法不规范、但能被宽松地认成 IP，核对就可能被绕过。修复后，Node 直接拒绝写法不规范的 IP 地址。全角数字那个只影响 24.x 和 26.x。

还有一个高危出在 dns.resolve（查域名对应地址的函数）：域名中间如果夹着一个空字符（NUL），Node 会在那里把名字截断，实际查的只是前半截。

中危里，用启动快照或者把程序打包成单个可执行文件（SEA）的要留意：crypto.randomUUID() 和 randomInt() 的随机数缓存会被一起存进包里，每次启动都生成同样的“随机”值。另有三个低危，涉及 26.x 读取 ZIP 文件，以及实验性的权限模型（--permission 开关）。

这次还更新了 c-ares、OpenSSL、SQLite、undici 等内置组件，修的是这些组件已经公开的漏洞。

【eMudhra 坏证书，Node 也拉黑了】

三个新版本都加了一份内置黑名单，第一批放进去的就是 eMudhra 那 8 枚出问题的中间证书。

这件事前几天刚曝出：印度发证机构 eMudhra 有 8 枚被各家系统认可的“网站公章”，盖章用的密码小到一秒就能算出来，谁拿到都能给任意网站做假证书。10 月 17 日被发现后，Chrome 和 Firefox 当天拉黑，eMudhra 18 日作废，Apple 19 日、Microsoft 20 日跟进，Node.js 21 日发版。

当时 Cloudflare 提醒，浏览器之外的程序要一路更新到编程语言这一层，Node.js 就在这一层。Node 内置了 Mozilla 的可信发证机构名单，却没有浏览器那种随时拉黑坏证书的机制，所以用这 8 枚章签出的假证书，旧版 Node 照样放行。这份黑名单对 Node 建立的所有加密连接都生效。修复的提交说明里写道，它和 Go 语言、Electron 拉黑的是同一批。

想测自己的程序还认不认这几枚章，可以用 Mozilla 工程师 Dennis Jackson 做的自查网站：https://t.co/iJDiH3dZ4O

text:
有朋友问，为什么据说是Musk主动向Trump提议给乌克兰星链降速？

这事情每天都有新进展，所以我们先把这个“据说”说清楚。10月16日，英国《每日电讯报》引了四个匿名消息来源，其中有一位欧洲高级官员和两位乌克兰人士，说Musk向Trump提了给乌克兰星链限速的主意，一位来源说Trump同意了，再由五角大楼对星链的军用版星盾执行。

前两天，路透社又引了两位美国官员和一位西方官员的说法，说是白宫里有人通知五角大楼降速，但没说是谁。被点到的人都在往外甩锅。Musk在14日说，星盾（Starshield，星链的军事版）归美国政府控制，速度和用途的限制由美军、最终由总统决定；Trump说他不认为自己或Musk该为此负责；白宫一位官员说电讯报的报道完全不实，星链根本没被降速；国务卿Rubio说政府里没人下过这道令，它是“就那么发生了”。所以“主动提议”有来源，还没被证实，Musk心里怎么想，更没人查清。

能说的，是这件事本身，到底发生了什么。军事上，网络降速不是网页打开慢一点的小问题。10月14日，乌方事先没收到任何通知，接星盾的无人机速度一过每小时160公里左右就断线，而俄罗斯的喷气式无人机和导弹差不多快一倍。Zelensky说，有一批喷气式“沙希德”因此没拦住，给前线送吃的喝的也受了影响。他还说，同样的设备在欧盟国家测试，时速180公里照常连得上，一开进乌克兰，到161就断，这是一次有计划的操作。到18日，他接受NBC采访还说速度没有恢复，决定来自美国政府，SpaceX执行。对照那句“就那么发生了”，很难相信它只是碰巧。

背景是Trump和Zelensky在吵乌克兰打俄罗斯炼油厂的事。写柴油交易那篇我说过，Trump的特使跟乌方讲，柴油安排是为了把俄罗斯拉回谈判桌，也希望乌克兰别再打炼油厂；电讯报还报道，美方警告过基辅，不停手就可能断情报。可Zelensky说，乌军打俄罗斯纵深本来就不用星链，星链在俄罗斯境内也用不了。也就是说，就算限速是冲着炼油厂去的，真被卡住的，是拦截无人机和送给养，压力落在了防守上。风波还没平，16日晚上，Trump又签了行政令，暂停了他上个月刚签署的那部对俄制裁法。

至于Musk为什么会这么做，可以有一个不那么阴暗的解释。他对这场战争早有立场，2022年10月他在推特上发过一个和平方案，克里米亚正式归俄罗斯，被吞并的地区在联合国监督下重新投票；同一年乌军想借星链偷袭塞瓦斯托波尔的俄国舰队，他没同意开通，说那样SpaceX就成了重大战争行为的直接帮手。他怕战争升级，也许是真心的。可让挨打的一方抵抗得弱一点，并不就能让打人的一方停手。电讯报那位来源还说，Musk担心欧洲消费者反弹，这多半只能解释他事后为什么急着说不是自己。

最说的深入一点，现在是技术现在变成了权力。一个人只是发表意见，乌克兰可以不听；可当他同时握着乌克兰一时换不掉的通信，又能直接跟美国总统说上话，他的意见就改变了别人拒绝的代价。写民主那篇我说过两种帮助，凭制度拿到的，可以感谢，也可以投诉；凭大人物照顾拿到的，就得看他的脸色。乌克兰这几年靠的星链，说到底是后一种。波兰外长Sikorski在网上对Musk说，作为你的欧洲客户，我们在看着你；欧盟自己的替代系统IRIS²，要到2030年才能用。

现在荒谬的是，责任蒸发了。据说提议的人说是军方定的，白宫说根本没降速。Rubio除了那句“就那么发生了”，又说那不是故意的，还说乌克兰眼下根本没有星盾的使用权限，可Musk说乌军用的正是星盾，连用的是哪套系统都对不上。财政部长Bessent则警告Zelensky，说话要非常小心。连共和党人也看不下去，众议员Turner在CBS上要求国会调查，说这种事关乎人命，也已经让人丢了命。我在制度论里对制度只要求一件事，人若要问，构要让他问得了，并且要答。乌克兰人问的是最简单的问题，谁下的令，到今天还没有人答。

写柴油那篇的结尾我说，不该拿乌克兰的安全，去换加油站上几美分的降价。这一次换的东西更直接。限速令到现在还找不到签字的人，可Zelensky说没拦住的那些无人机，每一架都有落下去的地方。

1) UPDATE EVERYTHING - main targets are:
a) Browsers - Chrome, Safari, Firefox 
b) OS: : Settings -> General -> software update; Linux: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade; Windows: I think there's a button. Do this for any remote home servers & Openclaw/hermes boxes
c) Phones: Update it all
d) Desktop apps (Slack, Cursor, Discord, etc)

2) Limit web browsing this week: Stay within walled gardens (twitter, youtube, etc); don't click random links this week. Just wait until the patches go through. Do step 1 again after a week.

3) Avoid untrusted Wifi networks until your devices are updated

4) Stay vigilant about phishing emails offering "certificate fixes" or fraud updates

5) Have an iPhone 11-16? TURN BLUETOOTH OFF for the time being until apple patches come through.

6) Code/Dev: UPDATE ALL YOUR REPOS - @charliermarsh has already updated uv 0.13.4 which reacts to the eMudra incident for uv (Python), Typesript according to Claude has equivelant. Tell your agents to go and update all your active repos to update package manager across uv, npm, bun, cargo, etc etc

Bugün de şirketler dolara bağlı kendi stablecoin'lerini çıkarıyor.

ABD bu kâğıt paraları 3 adımda kendi kuralları altına aldı.

Stablecoin yasasında da aynı 3 adım var.

Bessent bugün bunlardan sadece birini söyledi.

Tahminlere göre 1863'ten önce ABD'de 10 binden fazla çeşit kâğıt para vardı.

Bir eyalette basılan para, başka bir eyalette çoğu zaman daha düşük değerle kabul ediliyordu, bazen hiç kabul edilmiyordu.

O dönemde bu kâğıt paraların her biri bankanın imzaladığı bir senetti. 

Senedi imzalayan bankaya götüren kişi, karşılığında altın ya da gümüş alabiliyordu.

Bankalar ise sık sık kasalarındaki altın ve gümüşün yetmeyeceği kadar çok para basıyordu ve birçoğu battı. 

Bir banka batınca, senedi elinde tutan insanlar zarar ediyordu.

Senin cüzdanındaki stablecoin de aynı türden bir senet. Onu çıkaran şirket, her 1 stablecoin için 1 dolar geri vermeyi vaat ediyor.

İlk adım ortak bir kuraldı.

Lincoln'ün yasası, kuruluş iznini federal hükümetten alan ulusal bankaları ve onları denetleyecek OCC'yi kurdu.

Bu bankaların bastığı paraların hepsi aynı görünüyordu, sadece bankanın adı ve yöneticilerin imzaları değişiyordu. 

Bessent'in andığı adım buydu.

ABD'nin stablecoin yasası GENIUS, bu kuralı stablecoin şirketlerine getiriyor. 

ABD'de stablecoin çıkarmak isteyen şirketin izin alması gerekiyor ve kurallar 18 Ocak 2027'de yürürlüğe giriyor.

İkinci adım, senedin arkasına güvence koymaktı.

Ulusal banka, para basmadan önce ABD devletinin tahvilini alıp OCC'ye bırakmak zorundaydı. 

Banka batarsa bu tahviller satılıyor ve senedi elinde tutanlara ödeme yapılıyordu.

ABD o sırada İç Savaş'ın ortasındaydı. 

Yasanın amaçlarından biri de bankalara devletin tahvilini aldırıp savaşın parasını bulmaktı.

GENIUS Yasası'na göre stablecoin'in güvencesi nakit, banka mevduatı ya da ABD devletinin kısa vadeli borcu olan Hazine bonosu olabiliyor.

Üçüncü adım, ulusal banka olmayan bankaların bastığı parayla ilgiliydi. 

1863 yasası, eyaletlerden izin alan bu eski bankaların para basmasını yasaklamadı.

Mart 1865'te ise ABD, bu bankaların bastığı paralara %10 vergi koydu. 

Vergiden sonra yüzlerce eyalet bankası ulusal bankaya dönüştü ve eyaletlerde basılan paralar hızla azaldı.

Stablecoin'de bu vergi yerine bir tarih var. 

18 Temmuz 2028'den itibaren ABD'deki kişilere satış yapan kripto platformları, sadece izinli şirketlerin stablecoin'ini satabilecek.

Piyasa değeri en büyük stablecoin olan USDT'yi çıkaran Tether de 1865'teki eyalet bankalarına benzer bir yol seçti.

Tether bu yıl ocak ayında ABD için USAT adlı ayrı bir stablecoin başlattı. 

USAT'ı ABD'de lisanslı bir banka çıkarıyor.

1863'te parayı bankalar basıyordu, bugün şirketler çıkarıyor. 

Kuralı ise iki seferde de ABD yazdı.

Lincoln'ün yasası ABD'ye ülke çapında ortak bir para verdi. Bugün stablecoin doları internetin her yerine taşıyor.

Parayı kim çıkarırsa çıkarsın, kuralını yazan ülke kazanıyor.

İngiliz ekonomist Walter Bagehot 1873'te şöyle yazmıştı.

Para kendi kendini yönetmez.

ABD bu işi 1863'te kâğıt para için OCC'ye verdi, bugün stablecoin'de de aynı kurum görev alıyor.

最近 𝕏 上面有个很火的韩国 AI 游戏，叫做 《 80 亿分之 1 的人生》。

每次会让玩家随机投胎到全球的某个地方，可能是中国日报韩国美国英国，也可能是完全没听过的小国家。你将会在这个地方经历自己的一生。

看有一个玩家分享的故事很感人：

就是玩家在游戏里面有一个 16 岁的女儿，当时在他出生的那个国家，其实 16 岁要去结婚了，亲戚和镇上的长辈一直催着她结婚。

这位玩家选择顶住压力。即使因此与周围人的关系变差，也要让女儿继续读到大学。

然后在这个玩家的游戏人生结束的时候，他女儿在他的葬礼上说：

「爸爸一直都站在我们这边。」🥲🥲🥲

啊，有种在游戏中，也找到了自己想守护的人的感觉。

当然除了这种感人事件，还有很多抓马的故事。比如从未主动离婚，但由于丧偶结婚了 5 次，玩家本人都觉得是可以报警的程度。

还有那种出生就继承了父母 2 亿的加拿大富豪…（也是抽到 SSR 了）

总之就是，很有趣的一生呢！

text:
Anthropic's @felixrieseberg on the "IKEA effect" in AI: people want to be part of the process, not just get the final result:

"I think a lot about the IKEA effect. This idea that it was a cost-saving measure to send your furniture disassembled, but as it turns out people really appreciate being part of the process."

"I think there's something that translates over into AI where I think the range to which you feel authorship goes up the more you engage with the thing."

"If you just prompt make me art and then you disappear for a week and you come back and it's done, you don't feel much."

"But if you really engage with Claude and you have this back and forth, I'm sort of thinking of the great artists that had workshops and a bunch of really smart assistants. I think that's really where the magic happens."

text:
Regarding potential attacks on energy, food, and water infrastructure, the threat is quite real. Someone is currently probing infra and feeling it out, it is an active threat. Even a little preparation can be helpful, just in case. This comes from the joint cybersecurity advisory released by the NSA and partner agencies on August 19:

'The threat actors are conducting reconnaissance and capability development against U.S.-based Siemens PLC installations using Al-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools. The actors leverage Internet scanning services to find Internet-exposed PLCs running outdated software or that are otherwise poorly protected. The U.S. critical infrastructure sectors most targeted by this threat activity include Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Commercial Facilities. This is not a theoretical risk - it is an active threat. Depending on the specific circumstances, exploitation of poorly protected PLCS could lead to disruption of critical industrial processes, safety incidents, downtime or equipment damage, compromise of sensitive data, compliance violations, and cascading impacts across interconnected systems.'

'Using Al to generate exploitation scripts represents an evolution in threat actor capabilities, dramatically reducing the technical expertise and time required to develop working ICS exploitation scripts and malicious tools. In addition, Al enables adversaries to rapidly leverage additional attack vectors and adapt to defensive measures. Threat actors can easily collect public information about vulnerabilities and weaknesses, find exposed and exploitable PLCs, and use Al-generated scripts to act on that information. If PLCs are exposed to the Internet, they are at high risk for exploitation.

Threat actors are leveraging open source industrial automation libraries - specifically snap7.d11/python-snap7 - combined with Al-assisted scripting to create custom tools that mimic legitimate OT monitoring solutions. These tools provide read/write access to Siemens S7 Series PLC memory, configuration data, and ladder logic programs via the S7comm protocol.'

text:
The most common $AERO bear case: emissions are bigger than revenue.

Gross, they're roughly the same. Last 12 months:

> Revenue to holders: $109.9M
> Emissions: $110.1M

Net, the picture changes.

65% of emissions ($71.3M) were locked right back into veAERO. Net of re-locks, revenue covered net emissions 2.8x.

The part holders should watch: the re-lock rate is falling. It dropped to 30% in Q3, and net coverage fell to 1.3x.

In July and August, net emissions exceeded revenue, and October is tracking the same way so far.

@BautiDeFi is right that the key number for Aerodrome is how much in fees each $1 of emissions generates. But it also depends on how much of those emissions get locked again.

That's the real test for @aeroxyz's Predictive Allocation: $1+ in fees per $1 of emissions, with recipients still choosing to lock.

text:
现在还是太忙，没时间大块写理论。我抽空简单回复。

只要愿意深入到系统结构层次讨论问题，就好办得多。说明你有思考问题的品味。但从你的回复来看，你还不太了解系统论或者系统思维，因为你把国家和社会的结构变化想得太容易了。之所以系统思维比较有力量，就是因为系统结构有很强的稳定性，可以成为分析问题的一个较为稳定的基础。你别说国家，就是个人身上形成的结构，也极难改变。

第一个就是，系统有很强的惰性，或者稳定性。你可以替换掉系统里很多的元素，但是只要核心关系和连接不变，它还是原来那个系统，还是会一遍又一遍产生出类似的行为。就比如科技创新、外贸、个别特立独行的领导人，这些对于普通人一生中影响巨大的因素，实际上在一个宏观结构里，都是无关大局的元素而已，旧的换新的，疯的换癫的，其实那个结构其实一直没变。你不能一看到发生了什么科技创新，或者某某人来了个新政，就以为结构变了。那是低估了结构的稳定性。你比如说，互联网的兴起，这个事够大吧，但是其实它没有改变美国和中国的底层系统结构。因此你就不能看到一点变化，就很乐观的说结构要变了。结构如果那么容易变，那系统论就没有意义了。

第二，某些系统有很强的韧性。这种系统结构一旦形成，总是能够抵抗变化，回到原来那个结构。比如中国的这种一人专制大一统集权国家的底层结构可以说秦皇汉武以后就没有变过。这个过程中发生过多次崩溃，也有多次改革，在这些崩溃和改革当中，你都可以说结构真的变了。但是每次隔一段时间就复原。最近这一千年，大的就有宋元之变、明清之变、民国之变，再到 40 年改革开放，其实都是结构变革，但是这些变革形成的结构不稳定，隔一段时间还会回归到那个最稳定的结构上，就是一人集权的大一统专制。1980 年代金观涛写过一本书，就是从系统论来分析中国的超稳定结构。这说明什么呢？说明在这个结构之上还有一个元结构，那个元结构存在一个调节回路，总是能把中国的社会复原成一人集权的大一统专制结构上。你只要想保持由中央派出代表到地方进行治理、以文书作为主要治理机制这样一个郡县制文治的机制，那么在一个幅员辽阔、人口众多、文化和意识形态多样化的国家里，只有这个一人集权制是最稳定的，而且在一人集权制当中，又以血缘继承的皇帝制度是最稳定的。这个不是人的问题，也不是科技的问题，而是系统结构决定了的。所以每次你只要偏离这个结构，就会出现权力斗争、地方割据甚至战乱。其实过去十几年，就是中国从一个不那么稳定的结构回归一个相对稳定的结构的过程，是那个超稳定的元系统发挥作用了。而这个稳定点一旦达到，这个系统就会确定性地产生类似的行为，比如必须束缚民众的头脑，必须抑制非国有部门的经济活力和创造力，必须由中央财政供养庞大的官僚集团和军队，必须不断增加税赋。这些都是结构决定的。

美国也有美国的超稳定结构，它的核心架构也很难撼动。比如曾经有一段时间我觉得 1944 年建立和 1971 年放弃布雷顿货币体系，这是结构变革，后来才理解，其实这么大的事都算不上结构变革，只是关键存量水平的变化，导致本来次要的回路显性化了，按毛泽东的非常粗糙的系统思考直觉来说，就是次要矛盾上升为主要矛盾。像你所说的牛人、科技、AI 什么的，就更是小儿科，只会被这种结构消化，不会改变结构本身。比特币和区块链是真的有改变结构的能力，但是你也看到这个系统是怎么应对的了。

当然我也承认，对个人来说，哪怕宏观结构不变，一些小小的湍流逆流，也足以改变你的一生。但是既然是湍流逆流，就具有极强的不确定性，特别如果你观察到一些与这个结构背离的现象，那么可以很有把握的说，都是系统的扰动因素，最终会被系统的反馈闭环给抑制住。比如我就可以断言，现在为了搞新质生产力，给一部分所谓的民营公司很大的支持，让一些科技精英看上去风风光光。虽然这是出于高层自己的判断和决定，但这个与整个系统就是矛盾的，决策层最后一定会发现这样搞不行，得反手抑制，这些科技精英大多数都会不得善终，这不是哪个人的认识问题，也不是谁的品质问题，这是系统结构决定的。目前还没变，只是因为领导人“耐心”的存量还没有消耗完。

这个讨论就到这里，已经耗费我太多时间。现在美国有一些人提出来，AI 时代最重要的思维方式就是系统思维，我非常认同，因为 AI 是一个新的改变系统的杠杆工具。但到底多有用，还得观察。你要是对系统论感兴趣，建议系统的学习一下，肯定有收获。这个理论真的有用，而且有很多部分反直觉，不能想当然。

text:
Anthropic 推出 Claude Duet，7 x 24小时“主动型Agent”

Claude Duet 发布当天，OpenAI 的 Tibo 来到评论区，替自家的 Dot 打了个招呼：

“Dot，认识一下 Duet。Duet，认识一下 Dot。你们俩好好相处。”

继 Grok Bot、Meta Muse、OpenAI Dots 之后，Anthropic 也加入了Personal Agent 的竞争。

1、主动找你汇报，也能在你离开后继续工作

Duet 基于 Opus 5.5，主要面向专业人士和小企业主。它每天早上发送晨报，汇总已连接应用的重要事项，并判断哪些需要用户关注、哪些可以稍后处理。

官方披露的早期案例里，品牌策略师 Mya Dalton 有一通客户电话紧挨着航班起飞。Duet 在准备会前简报时发现了这个安排，主动提出调整时间。

它还配有自己的云端虚拟机和浏览器。用户关掉电脑、离开手机后，交代过的任务仍可以继续推进。

2、6000 多个连接器和插件，把不同软件里的工作接起来

Duet 可以沿用 Claude 账户里的记忆、技能和已连接应用，并调用 Claude Marketplace 中超过 6000 个连接器和插件。

例如，从 Stripe 找出未付发票并起草催款信，在 Gusto 中准备工资数据，通过 Docusign 发送待审核和签署的协议，或者搭建经营看板、制作财务预测和网页应用。

官方案例中，一位管理约 110 名员工的餐饮连锁店老板，已将它用于会计、客服、营销和逐店梳理发票。

3、关键操作，仍要本人批准

发送消息、付款、签署文件或删除内容前，Duet 会展示准备执行的操作，等待用户确认。证券交易和账户间转账，即使得到批准也不在允许范围内。

企业采购可以通过 Stripe 的 Link 或 Shopify 的 Shop Pay 完成。其中 Link 会要求用户批准支出，再使用虚拟卡付款。

4、首批开放有门槛，后台工作也消耗额度

目前是研究预览，首批通过候补名单向美国 Pro、Max 用户开放，支持 iOS、Android 和网页端，包含在现有订阅中。

Duet 通常每隔数小时检查一次已连接账户，后台检查与任务执行都计入套餐用量。官方也说明，早期版本仍可能误判对话或事情的紧急程度，目前尚不能向用户展示它的浏览器。

5、71 天，四款 Personal Agent 接连亮相

8 月 11 日，Grok Bot 开放测试；9 月 8 日，Meta 推出 Muse；9 月 29 日，OpenAI 发布 Dots；10 月 21 日，Claude Duet 进入研究预览。

从第一款到第四款，只隔了 71 天。几家的定位和权限不同，但都给 Agent 配上了云端电脑，让它跨应用执行任务，并在用户离开后继续工作。

从这些产品的设计看，各家正在争取同一种使用习惯：用户把邮箱、日历和业务系统接进来，把项目背景持续留在这里，再将越来越完整的工作交给同一个 Agent。

谁能稳定交付、少让用户来回补充和收尾，谁就更有机会成为下一次交代工作时的首选。从 Chatbot 到 Personal Agent，AI 的应用方向正在越来越走进人类生活，未来已来。

quoted_text:
OpenAI 买了一家 AI 药企，但不是设计分子的环节

OpenAI 收购了 Orchestra Bio，并进自家的生命科学项目 Rosalind。
这家公司不碰分子生成，做的事看着很传统：用 AI Agent 帮药企盯试验排期、临床进度，协调生产延误。

官方公告里说：一款新药，平均还要走 10 到 15 年。
大模型公司进医药，最先吃下的不是科学，是运营。

1、团队什么来头

CEO Ashoka Rajendra，Benchling 前开发与生产产品负责人。
- Benchling 是生物医药研发软件的龙头，2021 年 F 轮估值 61 亿美元，官方称有 1300 多家生物技术公司在用，包括默克、Moderna、赛诺菲，用来记实验、管样本和数据。
- 他做的正是药从实验室走向生产那一段的软件。药企在哪脱节、在哪漏钱，他看得最清楚。

CTO Andy Xu，Numenta 前工程副总裁。
- Numenta 是 Palm 创始人 Jeff Hawkins 2005 年创办的公司，从脑科学出发做 AI，后来主攻让模型推理更快、更省，官方称能把推理提速 10 到 100 倍以上。
- 排期和调度这种活，每天要跑大量推理，成本压不下来就用不起。

一个懂药企流程，一个懂把系统跑便宜。

2、瓶颈不在算法

分子设计热闹了好几年，大家以为 AI 能很快算出新药。
但算出来之后，合成、动物实验、三期临床，一步都省不掉。
物理世界的试错，算法替不了。

3、科学决定上限，脏活决定死活

新药研发的时间，大量耗在内部摩擦上：部门沟通脱节，外包研究机构排期延误，放大生产时断档。
把从发现到临床之间这层信息断层理顺，Agent 现在就能省出真金白银。

我觉得 OpenAI 这笔投资要的还有入口和数据。
只跑分子模型的工具，很难进药企的核心决策；接管了临床和生产的调度，药企每天真实的工作流数据，就从它这里过。

4、先啃流程脏活，再图科学圣杯。

分子设计卖的是十几年后的彩票。
流程协调卖的是明天的现金账本。

大家以为大模型进药企会先当爱因斯坦，结果它先去当了项目经理。

我去，这个大模型有点意思啊！
MemT 1.0 ：全球首个"记忆原生"  大模型（MoE构架）

现在 ChatGPT 、Claude Codex 都支持记忆，但都记在模型外部（记忆库/对话历史），用时检索注入上下文。

记忆来源于用户要求和对话自动保存，记再多，模型本身不会变，只是能看到更多信息。

MemT 1.0 直接把记忆做到模型内部，写入、保持、更新、读取全纳入模型计算过程。

模型会从用户的交互、指导、反馈纠错中积累经验，变成模型可以学习的能力，实现模型自我反思、进化。

完全是为为 RSI（递归自我改进）铺路啊！

ChatGPT 等模型的记忆可类比为 "外挂笔记本"，写下来记住，需要时再翻看，记住的是信息。

MemT 1.0 的记忆是更像 "大脑中的经验"，从纠错中学，下次就不犯错了，沉淀的是能力。

这好像才是更像人类大脑的长期记忆系统。

第二条论文中的技术解读和实验，感觉这开拓了一个解决记忆问题的新思路，很有价值。

I've been using Claude Duet the last couple hours and I'll say this:

It's EXCELLENT

The multi tasking is probably the best in the space

You get one simple thread you can talk to, and as you give it commands and prompts, it automatically spins up tasks on a list for you

So instead of having to manage a ton of side chats that could get long or confusing, you have 1 chat, but it makes 'task' threads automatically that you can watch and monitor

This allows you to just keep brain dumping ideas and tasks into the one thread, and not have to worry about the agent getting confused. The agent just will manage all the tasks for you

Very similar to Claude Code's new 'projects' feature which was probably a beta test for this

The coding was great. Built me a bunch of PRs quickly I was able to review. 

Proactivity was fantastic too. Came up with a bunch of tasks on its own and just asked me for the go ahead

As expected it's also fantastic to talk to. Claude has long been the best model to converse with (outside Opus 5) and the carries over to Claude Duet

Really pleased with the product, even in research preview. Very excited to see where it goes from here

Definitely sign up for the wait list

ICYMI, Solana and Ethereum are working on different bottlenecks.

@Solana targets faster finality; @Ethereum targets more execution capacity. Here's the TL; DR:

- Alpenglow (Solana):

Mainnet planned Oct 21 (epoch 1064), aiming to cut finality from ~12.8s to ~150ms. Phase 1 ships Votor (replaces TowerBFT); Rotor comes later. Voting fees shift to a burned 0.8 SOL/epoch admission fee.

- Glamsterdam (Ethereum):

Live on Sepolia; Hoodi scheduled Oct 26 with a 200M gas limit; mainnet date TBD. Key changes: ePBS in-protocol builder/proposer separation, and block-level access lists for more parallelism.

The net effect is palpable, faster finality helps payments/trading; more capacity supports higher demand and heavy on-chain activities like HFT, AI inferences, games and even more.

Everything is getting more autonomous. Except us.

When @jesseldn went out to raise his newest fund, he built the strategy around one word: autonomy.

But getting there was a long and circuitous route.

In 2016, @usv invested in Jesse’s company Mediachain. That’s given us the chance to work together for a decade, including his time at @a16zcrypto and now at @variantfund .

The through line is a belief that technology should give people more control over their lives.

In this week’s episode of The Slow Hunch, we trace that belief back to Jesse’s humble beginnings as an internet pirate and talk about what it will take for AI to fulfill that promise.

Jesse is consistently one of the most cogent thinkers I get the chance to speak with, and I think you’ll enjoy our chat.

text:
> Am I being a schizo to think that this could be a Chinese government ploy
Yes. Meds, now.
But there does exist a cynical read of DeepSeek's moves. Because V4.1 line is very strong, cheap and has zero strings attached, they destroy the case for hosting anything like K3 ($3/$15) by Western partners, so starve their domestic rivals of revenue. Moreover DeepInfer is useless for anything not shaped just like V4.1 (so, it'll be DeepSeek's models and finetunes). They also make compute ownership more valuable by having created mutual knowledge about its profitability even at "shockingly low" prices. Frontier labs and hyperscalers already understood how valuable compute is, so they can't go harder on securing allocation, but neoclouds will now ask premium.
Flash, in effect, requires a full NVL72 GB200 rack to hit these margins. V4.1 Pro and Ultra (hypothetical for now) will make the issue even more pronounced. When you need a whole cluster to run an 8T DeepSeek model efficiently, *but* it prints you like $40/GPU/hour, this removes a lot of colocated GPUs from easy access. And DeepSeek had little hope to tap into this pool, so they lose nothing, gain mindshare and keep building their new power base around Ascend, which will also become increasingly Whale-shaped due to co-design. In the end, DeepSeek will have defined the entire upstream and downstream AI ecosystem in China, harvesting a tiny slice of the profit in the process.

Heavenly Demon Sage 梁圣, ruthless in his benevolence…

text:
🚨PSA: I almost got wrecked🚨

Sharing the story to hopefully help nobody else get wrecked. DOUBLE CHECK YOUR @ensdomains NOW. 

I’ve used 7605.eth (my punk #) as the ENS for my main collection for a few years now. Usually I’m good about remembering to renew it but there’s been a lot going on and I forgot a couple months back. Yesterday I was extending a loan on @gondixyz and needed an additional 400 USDC to cover the origination. I went to my Coinbase and did what I’ve done many times before and sent 400 USDC to 7605.eth. After a few minutes of it not arriving I started to look into it and it took me a minute to figure out what happened. I put 7605.eth into etherscan and everything seemed normal at first, address looked like what I expected, but then I noticed a transfer out to a fatleopard.eth. I freaked out thinking my wallet was compromised, then noticed an ENS transaction. Went to https://t.co/eeKxy5vgOw and found that 54 days ago a wallet address with the same 5 beginning characters as mine (0x862) had registered the domain after it expired. 

I’m so used to checking those first 4-5 digits and assuming all is well so this has been a huge lesson learned. I’m extremely lucky to have only lost $400, it could have been a massive loss. I’m also very used to sending NFTs I buy from my hot wallet to this wallet using the 7605.eth ENS so I’m very lucky to have not purchased and moved anything in the last few weeks and to catch it before I did. 

If you use an ens domain for any important wallets make sure to remember the registration deadlines and stay on top of them. And get into the habit of checking more than those first 5 digits. 

Stay safe out there friends ❤️

text:
Agentic commerce seems to have developed with two stacks - text-based CLI and app-based GUI that can be mixed and matched. Some observations:

1/ Overall, CLI is more efficient, but GUI is more compatible. The CLI wave seemed to be triggered earlier in the year by agents such as Claude Code/OpenClaw/Hermes, whereas the GUI wave is much recent, with agents such as Instinct/Muse/Grokbot etc.

2/ In terms of payment volumes, today we see that CLI based systems such as x402 and MPP are still extremely early - x402 has a lifetime tx vol of 56M since its release over the past year, MPP has <1M tx vol in past 6mos, while Instinct claims to already have achieved 1B annualized tx vol.

3/ One big reason may be the "big-ticket" purchases (eg. buying $3000 Macbook) are primarily still processed through traditional checkout systems, in which GUI's compatibility advantage will be massive - all the merchants already operate on GUIs

4/ However, this may be a temporary transition phase. GUI and apps were built for humans, not agents. As agents become the dominant form of Internet traffic, we will see much more agent-to-agent communication - my Muse/Grokbot may communicate/relay tasks to Doordash or United's customer agent. A single transaction chain may be H -> A -> A -> A -> H.

5/ In the same way we've seen agents prefer Markdown files over HTML files, we'll like see that agents will prefer CLI solutions over GUI solutions for A2A. Once A2A activity becomes a dominant slice of Internet traffic, this will change the channel/payment/discovery layers of the Internet.

6/ In the future, both stacks will likely continue to exist - in the same way headless CLI and GUI based OS both exist. Generalist consumer agents will likely be continually be dominated by GUI solutions, while customized workflow agents and complex A2A workflows will likely lean on CLI solutions for efficiency.

text:
Procedural Terrains v2.0.0 is finally OUT! 🌍🚀

This is probably one of the biggest updates I've worked on so far, bringing a lot of new features, visual improvements, optimizations, and something I've wanted to do for quite a while :)

First, introducing Mini Terrains! 🏝️

You can now generate your own little procedural 3D dioramas!

• Square or circular terrains with customizable cutaway bases
• Procedural presets and compositions
• Customizable vegetation, water, clouds and props
• Dedicated controls for creating small, detailed environments

A big visual update too! ☁️💧
I've been reworking quite a few rendering systems:
• New Stylized, Realistic, Volumetric and Cinematic water shaders
• Improved reflections, refraction, shoreline foam and underwater effects
• Animated underwater caustics
• Reworked volumetric clouds with better shapes, lighting, erosion and cloud shadows
• Various lighting and atmosphere improvements

And something completely new: Procedural Terrains is now an npm package! 📦

Following feedback from @somaco_sf and others, I've been working on making the engine reusable outside the editor.

You can now integrate procedural terrain generation directly into your own Three.js applications!
The package supports finite, infinite, planetary and Mini terrains, along with water, clouds, materials and export APIs.

https://t.co/Z8BUTMlw1N

I've also added a dedicated documentation section with an API reference, code examples, and an interactive Playground where you can write and run terrain code directly in your browser!
Other changes in v2.0.0:

• Updated Unity plugin (0.4.0-alpha.2) and Blender add-on (0.4.1)
• New props and customization options
• Real-world terrain improvements, including city markers, routes and navigation tools
• Performance optimizations, energy-saving options and an experimental spatial upscaler
• Improved mobile support and UI / UX
• French and English language support
• A new Windows portable build
• Lots of bug fixes and smaller refinements!

The goal has always been to make Procedural Terrains useful for both artists and developers, and this update is a pretty big step in that direction.

There's still plenty I'd like to improve and add, but I'm really happy with how far this project has come :)

Thank you to everyone who has been following the project, sharing feedback, reporting bugs or contributing. It really means a lot! ❤️

And as always, #ThreeJS carries :)

Give it a try and let me know what you think!

At @Meta, 84% of engineers who've never worked anywhere else are at Senior level+ (E5 and above)

For those who joined Meta from other companies, it's 40% (when matching exact years of experience).

At Staff level+ (E6 and above), past the terminal level at Meta, the trend holds as well.

We looked at https://t.co/q2NOapsdJO data for US software engineers with 4-12 years of experience. Comparing ppl who've spent their entire career at one company with those who joined after 2+ years elsewhere, adjusted to match years of experience.

@Google's very similar. 61% of homegrown engineers are Senior+, vs 29% of outside hires. Microsoft is 47% vs 25%.

Engineers who've spent their whole career at these companies are ~2x as likely to be Senior or above.

Bloomberg is close to even (81% vs 78%). Intel too (34% vs 30%).

Some of this is who sticks around ofc. Ppl who get promoted are generally more likely to stay, while those who don't grow, leave.

That said, if you do have to switch, a big comp increase can still come with a downlevel.

Make sure you're coming in at your desired level on day 1. “You can get promoted once you're here” is never guaranteed.

quoted_text:
I believe Elon Musk is planning on using the Retaliator strategy to deal with aggression from the Democrats.

The Retaliator strategy is a behavior in evolutionary game theory that begins peacefully but fiercely defends itself if attacked. A Retaliator always starts an encounter acting like a cooperative 'Dove,' but if its opponent escalates the conflict, it immediately switches to an aggressive 'Hawk' tactic to fight back. 

If the opponent backs down and becomes peaceful again, the Retaliator matches that shift and reverts to a Dove. This conditional flexibility allows Retaliators to cooperate efficiently with peaceful neighbors while successfully punishing bullies and predators without being exploited.

It combines a preference for peace with a credible willingness to retaliate, and in competitive terms outperforms both indiscriminate aggression and unconditional submission.

When a Retaliator meets a Bully (e.g., the Democrat Party), the interaction quickly exposes the Bully's empty bluff. The Bully begins the encounter aggressively by playing like a Hawk, which instantly triggers the Retaliator to abandon its peaceful default and fight back fiercely. 

Because a Bully usually retreats when faced with real aggression, it panics and flees when the Retaliator pushes back with sufficient force. As a result, the Retaliator wins the entire resource with a low risk of injury, dominating the Bully and driving it toward evolutionary extinction. 

The Doves benefit by from being around a Retaliator as well, gaining friendly interactions with it, and protection against bullies. 

The Retaliator's strength lies not in seeking conflict, but in making exploitation unprofitable and unfounded agression costly. It cooperates whenever cooperation is possible, fights decisively when fighting becomes necessary, and stops fighting as soon as the threat has passed. In evolutionary terms, its success comes from aligning peaceful intentions with effective deterrence, and a willingness to use extreme measures when necessary. 

It's the right choice.

text:
Here’s another way to think about it:

Bitcoin, Zcash, etc. are vertically integrated in the sense that they have their own L1s. The risk is that their underlying infrastructure may struggle to scale to the throughput and performance required for the global demand of p2p non-sovereign electronic cash, while also supporting a native DeFi ecosystem that doesn’t require wrapping to other networks (trusted third parties, defeating the purpose).

Ore chose to not build its own L1, and instead inherits Solana’s transaction throughput, performance improvements, and rapidly expanding DeFi ecosystem (without having to wrap through trusted third parties).

By effectively outsourcing infrastructure development to Anza and the broader Solana ecosystem, Ore can focus its resources entirely on building future-proof money: immutably freezing core components of the protocol, the reserve, quantum resistance, etc.

Yes Ore is now relying on Solana's continued existence, censorship resistant infra, and continued performance improvements.

An argument could be made though that it is more likely that Bitcoin scalability is neglected and/or Zcash fails to grow a native DeFi eco vs Solana failing as infra+eco for Ore.

Perhaps Ore found a compelling point on the tradeoff spectrum.

强烈建议大家都配置一款自己的 Personal agent，真是能够极大地提高生产力和生活幸福感。给大家分享一下我的 Grok Bot 配置（无论是 Muse、Today AI 还是 Grok Bot，或者是喜欢自定义的 OpenClaw、Hermes）

主体上分为出海站点运营、自媒体运营、每周的 AI 大事总结，以及计划清单 Bot

出海站点运营Bot负责监控新词、监控我的网站的流量状态、每天自动上外链(通过插件)并汇报今天收入情况

自媒体运营 Bot 负责监控热点，监控我喜欢的几个博主发的内容，帮我审核我的小红书和抖音发布视频的流量状态

每周的 AI 大事总结bot，负责从 X 上总结每周发生的 AI 大事件。因为现在 Grok Bot 已经和 X 深度打通了，所以检索也不会花 API 额度

计划清单 bot 我觉得挺有用的。我想到什么计划都会发给它作为待办，并告诉它哪些需要定时推送给我。

原本我也用过很多计划清单（比如滴答清单这种 App），但它们往往只能设置一个完成时限；如果我没完成，可能就直接显示过期，并不会多次重复提醒。

但 bot 可以针对我没完成的事项定时提醒，这样我就能记住还有什么没做，用来规划日常很好用

而且我现在基本已经不怎么刷推特了，基本全是 Bot 给我推送我筛选好的博主。
他们发什么只需要看一下 Bot 给我的推送内容即可；如果感兴趣，我再点进去仔细看

关于额度，可能是因为我的 Cursor Ultra 的原因，现在的 Grok Bot 额度异常耐用，基本每天做很多事情都消耗不到 10%

最后，我觉得 Grok Bot 好用的原因：

1. 响应快。
2. 相比我自己去自定义一个需要我自己不断 update 的 Hermes 或 OpenClaw，Grok Bot 这种付费产品，其团队提供的服务显然更加稳定且易用（这也是我放弃 OpenClaw 和 Hermes 的原因）。
author: Pluvio9yte
quoted_text:
后面 AI 产品的机会在于 Personal Agent，谁能做好、宣发好，谁就有未来市场的主导权。

刚过去的 9 月，AI 圈几乎被 Personal Agent 刷屏了： Meta Muse 登顶美榜、Today AI 亮相、Manus 推出 Cue、OpenAI 上线 Dots，国内大厂全线跟进……

很多人以为又是一个新概念炒作，但我今天听了一个播客，听完业内人的复盘，才发现背后的演进脉络极其清晰。
简单提炼核心要点，以及我的一些思考：

时间演变顺序：
📈2023 年（Chatbot）：ChatGPT 诞生，定义了问答对话交互；
📈2024~2025 年（任务型 Agent）：Manus 展示了通用 Agent 能力，各类编程/工作流 Agent 爆发，重点在「帮你干活」；
📈2026 年初（生活化探索）：OpenClaw 等出现，让行业意识到「每个人需要一个 24 小时在线的生活助理」；
📈2026 年 9 月（Personal Agent 破圈）：从工具走向陪伴与日常协作者。

为什么在 Muse 和 Grok Bot 之前，那么多 Personal Agent（比如 OpenClaw 和 Manus）都没有破圈呢？

总结公式：品类爆发公式 = 技术的渐进成熟 + 让人看见可能性的样品（OpenClaw）+ 拥有顶级渠道与宣发势能的巨头（Meta）

这也是为什么后面 AI 产品的机会在于 personal agent 的原因：当基础大模型能力趋同时，谁能成为用户长期的 Personal Agent，取决于谁拥有一整套个人生活记忆库。

这种转移成本极高，我们都不会换掉一个用了很久的 Personal Agent。比如我现在，在 Muse 之前我就重度使用 Grok Bot，那我在没有看到 Muse 对 Grok Bot 有压倒性优势之前，是不会更换的

quoted_text:
前几天看了赛克（@Saccc_c）用 Opus 5.5 做《小王子》的教程，我尝试把陶渊明的《桃花源记》做成一个明亮的第三人称探险小游戏，Opus 5.5 加 3D 模型确实能够做出可玩的游戏了

用到的工具：Claude Code（Opus 5.5）、@ViggleAI 的 PINOC（JST-2），再加一个网页 3D 引擎。

大体是这么做的👇

① 先写策划
五幕直接对着原文：缘溪行 → 忽逢桃花林 → 山有小口，仿佛若有光 → 豁然开朗，桃源村 → 处处志之，不复得路。

② 再出概念图
用 AI 出全景设定、关键画面和角色三视图，这里我用的是 Codex 内置的生图功能。画面参考《小王子》的明亮感，人物参考《风之旅人》《光·遇》：渔郎戴竹斗笠、披稻草蓑衣，再加一条桃红色的长围巾。

③ 角色交给 PINOC
渔郎、老翁、小孩，把正、侧、背三视图丢进 PINOC，出来就是自带骨骼的 3D 高斯泼溅角色。
走、跑、挥手、点头直接从动作库里拿；坐下吃饭、作揖、小孩蹦跳这些用文字生成。
PINOC MCP 接进 Claude Code 之后，这些都是 Claude 自己去调。

④ 搭场景
远处的桃花山谷用 PINOC 的场景生成。近处的小溪、小路、桃树，还有几万簇随风摆动的草、雏菊、薰衣草、蕨类，都是 Claude 写程序搭出来的。

⑤ 对标迭代（最关键的一步）
学赛克的做法：固定几个机位，每改一轮就截图，和《小王子》并排对比，看差在哪，再改下一轮。光溪畔桃林这一个小场景就迭代了八轮，从一开始的"塑料感"改到现在这样。

最大的感受：一个人加上 Claude 和 PINOC，一天就能做出一个明亮、能玩的小世界

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
I didn't predict and do not predict defense running ahead of offense automatically. I predict cybersecurity will be endgame defense-favoring but the transition will be hard. In particular, "good guys find vulns in already-released software before the bad guys do" is not a defense-favoring game. Making the game defense-favoring requires deeper shifts in methodology including formal verification, aggressive TCB minimization, etc, and we've only barely started making those transitions.

(This distinction is a big reason why I continue to be friendly toward slowdowns/pauses, and we need >1% of GDP going toward cyber + bio + physical world hardening)

text:
The AI-driven surge in vulnerability discovery and exploitation has begun. Three indicators from the past few weeks:

1. chatter that incident response firms are fully booked and overwhelmed with business (meaning breaches are happening even if we don’t see headlines)

2. a major certificate authority compromise (eMudhra)

3. the massive PHP vulnerabilities discussed today (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) 
 
AI is either directly discovering the vulnerabilities or is a means to rapidly exploit the issue at scale and low cost. The combination of low cost and scale means industries that skated under the radar because of attacker interest / ROI are now squarely in the attack crosshairs.

This applies to all companies, big and small. You are not safe because “hackers won’t come after industry XYZ”. They will.

The defensive needs are clear. We need to migrate from human-driven cyber defense to defense at the speed of computers. This is the position I laid out in December when I spoke to the House Homeland Security Committee subcommittee in DC about the threat of AI-powered cybersecurity attacks.

What should organizations do today?
This is not an exercise in being clever. Rather the need is to be comprehensive.

1. Understand your exposure - Establish an automated inventory of your packages, libraries, operating systems, full tech stack, etc.

2. Understand when you need to respond - Build automated monitoring systems that monitor public CVEs and cybersecurity chatter and cross-reference this with your inventory. Response time is moving from days to hours to minutes. You need automation and alerting.

3. Mobilize and plan for response - The issue will inevitably hit at 2am. How will you mobilize the right team members? Can you bring the system offline in moments (operationally, and do you have internal authorization)? What team members are needed? Do you have reliable paging and response? Practice now.

4. Reduce Attack Surface & fix issues you can now - AI chaining is increasingly tying together otherwise low-risk issues into critical outcomes. This means you either need to comprehensively analyze all known vulns to better understand if a low is actually a high risk issue. Or, lacking this capability, be more aggressive to fix known issues. One simple way to fix issues - remove the access and exposure. A device that can’t be reached is much harder to exploit!

This is not business as usual. Your cybersecurity posture and strategy over the next 18 months are an opportunity to survive when your competition fails (and they may no longer be a competitor at that point). 
 
If you’ve been saying “We take cybersecurity seriously...” This is your chance to put your money where your mouth is.

text: It's striking that this vulnerability was found by Sol and Argon rather than being found and fixed in the wake of Mythos 6mo ago. Seems like a heavy strike against the "defense will run ahead of offense" theory, especially give that domains like bio are much harsher than cyber.
author: So8res
quoted_text:
AI systems found a working server takeover exploit in PHP, one of the most critical cybersecurity issues in recent memory!

- The vulnerability was found using a mix of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon, plus human expertise

- PHP is the programming language behind ~70% of websites, most notably Wordpress

- The bugs sit in PHP itself, so nearly every PHP site is exposed no matter how well its own code is written. Merely running PHP itself is the risk

- The vulnerability lets an attacker with no login either run code on a server or read its memory, which can hold passwords, session tokens, API keys, or other secrets

- The flaw is from from how PHP cleans up when a request crashes after running out of memory: corrupted state is left behind and the next request can pick it up. An attacker can force that memory crash with a crafted upload, so even a bare page on a vulnerable version can be taken over.

text:
I didn't predict and do not predict defense running ahead of offense automatically. I predict cybersecurity will be endgame defense-favoring but the transition will be hard. In particular, "good guys find vulns in already-released software before the bad guys do" is not a defense-favoring game. Making the game defense-favoring requires deeper shifts in methodology including formal verification, aggressive TCB minimization, etc, and we've only barely started making those transitions.

(This distinction is a big reason why I continue to be friendly toward slowdowns/pauses, and we need >1% of GDP going toward cyber + bio + physical world hardening)

text:
在硅谷待久了，我发现一件很有意思的事：

年薪高、财富自由和人生自由，其实是三件完全不同的事。

硅谷大厂的工程师，年薪二三十万美元，甚至四五十万美元，并不稀奇。

但收入高，不代表自由。

房贷、孩子、家庭开支，再加上每天开不完的会、做不完的项目，看起来收入很高，实际上时间还是属于公司的。

后来我发现，硅谷有些人走的是另外一条路。

比如 Zoom 的创始人袁征（Eric Yuan）。

他原来是 Cisco 的工程副总裁，管理着数百人的团队。

这已经是很多工程师职业生涯的天花板了。

但他一直觉得，当时的视频会议软件还可以做得更好。他在公司内部推动自己的想法，却没能得到想要的支持。

2011 年，他干脆离职，自己创办了 Zoom。

创业初期，很多投资人并不看好，觉得视频会议市场已经挤满了竞争者。

结果2019年，Zoom 上市，袁征成了亿万富豪。

再比如 NVIDIA 的黄仁勋。

他原来在 LSI Logic 工作，而且工作得很开心。

后来，两位朋友找到他，邀请他一起创业。

三个人经常坐在圣何塞一家 Denny’s 餐厅里，一边喝咖啡，一边讨论到底能做什么。

1993年，他们创办了 NVIDIA。

谁能想到，当年在餐厅里讨论出来的一家公司，后来会成为全球 AI 浪潮中最重要的企业之一？

这两个故事让我想到硅谷很有意思的一点：

打工，主要是出售自己的时间和能力；创业，则有机会拥有一份能够持续增长的资产。

当然，中间还有一条路：加入早期创业公司，拿股票。

如果公司成功上市，员工也可能获得几百万甚至上千万美元的财富。

这当然已经非常成功了。

但财富自由和时间自由，未必是一回事。

你可能不缺钱了，却仍然有做不完的工作、开不完的会。

而自己创业，虽然风险大得多，失败的概率也高得多，但一旦把生意做起来，建立起团队和系统，就有机会同时获得财富和时间上的选择权。

这也是为什么，我觉得硅谷最值得体验的，不只是那些大公司的办公室。

而是各种创业者聚会、Pitch Day、Demo Day、Founder Dinner。

因为你会发现，这里很多人关心的，不只是下一份工作能拿多少工资。

他们还在思考：

有没有可能，不再只是为别人创造价值，而是拥有一份真正属于自己的事业？

当然，创业不一定比打工更自由，尤其在最初几年，往往更辛苦。

但它提供了另一种可能性。

我觉得普通人来硅谷，最值得感受的，就是这种氛围。

一个人真正的自由，不是年薪有多高，而是有一天，可以自己决定时间花在哪里，人生往哪个方向走。

text:
这可能是 Delphi Digital 最近最好的一篇长文：《庄家通吃：为什么投机是未来十年的主题》。

小编看完觉得，重点并不在于它投研了什么新赛道，更像是一种姿态和明示：

别再装价值投资了，大方承认“投机”就是这个时代的刚需。而在一个全民皆赌的时代，最聪明的策略不是去牌桌上挑筹码，你最好直接买下赌场本身。

文章里几个非常刺骨的洞察，以及大量值得细品的数据：

1. 为什么所有人都在赌？因为“正常路径”已经失效

历史上的投机大多由两种引擎驱动：
a.新技术带来的“基建狂热”，如当年的铁路、现在的 AI；
b.阶层固化和法币贬值逼出来的“彩票绝望”,赌一把算了。

而现在，这两个引擎在历史上首次同时全速运转。

对年轻人来说，靠打工存钱买房的传统社会契约已经破产；目前美国首次购房者的中位年龄创下了 40 岁的历史新高，占购房比例降至历史最低的 21%。

存 0 块钱和存 1 万块钱毫无区别，因为都付不起首付。所以，去期权市场、预测市场和土狗盘里博一个 100 倍，成了年轻人在数学上唯一合理的突围方式。

数据显示，80% 冲向高风险资产的 Z 世代坦言，这么做是因为“感觉自己在财务上掉队了”；

过去一年，36% 的 30 岁以下美国年轻男性参与过体育博彩，35 岁以下投资者中有 43% 交易过期权。

2. AI 是生产力，更是最大的“逼赌机器”

这是全文最反直觉的视角。我们总以为 AI 是用来投资的，但报告指出，AI 正在全方位把普通人逼向赌桌。

一方面，微软、谷歌、亚马逊和 Meta 四大巨头 2026 年的资本支出预计高达 7000 +亿元（约占美国 GDP 的 2.3%，是当年电信泡沫顶峰的两倍多）；

另一方面，AI 正在消灭年轻人的上升阶梯。受 AI 冲击最严重的行业中，22-25 岁年轻人的就业率比正常水平低了 19%。

AI 一边在宏观上制造着百年一遇的财富神话，一边在微观上抽干年轻人的出路，直接给“彩票引擎”灌满了汽油。

3. 终极明示：抛弃筹码，去买赌场

既然投机是未来十年的绝对主题，散户的标的（今天炒 AI 算力、明天炒 Meme、后天赌球）会像走马灯一样轮动，绝大部分人最终都会归零。

数据大家也都知道，在 https://t.co/lh7cHMjjiD 发行的超 1900 万个代币中，只有 0.4% 的钱包实现了超 1 万美元的利润。

而“赌场们”正在吸金：

- 2026 年 Q2，Robinhood 光靠“事件合约（预测市场）”就赚了 1.56 亿美元，历史性地超越了它的股票业务和加密业务。

-Kalshi 和 Polymarket 的合并月交易量，从 2025 年中期的 20 亿美元，暴涨了 25 倍，在 2026 年 7 月达到惊人的 530 亿美元。

-Hyperliquid 在 2025 年处理了 3 万亿美元交易量，捕获了 9.72 亿美元的真实手续费，且几乎全部用来在二级市场回购 HYPE，如此财力其实也源自于链上的投资热情。

在文章最后，Delphi 实际上也给 Crypto 重新定了性：

别再纠结区块链到底有什么用，Crypto 最大的真实效用，就是为全球提供了一套零门槛、无休眠、成本低于 2 美元的终极投机基础设施。

叙事会死，代币会归零，但只要年轻人还需要一张改命的彩票，抽水的牌桌就永远印钞。

这就是未来十年最确定的 Alpha。

text:
Some people I've talked to wonder why Elizabeth Holmes wanted to be filmed in the days leading up to her incarceration. It's very clear to me what her goals were for the documentary: it's a calculated PR bet for Elizabeth to launder her reputation.

I understand why Nathan Fielder doesn't relitigate her case in the documentary. That story has been told. The case is literally closed. Elizabeth is serving jail time for defrauding investors. Her guilt is incontrovertible and not up for discussion.

However, the documentary introduces (and reintroduces) Elizabeth's story to audiences who are either unfamiliar with her lore or who don't have the details of the case top-of-mind.

Elizabeth knows that it's highly unlikely her conviction will be overturned. But she can change her perception in the court of public opinion. In the doc, Elizabeth achieves her goal of recasting her public image from the cold, calculating CEO to a tradwife-adjacent new mom who seems too socially unaware/oblivious/confused to have committed the crimes for which she is serving time. With her wide-eyed stare, rosy cheeks, and beatific smile, she even looks cherubic. AND she's running her old playbook of deploying her romantic partner in the role of unlikeable male enforcer (previously her ex-boyfriend/Theranos COO Sunny, now her husband Billy) as a reputational shield, garnering sympathy for herself. 

Because Elizabeth is difficult to read, she keeps her positioning options open. She could position herself as a poster-child for the new right's idea of womanhood: soft, feminine, devoted to her babies, and aligned with Trump, MAHA, and Charlie Kirk. Or she could fall back on her old 2010's-coded mission-driven girlboss CEO persona who just wants to save the world. Having Billy operate her Twitter account sets him up to be a potential fall guy and gives her plausible deniability about the views expressed online in her name.

Don't let her soft beige sweaters and feigned perpetual confusion fool you. Elizabeth has always been extremely strategic around her public image, and this documentary is no exception.

text:
imo this is the single most important line in the Wiz blog on the PHP hack -

"As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets."

code has always been slop-prone. but pre-ai, there were too many details to brute force and track. its crazy how much of the internet runs on "security through obscurity" (which is never real security)

but now the cost of brute-force attacks has gone to 0 thanks to ai, we're going through a phase where 20 years of cascading vulnerabilities can all explode to the surface that @fiveoutofnine describes.

purely fixing the bugs isn't a sustainable solution, as ai slop will likely introduce a variety of new ones. sustainable solutions need to be structural - i think we'll see much more formal verification + new languages that follow Rust/TypeScript's success in eradicating error categories from better code design from the get go.

Because GitLab also dropped a CVSS 10.0, which is the highest score they give out, for a bug that's been there since 2014, so that's every self-hosted GitLab for twelve years, and then LiteLLM 1.107.0 got hijacked and shipped a credential stealer and a remote access trojan in every single wheel and the Docker images, including latest, and you didn't even have to import it, just installing it was enough, and it's the second time this year, and then Railway paused every deployment on the entire platform because someone got into the environment variables, so now everyone has to rotate every secret they've ever stored there, and TiDB Cloud said someone was walking around inside with stolen credentials for basically a month and an extortion group says they took 10.6 terabytes, and Zeabur got breached for the second time in two months and is just shutting down, like the whole company, and Node.js patched remote code execution and a TLS bypass, and CISA says Plex is being actively exploited, and someone took over 300 Tor exit relays to steal SSH passwords, and SafePay ransomware has hit over 600 critical infrastructure orgs, and India's biggest bank filed a data loss incident, and Japan has been in an official state of emergency in cyberspace since October 9, which honestly explains the 5:55 AM post. Oh, and eMudhra, a certificate authority that's issued over 60 million certificates, whose entire job is proving websites are who they say they are, was supposed to be using private keys that are random numbers over a hundred digits long, and one of them was 4. AI-accelerated follow-on activity included reconnaissance, application credential changes, and attempts to modify privileges that could enable expanded or persistent access.

Read our blog for a detailed analysis and indicators of compromise (IOCs), along with Microsoft Defender detections, protection recommendations, and guidance on investigating service principal sign-ins and unexpected application credential or privilege changes.

22年中期选举之前，通胀爆表创四十年新高、美联储暴力加息、美股大盘暴跌30%多，美国国内对执政的拜登和民主党不满情绪非常高，“共和党红潮”席卷全美，当时中选前市场都认为共和党要横扫，但最后共和党只拿下众议院，执政党民主党不仅保住了参议院还增加了一个参议员名额扩大了的优势。

26年中期选举前，因为伊朗战争油价持续高位、通胀反弹，美国国内对川普的意见很大支持率新低，“民主党蓝潮”势头正盛，预测市场上都认为民主党要横扫拿下两院。

把今年中选前的势态与22件对照，是不是发现攻守易位。从22年“共和党红潮”到平局收场，给我们看待中期选举结果的启示是什么？

那就是全国性的声势浪潮，到了选举特别是中期选举就是一个州一个州的阵地战。而今年中选的关键是参议院的争夺，参议院的争夺也是在少数几个关键州的结果上。

26中期选举参议院合计改选席位：35个，其中共和党席位：22个，民主党席位：13个，独立议员：0个（目前2名独立议员均与民主党结盟，且不在本次改选范围内）

当前参议院整体格局约为共和党53席、民主党党团（含2名独立议员）47席。
因此今年年共和党需要防守更多席位，而民主党需要净增约4席才能夺回多数（如果民主党防守的一州失守、就需要净增更多一席）。

民主党能否守住密歇根，以及在北卡之外，能否把阿拉斯加、俄亥俄、德州、缅因等州的领先转化为足够的实际席位是这次民主党能否真的横扫的关键

整体看今年中选：
1）民主党拿下两院，仍是当前证据支持更强的单一情景，已经是当下预测市场和舆论中的大概率事件。

2）民主党拿下众院、共和党保住参院的分裂国会情景并不是没有可能，也值得重新放回框架来看，
这条路径主要依赖红州回归、个别共和党候选人跑赢全国环境，以及民主党在关键州的窄幅领先没有完全兑现？

quoted_text:
汽油价格与选票，此次中期选举民主党一定会横扫么？高盛这张图将民主党通用选票领先优势与美国平均零售汽油价格叠加对比：民主党的领先优势在伊朗战争爆发导致汽油价格飙升后逐步扩大，两组数据近期朝同一方向运动。而且油价还稍稍有点领先信号的意思。

现在预测市场关于中期选举民主党横扫的概率很大，已经成了当下是评估中期选举结构的基准情景了。不过高盛近期给了两个历史性警示还是值得看看的：
1）挑战党的横扫概率在历史上往往在选举日前收窄。高盛对2002、2006、2010、2018、2022年历次中期选举进行了回溯，发现“挑战党的横扫概率平均在选举日前下降约5个百分点”。以当前63%的民主党横扫概率为基准，历史规律暗示最终概率约为58%——仍是大概率，但舒适度大幅下降。

2）红州民调历史上系统性高估民主党表现。高盛绘制了历次参议院民调误差与各州党派倾向的关系图，发现“中期选举民调倾向于在民主党倾向州低估民主党，在共和党倾向州低估共和党”，与选民在选举周期末期“回归本党”的规律一致。这一模式在最近的数据中更为显著，而这一次参议院多数席位的争夺恰恰取决于那些红州。

还有一个点，共和党整个夏天在参议院竞选支出上均落后于民主党，直到前段时间才开始反超，并持续扩大差距。过去两周，共和党支出2.4亿美元，民主党支出1.3亿美元，共和党支出约为民主党的1.85倍。

如果油价和通胀对选情的影响如此之大，川普更需要的是一箱便宜的汽油。中选投票日之前压制油价成了重中之重

Claude Opus 5.5 is that damn good. It pulled 3,312 frames from one of my unreleased sites and wrote the 3D scene as code. Its first attempt was done in 2 hours and 20 minutes. I just wanted to see how it'd do with zero notes, sounds or music from me yet.

If you want to try the prompt on your own site or don't want to pay for After Effects, it's in the reply below.
author: kloss_xyz

text:
Note: Fill the brackets below, open Claude Code in an empty folder, and paste it.

P R O M P T :

Make an 8-bar 3D motion design film of my website: 1920x1080, 30 fps, Blender Cycles on GPU, headless, built entirely from code, in this folder.

INPUTS
SITE: [path to your site's repo, or its live URL]
HERO: [a .glb, 3 to 4 views of your character, or "the site's logo mark"]
AUDIO: [a WAV you own or licensed, with a clear drop, or "synth"]
LINE: [the one sentence the film proves]

STORY
Bar 1, hook: the site fills the frame, flat, and something alive inside it moves within 2 seconds. No title card.
Bar 2, premise: the hero breaks out of the page and the page splits into its sections as floating slabs.
Bar 3, drop: the first landing hits the music's drop.
Bars 3 to 5, proof: each landing switches one real section on. A landing that changes nothing gets cut.
Bar 6, breadth: every section lit in one frame.
Bar 7, thesis: the slabs fly back into one page.
Bar 8, close: a clean poster frame. Make the last frame match the first so it loops.

TRUTH
- Real pixels only. Capture each section of the running site with headless Chrome. Replace every clock the page uses (the performance timer, requestAnimationFrame, setTimeout and CSS animations) with a stepper so every frame is reproducible. Measure every target from the DOM.
- Never draw a screen, logo, number or claim that is not on the site. Cut empty sections.
- The look comes from the site: color, type, radius and easing tokens (from the code, or computed styles for a live URL), written into a style guide with the source of each. Anything not on the site is marked as a film choice.
- Banned: dark chrome, iridescent porcelain, a centered title over a gradient, fade-in on everything, particles that mean nothing.

TIMING
- One Python timeline file is the only clock: every event in beats at the track's tempo, with a check that fails on gaps. Capture, Blender and sound all read its JSON.
- Randomness only from one seed. Every frame renders correctly on its own.

MOTION
- Use the site's easing first. If it has none: enter and exit cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), moves on screen cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1).
- Buttons press in 100 to 160 ms and release without overshoot. Slabs settle once, no wobble. Text arrives fast and holds at least one beat. The hero squashes on landings and stretches in the air, and it is the only thing allowed to overshoot.
- Stagger 30 to 80 ms. Nothing scales up from zero; start at 95%.
- The hero never covers a word. Each section holds still, lit and readable before the next move. Start a switch-on a frame or two before contact so it reads on the landing.
- Rotations stay continuous (no flips between frames). No two surfaces ever share a plane.
- After every move: does the viewer know where to look next?

CAMERA
- Frontal on the flat page, then follow the action near hero height with shallow focus, then frontal again on the poster frame.
- Slow down whenever text is on screen: motion blur on a fast move doubles text. Focus distance follows the subject.
- Text and hero stay inside a 5% safe margin.

LOOK
- The set is the site's background color extended into an endless studio.
- Sections are emission. Render one, compare it to the capture, and keep the view transform with the lowest error and no clipped whites.
- Hero lights reach the hero only (light linking), so screens never reflect a light.
- Motion blur at 0.5 shutter. Measure the hero's colors against its source and fix exposure until they match.

SOUND
- Built from the same timeline, every cue on its exact second.
- With a track: use one window of it without re-timing; low-pass it until the drop, open it fully on the drop. With synth: pad and ticking hats before the drop, the full beat on it, a final chord that rings out.
- Foley synthesized in code, no samples, no words.
- -14 LUFS, true peak under -1 dB. The drop is the biggest step up in the film; never duck under it. No cue pokes more than 3 dB over the bed. End on a 0.5 s ring-out, never a hard cut.

REVIEW
- Before the full render: one still per beat at half resolution.
- Judge only rendered frames. Name the three worst defects, each with its frame, what proves it and a local fix. Re-render only the affected frames.
- Render in resumable chunks, then repeat the review on strips around the fastest moves. Log every round.

DELIVER
- An H.264 MP4 for X (BT.709 tagged), a ProRes 422 HQ master, a poster frame, one-sentence alt text, contact sheets and an asset list.
- Add a note on what still needs a human eye.
- Verify frame count, A/V sync (pad audio to whole frames) and loudness on the encoded file.
- 9:16 only if I ask, as its own composition, never a crop.

If HERO is only images, build one stylized model and show me a turnaround before animating. Ask only for what is missing; never use stand-ins. Decide everything else and log each decision with its reason.

Tools: Blender 5, Node with puppeteer, ffmpeg, Python 3 with numpy, scipy and pedalboard. Check them first and tell me what is missing.

text:
Just wrapped Money20/20. My biggest takeaway as a VC: the two forces reshaping fintech right now are AI agents and stablecoins. 
@SirDigitalDan from @CoinflowLabs and I dug into both in our fireside.

Some takeaways: 

* Where will value accrue? 

AI is collapsing the cost of cognition, and stablecoins the cost of settlement. This changes value accrual, when those inputs aren’t scarce. I’m expecting value to migrate to regulated trust, proprietary data, distribution, underlying physical assets, networks.

* What does stablecoins as programmable money unlock? 

Funds and spending rules can execute together, letting a product enforce agent budgets or trigger conditional payouts with less coordination across banks, processors and operational teams.

* Where is agent demand emerging? 

Dan pointed to compute, inference and data APIs, which agents need to complete tasks. I’m looking for infra on fraud, KYA, chargebacks, and merchant side ops to help proliferate agentic commerce usage. 

* Who carries agent liability? 

A purchase can comply with the spending rules and still be a mistake. Before delegating larger budgets, businesses will want audit trails, a way to dispute purchases and an agreement on who absorbs losses. 

* Where’s the distribution advantage? 

Local integrations and merchant relationships give providers access to existing payment volume. Stablecoins can improve settlement without changing how customers pay. (Coinflow connects cards, ACH and PIX this way.)

* How do existing PSPs participate? 

A provider can earn a processing fee when a developer funds an agent by card, even if subsequent payments settle in stablecoins. (Coinflow powers card funding for Tempo’s MPP Credits.)

Thanks for the week @money2020! Curious what others took away too!

text:
书接上回，接着聊昨晚聊的多端技术选型，今天我们来聊第二篇，说说我是怎么在 Mac 上来开发原生 Windows 软件的，以及我是如何搭建编译、测试环境的，还有最近一个月做 Mole Windows 版踩过的一些有意思的坑。

技术栈上，Mac 版本的 Mole 使用的也是原生的 Swift + SwiftUI，能够让我很好调用系统能力以及非常好的性能体验，想着不将就，所以在 Windows 上我也是想着直接用本身写 Windows 软件最直接的语言， C# 加 WinUI 3，跑在 .NET 10 上，过程虽然难搞，但是相比十年前我了解轮子哥谈的 Windows 开发要简单好理解一些了。

Windows 上的原生界面框架其实挺多的，包括很多年前了解过的 Win32、WinForms、WPF、UWP 这一波，WPF 是 2006 年出的，到现在还在维护，但控件和设计语言不是很好看，非常上一代的感觉，然后 UWP 又被沙盒和应用商店给绑定住，现在微软主推的是  Windows App SDK 里的 WinUI 3，界面框架从系统里面拆出来单独发版，这样就有一个好处，普通的 Win32 程序也能用，基础组件就是 Windows 11 自己的 Fluent 风格，我还挺喜欢，高分屏缩放和 ARM64 都是原生支持。

然后这里 .NET 10 是去年 11 月发的长期支持版本，打包时我把运行时一起打进去，用户不需要另外装 .NET，x64 和 ARM64 这里各出了一个原生安装包，骁龙的 Windows 笔记本就不要走转译了，相当于尽量让用户使用简单不折腾。这里安装和更新用的是开源的 Velopack 框架，可以很方便做增量更新，也很好用。

工程师开始写代码时候肯定会想到能复用尽量复用，所以我开始写的时候也非常想复用 Mac 的 Swift 代码，后面让 AI  分析了一下，十几万行代码 Swift 代码可以脱离  AppKit、SwiftUI 这些系统框架使用的20%都没有，处理的逻辑也是  ~/Library  这类 macOS自己的路径规则，基本用不上，所以  Windows 版几乎是从零开始写的。

两边的关系其实非常简单，外观和交互我尽量完全一致，尽可能让大家意识里面认为的 Windows 软件不那么精致美观的感觉在这里也保持我认为好的水平，然后底层代码各写各的，关于视觉的一致性还原有了AI以后很简单，我把原本的 Mac 版写在 Swift 里的颜色、字号、间距、圆角这些设计 token，直接写了一个脚本生成为 Windows 里面XAML 资源，文案也是从 Mac 的多语言文件转成 Windows 的格式，11 种语言一起转过来，甚至大家看到的菜单栏里面的那个runner动画也是用的同一个脚本同步来的。

虽说同步，可能大家会觉得很简单，其实这里需要花点精力防止 AI 直接给你跑偏了，每次同步其实我会记录对应的是Mac的哪一个提交，这样两边就不会走偏去，然后功能上会有一份 SYNC.md 当做对账表，Mac 每加一个功能、修一个安全问题，Windows 这边都会标清楚哪些是已经实现、哪些是刻意不同还是不适用，以及为什么这样判断。

通过这两个机制，我可以很好的让两边的底层完全各写各的，但是又能很好地保持功能对齐，完全不需要刻意去硬写一层兼容去磨平，反而会变复杂，这里能复用的反而是设计、文案以及踩坑后定下来的各种规则，反而这些是 AI 非常喜欢的“能力抽象层”，也就是说随着时代发展，慢慢所谓的代码抽象没有那么重要了，反而是规则抽象更重要。

另外 Windows 开发还有一块比 Mac 要麻烦不少，就是证书签名，没有签名的，一打开会出现「Windows已保护你的电脑」，甚至 Windows 11 的智能应用控制会直接不让运行，国内不少安全软件也会把没签名的程序当成可疑报毒，这和 Mac 上没签名、没公证的软件提示「已损坏」差不多，平时 Mac 上大家还可以跑一条命令解掉，Windows 上想正规分发，这一步没有啥好办法，就是需要。

调研下来微软的签名生态的确比苹果差太多了，微软有自己的 Azure Artifact Signing，一个月 9.99 美元最省事，居然个人只开放给美国和加拿大的开发者，没办法使用，很奇葩的规定，然后行业还规定从 2023 年起签名私钥必须放在硬件或者云端 HSM 里，不能再是电脑上的一个文件，今年起单张证书最长只能用 460 天，差不多一年多就得换一次证书

最后我买的是 Certum 的云端 OV 证书，3 年 3百多美元，签名时登录电脑上的 SimplySign，再用手机上的 App 给一个动态码，SmartScreen 的信誉也跟着证书上审核过的名字慢慢积累。刚开始一段时间的签名包在 ThinkPad 上也会一样被 SmartScreen 拦了下来，后来我每次发版都把安装包提交到微软的恶意软件分析门户，让信誉慢慢积累起来，而且 SimplySign 的登录会话闲置几个小时就会断开，需要再次输入动态码才能继续签名，所以这里其实很难做成云端自动打包。

证书搞定后，就是开发环境的事情了，我的研发要求是代码和 AI 的上下文必须全留在 Mac 上，Mac 用习惯了，真的很难使用 Windows 去研发，这里 Windows 只负责编译和验证效果和各种测试，所以我在 Mac 上装了 Parallels Desktop，大概 3 百多块一年，之前也挺不少小伙伴吐槽过这个软件，不过在我的 M5 Pro 上跑 Windows 11 还挺顺滑，让我感觉这个钱花得很值。

它最好用的一点是我的 Claude 能很顺手地操作它，仓库直接作为 Parallels 的共享文件夹挂进虚拟机，变成一个 X 盘，Mac 上改完代码，虚拟机里直接编译，不需要来回 Copy 文件，只是两边的编译产物要分到不同的目录，对于编译、启动、看日志的工作都被我写成了脚本，通过 Parallels 自带的 prlctl exec 直接在虚拟机里执行，程序启动就崩的时候 Windows 只给一个 0xc000027b，Mole 会把真正的异常写进日志，脚本跑完顺手打印出来，Claude 直接就能读到。相当于写代码还是在 Mac 上的 Claude Code 里，调试和运行都在虚拟机里，脚本不能解决的地方，直接用 Codex 的 computer use 去点，只有少部分那种系统确定弹框点不了，我在这里就是这个职责，点点系统弹框确定，哈哈。

说到这里，可以和大伙分享一下 Mole Windows的架构分层，一共四层，最底下的 Core 只依赖 .NET，不碰任何 Windows 接口，清理规则、路径安全检查、卸载残留的判断都放到这里，测试用的是一个按 Windows 路径规则模拟出来的内存文件系统，这样在 Mac 上也可以很好的跑；往上是 Platform 层，注册表、文件系统、Win32 调用这些真正的系统接口都放在这一层，打开 EnableWindowsTargeting 以后，Mac 上也能编译通过；再往上就是写过应用同学非常熟悉的界面状态的 ViewModel 层，这里和 Mac 版本会一一对应，这样也能够在 Mac 上测，只有最上面这一层的 WinUI 界面必须去 Windows 里编译。

这也是让我一个月时间可以写8 万多行 Windows 代码、4000 多个测试，但是几乎大部分可以在 Mac 上完成的一个很方便的地方，也是架构设计的巧妙处，当然这里我只提供之前做架构时候的想法建议，大部分是 Opus 5.5 去帮我整的，很牛逼。

接着可以聊测试了，我反而认为 在 AI 时代，工程师最大的价值，除了架构设计外就是这个测试验证了，所以为了保证产品是可以售卖的，肯定需要在真实环境测试验证，反复找体验问题去修复的，所以我整了一台 ThinkPad X1 Carbon，这个机器质感还不错的，我把它当成真机环境，设置永不休眠，可以让我和我的Agent 24 小时去验证测试回归，包括获取各种真实系统环境的参数验证，400 多款 Windows 软件的卸载、残留清理、注册表、启动项测试，大部分在虚拟机里跑，x64 安装包、真实的高分屏、电池、SmartScreen 这些虚拟机看得不准确的，就直接放到这台机器上验，所以这台机器让我感觉也非常值。

然后为了不想在两台机器拷来拷去，最后还是用了 UU 远程，直接在 ThinkPad 那边开一个远程终端，我这边在 Mac 上直接操作，然后还把 ssh 连接当做备用，大部分软件的安装、卸载和调试，都是通过命令行脚本去完成的，剩下需要看界面的，直接通过远程桌面让 computer use 去操作，非常方便，最终相当于我还是在 Mac 上做的所有的事情。

差不多就是这些啦，这个过程下来，到最后成品让几个 Mole 天使用户去试用，大伙用着很爽，感觉这个过程的开发非常值，很有意思，而且可以帮助大家解决不少痛点，加上 Windows 上小白用户应该比 Mac 要多不少，让他们也享受到好软件的体验其实很值得开心。

差不多这两天这两篇文章算是把我这一个月的思考和想法聊完了，欢迎交流，有在做 Windows 开发的小伙伴也可以一起聊聊你们的最佳实践，假如还有空，下一篇我想着给大伙聊聊怎么在研发过程中借其他程序语言的生态来补桌面端的短板，这里也非常有意思。

text:
What's happening in cybersecurity is a COVID-like wave ripping through the Internet. Honestly surprised it took this long, but seems like it's here now.

Crypto already saw this.

Onchain hacks are a canary for what will happen in the rest of web security, because onchain is the first and easiest place to monetize cyberattacks. Crypto protocols have already hardened themselves against this (small protocols are mostly getting popped; large protocols are using AI tools to protect themselves). This means that while the NUMBER of hacks has gone vertical, the run rate of $$s hacked is actually roughly equal to 2025. Meaning the dollar value of hacks has gone down, while the number has gone up—a mass looting of small, poorly maintained protocols.

I expect the same thing to be happening in the general web.

text:
Meta 营收暴涨 26%，扎克伯格却在为资本运作铺路？

Meta Q3 营收达到 646 亿美元，同比增长 26%，财报后股价盘后上涨约 3%–4%。但强劲增长背后，AI 投资正在给现金流带来压力。

几个关键数字值得关注：

• 利润承压：计入约 98.9 亿美元青少年心理健康诉讼费用后，GAAP EPS 降至 3.83 美元；剔除后约为 7.40 美元。

• 资本开支凶猛：经营现金流约 328 亿美元，而设备购置及融资租赁本金支出合计约 349 亿美元。全年资本开支指引高达 1,350 亿至 1,450 亿美元。

• C 类股票安排：Meta 计划向现有股东派发无投票权的 C 类股票，为未来融资、并购和员工激励增加工具，也为扎克伯格提供了在保留控制权的同时增加个人资产流动性的空间。

但要注意：派发股票本身不会给 Meta 带来现金，扎克伯格出售个人股票所得也不属于公司收入。真正能为 AI 投资输血的，是公司未来可能进行的融资。

广告业务负责赚钱，AI 基础设施负责烧钱，C 类股票则为未来资本运作预留空间。

Meta 真正要解决的，是如何在继续重金押注 AI 的同时，维持创始人的控制权。

We formally announced Mirendil less than 4 months ago. Today, I'm excited to share an important milestone for:

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.

Mirendil's mission is to solve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) and use it to democratize frontier AI development, ultimately accelerating science and technology. At Mirendil, when we think about RSI, we think holistically about the company as an intelligent entity that self-improves toward its goal. From that perspective, the most powerful notion of acceleration is reducing the time and resources (number of human experts, compute, and other costs) needed to achieve ambitious goals.

Given that pretraining is perhaps the most important yet most challenging part of frontier AI development, we decided to run an ambitious controlled experiment: Starting fully from scratch, can we significantly reduce the time, number of human experts, and compute resources needed to go all the way to successfully pretraining a strong coding model at scale?

Mirendil-Base is the result of this experiment. Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute. This includes all the research and small-scale experiments it took to get there, as well as the final training run.

The recipe holds up as the models get bigger. For reference, Mirendil-Base is in the 100B-500B parameter range, Mirendil-Base-Large in the 500B-2T range, and Mirendil-Base-XL in the 2T-10T range.

We're beginning to see a world where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can take on work that once required an entire research organization. As these systems improve, the bottleneck shifts from the size of a team to the ambition and judgment of the people directing them. This has profound implications for who gets to build AI and, ultimately, who gets to push the frontiers of science and technology forward.

We’ll share independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks and API-access sooner than you think so stay tuned!

OKX Shield is more than a protection program. It’s designed to encourage users to adopt stronger account security through technologies such as passkeys, secure enclaves, and anti-deepfake protection.

We backtested these security measures against five years of historical account takeover cases. The results were encouraging: very few of those cases would have succeeded if users had enabled these protections.

Our goal is to prevent account takeovers before they happen—not just compensate users afterward.

OKX Shield covers eligible account takeover incidents, but not scams involving transactions authorized by users.

Better security. Stronger prevention. Real protection.

That’s how we build trust through technology. 🛡️

People generally understand that tokenization will create an explosion in the amount of assets to trade.

They're only beginning to be understood the boom that this will create in trading venues and front ends.

My early impression is that the combo of fintech + crypto will be more disruptive to trad brokerage and exchanges than people think.

The brokerages expecially have benefitted from operating in a highly regulated industry for a long time, and therefore have pretty universally poor UX.

I think once tech companies move payments and treasury mgmt onchain (already happening), it will open their eyes to opportunities in finance they never previously would have considered.

SpaceX / xAI / Elon will make a HUGE splash in this next year and put the fear of god in finance generally.

But the larger trend is an explosion in the number of trading venues and a sea change in the composition.

They will be faster, more innovative, and lean into AI first versions of supporting trading and investing.

The roles of a financial advisor and trader will be condensed into an agent that every retail trader in America will have access to.

If you aren't excited about this future, I don't know what to tell you.

It's bright, and it's for the taking.

text:
时间在策略里不算一个独立的模块，但它通常以几种身份出现。

1. 状态划分（regime） 最常见的用法。把一天切成几个不同的"市场状态"，比如盘前、盘中、盘后、夜盘、休市，每个状态下流动性和波动都不一样。策略先判断"现在处于哪个状态"，再决定怎么做。这在研究里叫按时段做条件化（session conditioning）。

2. 风控和执行的开关（gating） 比如重大数据公布前缩量。这类用法不预测方向，只决定"现在能不能交易、该用多大仓位"，属于风控层或执行层。给每个时刻打一个时段标签，策略根据标签决定照常报价、停报价，还是平仓。

3. 参数调整 同一个策略，不同时段用不同参数，比如流动性低的时段把价差拉宽、下单量减小。这属于参数随状态变化。

4. 信号本身 时间也可以直接当因子，叫日内季节性（intraday seasonality）或日历效应，比如某些时段波动或方向有规律、月末效应、周一效应。这时它属于alpha 层。

5. 数据和基础设施 交易日历、假日表、夏令时换算、不同市场的时区，属于数据层。这一块不起眼，但错了上面全错。

> LiteLLM (again!): Backdoored release stealing API keys, credentials & secrets → rebuild affected systems, rotate keys
> GitLab: CVSS 10.0 flaw could allow unauthenticated server takeover → patch self-hosted instances
> Railway: Customer environment secrets potentially exposed, including API keys & database credentials → rotate all secrets, check logs
> Node.js: High-severity flaws including potential RCE → update Node.js
> ConnectWise: 300+ successful suspicious Microsoft 365 sign-ins → audit app access
> OVHcloud: Official CLI downloads replaced with malware, ~250 downloads during exposure → reinstall & rotate credentials
> OpenCode: API keys potentially exposed for 1.4% of Console users → revoke keys, check your billing

Infra is becoming the attack surface.
What else am i missing?

🚨赵长鹏：建议未来数日谨慎访问任何网站，警惕潜在漏洞

赵长鹏 @cz_binance  发推表示，建议未来数日谨慎访问任何网站，因部分网站管理员未必及时更新安全补丁。

PHP 被披露存在两项漏洞（CVE-2026-109618 与 CVE-2026-109619）后，影响运行 WordPress 及 Magento 等热门应用的服务器。

由于漏洞细节提前泄露，补丁已于 10 月 21 日发布，目前已确认出现利用行为。未认证攻击可将被访问网站转化为凭证窃取或设备利用的载体。

此前，慢雾 @SlowMist_Team  曾发布安全预警称，上述两项漏洞的 CVSS v4.0 评分均为 9.2，可导致远程代码执行；PHP 官方计划于北京时间 10 月 21 日 22:00 发布安全更新并公布受影响与修复版本。

慢雾建议相关团队排查使用 PHP 的服务器及业务系统，并在修复版本发布后及时升级。
